docs.title: Epistemic Anchoring in Stochastic Large Language Models: A Neurosymbolic Architecture for Verifiable Argumentation and Reproducible Evaluation
docs.text:
Quorum Research Collective

arXiv preprint: cs.AI / cs.CL / cs.DS

docs.title: Abstract
docs.text:
Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) operate as stochastic token probability generators whose unconstrained inference paths are fundamentally susceptible to hallucinations, semantic drift, error compounding, and epistemic instability. This paper presents the Quorum architecture: a formal neurosymbolic computational framework that transforms unconstrained stochastic generative processes into a deterministically supervised, epistemically anchored state machine. The theoretical foundation comprises:

  1. Propositional epistemic atomization via the six-tuple Linked Atom Graph (LAG) propositional frame,
  2. Wave-based topological execution over a Cognitive Directed Acyclic Graph (Cognitive DAG),
  3. Topological Directed Atom (TDA) poset wave scheduling governed by an orthogonal two-tier epistemic firewall (deterministic physical citation provenance and role-asymmetric Popperian falsification),
  4. Interactive diagnostic argument surgery, Assumption-Based Truth Maintenance Systems (ATMS), and Toulmin warrant reachability under counterfactual premise retractions,
  5. Pure stateless baseline argument causal cohesion evaluation via the 0-token Cumulative Guttman Invariant (Guttman, 1944) over unperturbed graph topologies, and
  6. An orthogonal multi-factor BARS evaluation matrix combining asymmetric Popperian falsification, event-sourced state projection, and continuous piecewise power-curve damping.

We formalize this framework through two core architectural principles (confluent wave scheduling under Kahn partial ordering and epistemic warrant reachability under discrete ATMS graph surgery) and two mathematically verified system properties (decoupled epistemic error suppression separating physical citation provenance from semantic entailment, and monotonic Lipschitz score stability). The framework is empirically validated through two controlled pairwise audit trials across organizational policy and strategic foresight domains ($T = 2$ paired trials, 4 full workflow executions, $N = 110$ common proposition atoms per trial), demonstrating high inter-run stability (observed raw agreement $95.45\%$ and $98.18\%$; Cohen's $\kappa = 0.9064$ and $\kappa = 0.9633$; pooled mean $\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$; mean Shannon entropy $\bar{H} \le 0.0455$) under unconstrained native stochastic frontier sampling (provider default entropy without greedy clamping), with zero system crashes or Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) drops. Furthermore, across a controlled 5-configuration component ablation benchmark ($N = 220$ proposition atom frames), Quorum elevates evaluative test–retest reliability from $\kappa = 0.2146$ (unconstrained prompt-based LLM judge) to $\kappa = 0.9453$ ($P_o = 97.27\%$ in the ablation benchmark harness; and $\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$, $P_o = 96.82\%$ in physical production trials), eliminates unanchored chimera citations from $20.7\%$ to $0.0\%$ under an offline benchmark stress test with 19.7% candidate attack pressure ($\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$), and eradicates the $8.6\%$ criterion omission rate observed in monolithic step evaluation. Across a 70-proposition human-calibrated sample, the lexical firewall achieves a physical citation specificity of $\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$ ($95\%$ CI: $[0.890, 1.000]$) and an empirical Positive Predictive Value of $\widehat{\text{PPV}} = 1.000$ ($95\%$ CI: $[0.912, 1.000]$), successfully rejecting $100\%$ of chimeric and fabricated citations. While naive single-segment extraction exhibits a baseline False Omission Rate of $\widehat{\text{FOR}} = 13.33\%$ and inter-run retrieval variance ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$), extending the firewall with ordered multi-segment bounding span vectors ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}i, 1 \le m \le 3$), decoupled Gate 5 morphological stemming ($\zeta{\text{lex}}$ vs. $\zeta_{\text{score}}$), and bounded root axiom anchoring ($K_{\text{axiom}}^{\max} = 8$) reduces the False Omission Rate to $\widehat{\text{FOR}} \le 2.00\%$, elevates offline ablation recovery from $52.7\%$ ($116/220$) to $58.2\%$ ($128/220$), bounds extended-corpus deliverable isolation to $r_{\text{iso}}^{\text{deliv}} \le 0.200$, and elevates inter-run agreement to $\bar{\kappa} \ge 0.9800$ while strictly preserving $\text{Specificity}_{\text{lex}} = 1.000$ ($0/21$ chimera leaks). Across two independent production evaluation pairs ($2 \times 110$ criteria; $141$ to $252$ extracted claims per run), the deterministic topological engine executes full ATMS cascade propagation and root-cause isolation in $< 1.0\text{ ms}$ with zero additional LLM token overhead. We report these initial findings transparently from two paired experimental runs, noting that broader multi-corpus evaluations are required for population-level statistical generalization. Finally, we synthesize Quorum's positioning across the landscape of reasoning architectures, retrieval frameworks, and cognitive governance paradigms.

docs.title: 1. Introduction and Problem Formulation
docs.text:
An autoregressive language model is formally defined as a conditional probability distribution over a discrete vocabulary $\mathcal{V}$:

$$P(Y \mid X; \theta) = \prod_{t=1}^{T} P(y_t \mid y_{<t}, X; \theta), \quad y_t \in \mathcal{V} \tag{1}$$

where $X = (x_1, \dots, x_N)$ is an input prompt sequence and $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^D$ represents the static model weights. Although modern frontier models produce syntactically fluent discourse, their epistemic utility in high-stakes reasoning is bounded by three structural failures:

  1. Aleatoric Uncertainty and Calibration Divergence: The distribution $P(Y \mid X; \theta)$ models statistical token co-occurrence frequencies across training corpora rather than objective truth values ($\mathcal{T} \neq \mathcal{P}$). The model generates statistically plausible assertions that lack empirical backing.
  2. Conflation of Association with Causation: Autoregressive attention captures symmetric correlation $P(A \mid B)$ but cannot distinguish a genuine causal mechanism $B \to A$ from confounding background factors ($C \to A \land C \to B$) or reverse causation ($A \to B$).
  3. Superlinear Error Cascade: In unconstrained multi-step inference, a minute semantic drift at step $t$ conditions the distribution at step $t+1$, causing errors to compound exponentially across generative trajectories—formalizing exposure bias and compositional error cascades in autoregressive models (Ross & Bagnell, 2010; Dziri et al., 2023):

$$\mathbb{E}\left[|\hat{y}{t+k} - y^*{t+k}|\right] \sim \mathcal{O}\left(e^{\lambda_{\text{casc}} k}\right), \quad \lambda_{\text{casc}} > 0 \tag{2}$$

The Quorum architecture addresses these vulnerabilities by stripping the LLM of autonomous state transitions. The generative model is restricted to a stateless, constrained propositional sensor, while the control logic, state progression, and evidentiary evaluation are enforced by an external, mathematically validated neurosymbolic engine.

docs.title: Research Questions and Empirical Scope
docs.text:
To systematically investigate the operational efficacy and architectural contributions of this neurosymbolic design, this paper addresses three fundamental research questions:

  • RQ1 (Evidentiary Anchoring & Replication Reliability): To what extent does an orthogonal multi-gate lexical firewall combined with parallel Best-of-3 ensembling suppress chimera citations and improve test–retest reproducibility ($\kappa$) relative to unconstrained LLM-as-a-judge baselines? (Evaluated in Sections 4.1, 6, 8.2, 8.4, and 8.5; Tables 2, 6, and 7)
  • RQ2 (Decomposition & Attention Integrity): How does propositional atomization (Linked Atom Graph 6-tuple) and deterministic single-token UUID aliasing mitigate attention degradation (lost-in-the-middle criterion drops) and Byte-Pair Encoding tokenization boundary perturbations across extended context windows? (Evaluated in Sections 2.1, 3.1, 8.1, and 8.5; Tables 3 and 7)
  • RQ3 (Structural Causality & Human Agency Discrimination): Can a 0-token Cumulative Guttman Invariant on mined argument graphs combined with an orthogonal Human Agency & Collaboration Matrix ($\mathcal{M}_{\text{HACM}}$) reliably differentiate substantive reasoning from passive human delegation and surface rhetorical fluency? (Evaluated in Sections 4.2, 5.4, 8.3, and 8.4; Tables 1, 3, 4, and 6)

docs.title: 2. Epistemic Atomization and the Linked Atom Graph (LAG)
2.1. Ontological Disambiguation and the Atomization Morphism
docs.text:
Ontological Partition (Discourse Claims vs. Rubric Criteria): To establish formal mathematical precision, Quorum explicitly distinguishes between two structurally distinct propositional collections that operate across different pipeline phases:

  1. Dynamic Discourse Graph Claims ($\mathcal{V}_{ ext{claim}}$): In Phase 1 Cognitive DAG execution, an unstructured natural language input or discourse history $\mathcal{D} \in \Sigma^$ is dynamically decomposed via the mining morphism $\alpha_{ ext{mine}}: \Sigma^ o \mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}$ into a variable set of minimal, mutually independent empirical assertions: $$\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}} = { v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n } ag{3}$$ These mined assertions form the node set of the directed proposition graph $\mathcal{G}{ ext{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{ ext{deps}})$, exhibiting discourse-dependent graph cardinality across runs ($|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \in [141, 252]$ across the three-document trial payload, well within the combined ceiling $N_{\max}^{ ext{payload}} = 300$; Section 8.1, Section 8.3).
  2. Fixed Evaluative Rubric Criteria ($\mathcal{A}_{ ext{rubric}}$): In Phase 1 matrix evaluation, the discourse is evaluated against a pre-compiled, design-time curated benchmark schema consisting of fixed Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) criteria: $$\mathcal{A}{ ext{rubric}} = igcup{m=1}^D \mathcal{A}m, \quad |\mathcal{A}{ ext{rubric}}| = N = 110 ag{4}$$ totaling exactly $N = 110$ immutable criteria across the five evaluated matrices ($25 + 5 + 25 + 25 + 30 = 110$; Table 3).

Definition 1A (Evaluated Rubric Proposition Frame). Every evaluated rubric proposition $a_i \in \mathcal{A}_{ ext{rubric}}$ is formally tested against discourse $\mathcal{D}$ as an immutable six-tuple:

$$a_i = \langle au_i, \vec{\mathcal{C}}i, \sigma_i, \pi_i, \lambda_i, au{ ext{val}, i} angle ag{5}$$

  • $ au_i \in \mathcal{L}_{ ext{prop}}$ is the declarative target hypothesis formulated in formal logic with unambiguous truth-evaluable acceptance criteria.
  • $\vec{\mathcal{C}}i = (\mathcal{C}{i,1}, \dots, \mathcal{C}{i,m})$ is the ordered bounding span vector where $1 \le m \le 3$, isolating up to 3 non-contiguous verbatim text spans in source document $\mathcal{D}_k \in \mathcal{D}$ extracted to substantiate $ au_i$. Each constituent segment $\mathcal{C}{i,j} \subset \Sigma^*$ is an unbroken character substring satisfying monotonic spatial ordering: $$s_1 < e_1 < s_2 < e_2 < \dots < s_m < e_m \le s_1 + 1\,000 ag{5b}$$ enforcing a maximum bounding distance $(e_m - s_1) \le 1\,000$ characters and strict single-document buffer boundary isolation ($ orall j \in {1, \dots, m}: \mathcal{C}_{i,j} \subset \mathcal{D}_k$), mathematically banning cross-document quote stitching and unbounded multi-segment expansion ($m > 3$). For single-segment citations ($m=1$), the floor is $\ge 10$ characters; for multi-segment citations ($m > 1$), each segment enforces an individual floor of $\ge 30$ characters.
  • $\sigma_i \in { ext{USER}, ext{ASSISTANT}}$ is the speaker attribution index, separating human supervisory intent from model-generated synthetic drafts.
  • $\pi_i \in {+1, -1}$ is the evidentiary polarity index: $\pi_i = +1$ denotes a positive capability claim (demonstrating analytical competence), whereas $\pi_i = -1$ designates an asymmetric anti-pattern detector (identifying cognitive failure modes, fallacies, or uncritical adoption).
  • $\lambda_i \in {0, 1}$ is the physical citation and speaker provenance index, governed by an uncompromising null hypothesis parameterized by decoupled lexical strictness $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \in [0, 100]$:

$$\lambda_i = egin{cases} 1, & ext{Lex}(\vec{\mathcal{C}}i, \mathcal{D}; \zeta{ ext{lex}}) \;\land\; ext{Prov}(\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i, \sigma_i) \ 0, & ext{otherwise} \end{cases} ag{6}$$

  • $ au_{ ext{val}, i} \in {0, 1}$ is the discrete semantic rubric validation decision emitted by the model's structured reasoning trace $\mathcal{T}_i$ and confirmed via parallel Best-of-3 ensemble consensus:

$$ au_{ ext{val}, i} = egin{cases} 1, & ext{Decision}(\mathcal{T}_i) = ext{PASS} \;\land\; ext{Triangulate}(\mathcal{T}_i, \vec{\mathcal{C}}_i) \ 0, & ext{otherwise} \end{cases} ag{6b}$$

where $\mathcal{D}d \in \mathfrak{D}$ is an individual source document buffer indexed by identifier $d \in \mathfrak{D}$, preventing cross-document chimeric stitching across distinct provenance streams. When the initial segment $q_1$ occurs at multiple candidate positions ${s_1^{(1)}, s_1^{(2)}, \dots, s_1^{(R)}}$ within the normalized coordinate space of $\mathcal{D}_d$ (via bidirectional index mapping $\mathcal{M}{ ext{idx}}$), the anchor validator evaluates candidate anchors sequentially until it identifies an occurrence $s_1^{(r)}$ from which monotonic forward-scan resolution ($s_k = \min{s > e_{k-1} \mid \mathcal{D}_d[s:e] \cong q_k}$ for $k \in {2, \dots, m}$) satisfies Equations (5b)–(6b). Under the asymmetric proof burden of anti-pattern criteria ($\pi_i = -1$), clean performance requires the absence of grounded violation citations ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i = \emptyset \implies \lambda_i = 0$), whereas penalizing an observed anti-pattern ($\omega(a_i) = ext{FAILED}$) requires extracting a verified physical violation span ($1 \le m \le 3 \implies \lambda_i = 1$). Conversely, positive capability claims ($\pi_i = +1$) strictly require verified empirical citations ($1 \le m \le 3 \land \lambda_i = 1$) to pass.

Definition 1B (Mined Discourse Claim Node). Every empirical assertion $v_j \in \mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}$ mined dynamically from unstructured discourse $\mathcal{D}$ is represented as an attributed node in $\mathcal{G}{ ext{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{ ext{deps}})$ via the sovereign six-tuple:

$$v_j = \langle au_j, \vec{\mathcal{C}}j, ext{src}_j, s_j, \lambda{ ext{claim}, j}, \gamma_j angle ag{6c}$$

  • $ au_j \in \mathcal{L}_{ ext{prop}}$ is the minimal, mutually independent propositional assertion extracted from the source discourse.
  • $\vec{\mathcal{C}}j = (\mathcal{C}{j,1}, \dots, \mathcal{C}_{j,m})$ is the verbatim bounding span vector ($1 \le m \le 3$) locating the assertion in discourse buffer $\mathcal{D}_d \in \mathfrak{D}$.
  • $ ext{src}_j \in { ext{DOCUMENT}, ext{DIALOGUE}, ext{SYNTHETIC}}$ is the provenance stream origin, strictly segregating candidate-authored deliverables from supervisory conversational dialogues and auxiliary instructions.
  • $s_j \in {0.0, 0.5, 1.0, ext{N/A}}$ is the discrete epistemic fulfillment state assigned to the proposition (where $ ext{N/A}$ indicates topological short-circuiting under precondition or warrant failures; Section 4.2, Section 6).
  • $\lambda_{ ext{claim}, j} \in {0, 1}$ is the deterministic anchor validity returned by the five-gate lexical firewall (Section 4.1.1), certifying that all segments in $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_j$ exist within a single physical document buffer $\mathcal{D}_d$ and satisfy monotonic spatial ordering.
  • $\gamma_j \in { ext{EMPIRICAL}, ext{DEDUCTION}, ext{UNANCHORED}}$ is the epistemic grounding type, classifying whether the assertion is directly anchored in physical text ($\lambda_{ ext{claim}, j} = 1$), derived via a formal logical warrant ($ au_{ ext{ded}} = ext{True}$), or flagged as an unsubstantiated orphan claim ($\lambda_{ ext{claim}, j} = 0 \land eg au_{ ext{ded}}$).

Theorem 1 (Lexical Specificity Invariant under Multi-Segment Bounding). Let $\Phi_{ ext{lex}}: (\vec{\mathcal{C}}i, \mathfrak{D}) o {0, 1}$ denote the deterministic multi-segment lexical firewall enforcing single-document buffer isolation ($\mathcal{C}{i,k} \subseteq \mathcal{D}d \; orall k \in {1, \dots, m}$), monotonic forward-scan ordering ($s_1^{(r)} < e_1^{(r)} < s_2 < \dots < e_m$), minimum segment length floors ($e_k - s_k \ge 30$ for $m > 1$), and maximum span bounding ($e_m - s_1^{(r)} \le 1\,000$). For any adversarial or hallucinated citation tuple $\vec{\mathcal{C}}{ ext{adv}}$ containing at least one fabricated substring ($\exists k: \mathcal{C}{ ext{adv}, k} subseteq \mathcal{D}_d$), cross-document chimeric splice ($\mathcal{C}{ ext{adv}, 1} \subseteq \mathcal{D}a \land \mathcal{C}{ ext{adv}, 2} \subseteq \mathcal{D}b$ with $a eq b$), inverted rhetorical stitching ($s{k+1} < e_k$), or long-range context jumping ($e_m - s_1^{(r)} > 1\,000$), $\Phi_{ ext{lex}}(\vec{\mathcal{C}}_{ ext{adv}}, \mathfrak{D}) = 0$, preserving exact physical citation specificity:

$$ ext{Specificity}{ ext{lex}} = rac{ ext{TN}}{ ext{TN} + ext{FP}} = 1.000 \quad (\alpha{ ext{chimera}} = 0) ag{6d}$$

bounding the empirical chimera quote leakage rate to the physical string collision floor $\epsilon_{ ext{lexical}} o 0$.

Proof. Let $\mathcal{H}0$ denote the null hypothesis that candidate vector $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i$ contains synthetic hallucination, cross-document splicing, or out-of-order clauses. In Gate 1, each constituent segment $\mathcal{C}{i,j}$ undergoes normalized forward scanning in $\mathcal{D}k$ with monotonic cursor advancement $s{j+1} > e_j$. If any segment $\mathcal{C}{i,j} ot\subset \mathcal{D}_k$, or if $e_m - s_1 > 1\,000$, or if segments cross document buffer boundaries, the forward scan deterministically fails, forcing $\lambda_i = 0$. In Gate 5, for $\zeta{ ext{lex}} < 100$, approximate matching requires contiguous morphological stem-sequence alignment or $\ge 70\%$ unbroken longest-common-substring coverage. Because synthetic hallucinations assert non-existent terms whose stems are absent from $\mathcal{D}k$, stem alignment fails, yielding $FP{ ext{chimera}} = 0$. Empirical evaluation across $N = 220$ benchmark atoms under 19.7% candidate attack pressure verified $0 / 21$ leaked fabrications ($FP = 0$, $TN = 21$), yielding $ ext{Specificity}_{ ext{lex}} = 21 / (21 + 0) = 1.000$. Physical containment is thus formally decoupled from semantic entailment ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i \models au_i$), guaranteeing zero synthetic fabrication leakage into downstream A-SCM graph synthesis. $ lacksquare$

The Syntactic Provenance vs. Semantic Entailment Boundary: An exact substring match $ ext{find}(\mathcal{C}{i,j}, \mathcal{D}) eq -1$ provides physical provenance—irrefutable proof that citation vector $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i$ physically exists within document $\mathcal{D}$ and was neither fabricated nor spliced across disparate paragraphs. However, deterministic string matching is semantically blind: it verifies the syntactic existence of character sequences, not that proposition $ au_i$ semantically follows from $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i$ ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i \models au_i$). Because natural language discourse is inherently open-ended and pragmatic, universal automated verification of semantic entailment over unrestricted natural language exhibits an intrinsic semantic entailment gap (formally bounded by Rice's theorem on the undecidability of non-trivial semantic properties in computational systems; Rice, 1953; Turing, 1936). Pre-compiling propositions $ au_i$ as typed Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) rubrics within a centralized declarative schema defines the target hypotheses rigorously, but does not eliminate the semantic gap between a real quotation and its purported interpretation. Consequently, Quorum structures epistemic defense across two orthogonal layers: 1. Deterministic Physical Grounding (Type I Defense): Eliminates fabricated and chimera citations with mathematical certainty ($\lambda_i = 0$ if $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i ot\subset \mathcal{D}$), bounding citation fabrication error to the physical substring collision floor $\epsilon{ ext{lexical}} o 0$. 2. Adversarial Neurosymbolic Entailment (Type II Defense): Constrains semantic misattribution ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i \subset \mathcal{D}$ but $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i ot\models au_i$) through role-asymmetric Popperian falsification ($\pi_i = -1$), syntactic anchor triangulation, and downstream Argumentative SCM (A-SCM) reachability pruning, ensuring that residual semantic drift is bounded by parallel Best-of-3 ensemble consensus rather than conflated with lexical string matching.

Symbolic Interface Grounding and Subword Entropy Suppression: In physical persistence, propositions $a_i \in \mathcal{A}{ ext{rubric}}$ and discourse nodes $v_j \in \mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}$ are addressed via high-entropy 128-bit identifiers ($\mathcal{I}_{ ext{UUID}}$, specifically RFC 9562 UUIDv7 prefixed hexadecimal identifiers). Directly exposing multi-token hexadecimal strings to autoregressive prompt contexts induces subword tokenization fragmentation (5–10 Byte-Pair Encoding subwords per identifier), triggering attention diffusion, positional degradation over extended contexts, and character transposition hallucinations during decoding. To isolate the generative sensor from persistent storage mechanics, the neurosymbolic boundary executes an ephemeral bijective alias morphism:

$$\mu: \mathcal{I}{ ext{UUID}} \longleftrightarrow \mathcal{V}{ ext{alias}}, \quad \mathcal{V}{ ext{alias}} = {a_0, a_1, \dots, a{n-1}}$$

This morphism compresses each propositional target into an atomic single-token Attention Anchor ($a_k$). Concurrently, the generation grammar enforces constrained decoding via dynamic finite categorical vocabularies, restricting output logits strictly to the closed support $\mathcal{V}_{ ext{alias}}$. Upon receipt, the runtime executes deterministic $\mathcal{O}(1)$ reverse hydration $\mu^{-1}(a_k)$, triggering an immediate validation failure if an unmapped alias is generated. This preserves single-token attention fidelity while guaranteeing mathematical referential integrity across the proposition graph.

docs.title: 2.2. Linked Atom Graph Structure and Root Node Typology
docs.text:
The mined discourse claims $\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}$ are structured into a directed, attributed multi-graph $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{dep}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{temp}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{causal}})$, where edge sets define logical dependency, temporal order, and inferred causal transmission.

To avoid misclassifying legitimate foundational axioms, $\mathcal{G}_{\text{LAG}}$ partitions root nodes ($\text{InDegree}(v) = 0$) and isolated claims into distinct epistemic categories:

  1. Active Exogenous Boundary Axioms ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{axiom}}$): Primitive operational constraints or historical baseline premises ($U_i$) that require no internal textual ancestors ($\text{InDegree}(v) = 0$), but serve as active antecedents for downstream inferences ($v \to u$), satisfying $\text{OutDegree}(v) \ge 1$. Consequently, its total graph degree is $\text{deg}(v) = \text{InDegree}(v) + \text{OutDegree}(v) \ge 1$, which naturally excludes it from the isolated concept ratio $r_{\text{iso}}$ without requiring heuristic whitelisting. To prevent horizon truncation of foundational premises across extended documents ($|\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}| > 140$) without incurring $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ full-graph attention overhead, each window $w > 0$ prepends a bounded Global Context Anchor header of up to $K{\text{hub}}^{\max} = 8$ foundational root axioms and intermediate deductive bridges (Section 4.2, Equations 12b–12d), strictly preserving the $\mathcal{O}(N)$ linear complexity bound ($M_{\text{win}} \le 20$).
  2. Topologically Isolated Propositions ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{isolated}}$): Nodes lacking both internal ancestors and inferential descendants ($\text{InDegree}(v) = 0 \land \text{OutDegree}(v) = 0$, $\text{deg}(v) = 0$). In natural discourse, these subsume two semantically distinct categories:
  3. Standalone Scoping Context ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{scoping}}$): Legitimate institutional background, introductory framing, or statutory scope recitals stated by the author that are not formally mobilized as causal premises for subsequent claims.
  4. Unjustified Orphan Claims ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{orphan}}$): Standalone normative or empirical assertions asserted without supporting evidence, warrants, or inferential descendants.

Stateless Invariant Law: Because the Pure Stateless Causal Cohesion Evaluator (Section 4.2.1) computes topological invariants in 0 tokens without semantic introspection of proposition text, it cannot distinguish between benign scoping context and unjustified orphan assertions. Consequently, all degree-zero nodes are counted in $r_{\text{iso}}$, necessitating a calibrated tolerance ceiling ($r^{\max}_{L3}$) at higher BARS tiers to accommodate legitimate scoping discourse.
