docs.title: 3.1. Wave-Based Topological Execution
docs.text:
Because $\mathcal{G}{\text{DAG}}$ is acyclic, Kahn’s topological sort partitions $\mathcal{V}{\text{cog}}$ into discrete, parallel computational waves $\mathcal{W}0, \mathcal{W}_1, \dots, \mathcal{W}{J-1}$:

$$\mathcal{W}0 = { v \in \mathcal{V}{\text{cog}} \mid \text{InDegree}(v) = 0 } \tag{8}$$

$$\mathcal{W}{j+1} = \left{ v \in \mathcal{V}{\text{cog}} \setminus \bigcup_{l=0}^j \mathcal{W}l \;\middle|\; \text{Parents}(v) \subseteq \bigcup{l=0}^j \mathcal{W}_l \right} \tag{9}$$

Operators within wave $\mathcal{W}_j$ are executed concurrently as isolated asynchronous coroutines. Each operator $v \in \mathcal{W}_j$ evaluates an invariant deterministic function over immutable typed records:

$$\Phi_v: \prod_{u \in \text{Parents}(v)} \mathcal{O}u \times \mathcal{S}{\text{global}} \to \mathcal{O}_v \tag{10}$$

docs.title: 4. Topological Directed Atom (TDA) Scheduling and Structural Argument Truth Maintenance
4.1. Topological Directed Atom (TDA) Poset Scheduling and Verification
docs.text:
Nomenclature Demarcation and Scope Calibration: To prevent terminological confusion with Topological Data Analysis (TDA in applied mathematics and machine learning, which studies persistent homology, simplicial complexes, and Betti numbers $\beta_k$ over metric point clouds; Carlsson, 2009; Edelsbrunner & Harer, 2010), we explicitly clarify that in Quorum, the acronym TDA designates Topological Directed Atoms (and their associated dependency argumentation). The term topological is employed strictly in its foundational computer science and order-theoretic sense: Kahn's topological sorting (Kahn, 1962) on finite directed acyclic graphs inducing an Alexandroff topology and a specialization poset ($\mathcal{G}_{\text{LAG}}$). Quorum asserts no claims of computing algebraic homology groups or metric simplicial filtrations. Rather, TDA in Quorum denotes the order-theoretic scheduling, exact lexical provenance, and cycle-free verification of propositional claims:

  1. Strict Lexical Grounding: Proposition truth values are grounded directly in verbatim source evidence. Unanchored assertions fail closed ($\lambda_i = 0$).
  2. Cycle Elimination and Poset Acyclicity: Circular reasoning chains ($a_1 \implies a_2 \implies \dots \implies a_1$) violate epistemic partial order invariants. Rather than invoking homological machinery, circularities and phantom dependencies are detected prior to wave evaluation via Tarjan's strongly connected components and Johnson's elementary cycle enumeration algorithm (Tarjan, 1972; Johnson, 1975). Nodes participating in directed cycles are immediately quarantined, and any downstream nodes left unresolved after Kahn wave exhaustion are deterministically clamped to an unfulfilled state $\text{BLOCKED}$, enforcing strict directed acyclicity across the proposition graph.

docs.title: 4.1.1. Deterministic Physical Provenance Verification and Defense Against Fabricated Evidence
docs.text:
A foundational failure mode in contemporary LLM evaluation (including LLM-as-a-Judge [Zheng et al., 2023], G-Eval [Liu et al., 2023], and Self-RAG [Asai et al., 2024]) is Second-Order Hallucination (Quis custodiet ipsos custodes?). If a secondary LLM is queried to determine whether a document entails a proposition ($P( ext{Entail} \mid \mathcal{D}, au_i)$), the verifier is itself an autoregressive stochastic sampler susceptible to sycophancy, confirmation bias, and the synthesis of chimera quotes (stitching isolated words across disparate paragraphs into a fabricated sentence).

To defend against unanchored evidence and citation fabrications, Quorum strips the generative model of judicial authority. Rather than allowing the LLM to self-certify its outputs, evidence verification is structured across two orthogonal layers: physical citation provenance and exact lexical containment are verified exclusively through a compiled deterministic lexical verification engine, while semantic entailment is audited through role-asymmetric Popperian falsification and downstream A-SCM reachability:

  1. Gate 1: Post-Hoc Lexical Verification with Dual Normalization Invariant: While raw input text is preserved under conservative Canonical Composition (NFC) during initial ingress to maintain typographical provenance, the post-hoc verifier applies Unicode Compatibility Decomposition (NFKC) and canonical decomposition (NFD) symmetrically to both the source corpus $\mathcal{D}$ and the candidate extraction $\mathcal{C}i$. An invariant bidirectional index map $\mathcal{M}{ ext{idx}}: \mathbb{N} o \mathbb{N}$ maps normalized character indices back to original source byte positions. The candidate quote $\mathcal{C}_i$ is validated via exact $O(N)$ containment:

$$ ext{find}( ext{Norm}{ ext{NFKC}}(\mathcal{C}_i), ext{Norm}{ ext{NFKC}}(\mathcal{D})) eq -1$$

If matched, the exact verbatim string is sliced from the original immutable text, preventing case-folding or formatting drifts from fabricating false evidence. This two-tier normalization design ensures that typographical variations (specifically non-breaking spaces U+00A0 and en-spaces U+2002) do not induce false negative citation rejections during post-hoc auditing.

  1. Gate 2: Entropy Gate & Contiguity Guard (Chimera Quote Defense):
  2. Entropy Gate (< 10 chars): Short quotes under 10 characters (specifically isolated buzzwords) are strictly forbidden from approximate matching; 100% exact substring containment is unconditionally required.
  3. Contiguity Guard (< 30 chars): Short phrases enforce strict contiguous character sequence matching via partial string edit ratio, strictly prohibiting token reordering or word skipping.
  4. Token-Set Evaluation ($\ge 30$ chars): Longer spans evaluate token-set overlap to tolerate minor word-order permutations or morphological case conjugations. However, to prevent bag-of-words chimera stitching across disparate paragraphs, token-set overlap does not confer standalone acceptance: it is strictly constrained by Gate 5's downstream morphological stem-sequence alignment and unbroken longest-common-substring coverage verification.

  5. Safety Ceiling (> 1000 chars): Quotes exceeding 1000 characters trigger an immediate verification rejection to prevent prompt injection and quote stuffing.

  6. Gate 3: Cross-Speaker Provenance Boundary Guard: Discourse is partitioned into structured provenance capsules: $\mathcal{K}{ ext{user}}$ for human supervisor inputs, $\mathcal{K}{ ext{draft}}$ for model drafts, and $\mathcal{K}{ ext{task}}$ for task instructions. When evaluating human capability ($\sigma_i = ext{USER}$), candidate quotes must reside strictly inside $\mathcal{K}{ ext{user}}$:

$$ ext{Prov}(\mathcal{C}i, \sigma_i) = \mathbb{I}\left( ext{Lex}(\mathcal{C}_i, \mathcal{D}{ ext{speaker}}; \zeta) = 1 ight)$$

If an LLM quotes the AI assistant's draft to substantiate a human competence claim, the verifier rejects the claim on provenance boundary violation, mathematically preventing cross-speaker competence contamination.

  1. Gate 4: Reasoning Trace Triangulation: The model's structured schema requires an explicit reasoning trace $\mathcal{T}_i$ specifying an exact syntactic anchor $ ext{Anchor}_i$ and decision $ ext{Decision}_i \in { ext{PASS}, ext{FAIL}}$. Deterministic triangulation asserts three consistency invariants:
  2. Contradiction Ban: If $\mathcal{T}_i$ concludes $ ext{Decision}_i = ext{FAIL}$, but candidate quote vector $\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i eq \emptyset$, the atom is rejected for logical contradiction.
  3. Empty Anchor Ban: If $\mathcal{T}_i$ declares $ ext{Anchor}_i = \emptyset$, unanchored extraction fails closed.

  4. Hallucinated Anchor Ban: The anchor string parsed from the trace must physically exist in the source document; fabricated anchors trigger immediate rejection. Formally, this gate evaluates the syntactic anchor $ ext{Anchor}i$—a localized 2–5 word invariant lexical pivot extracted in the model's Chain-of-Thought—using strict Tier 1 normalized substring containment ($ ext{find}( ext{Norm}{ ext{NFKC}}( ext{Anchor}i), ext{Norm}{ ext{NFKC}}(\mathcal{D})) eq -1$). This guarantees that the physical sentence locus exists in $\mathcal{D}$. Concurrently, Gate 5 evaluates the full candidate quotation $\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$ spanning that locus using the parameterized predicate $ ext{Lex}(\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i, \mathcal{D}; \zeta{ ext{lex}})$, permitting bounded morphological stem-sequence verification and edit-distance relaxation when $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} < 100$.

  5. Gate 5: Piecewise-Stratified Lexical Strictness Schedule and Epistemic Strictness Decoupling: To eliminate cross-tier interference between scoring dampening and evidentiary verification, Quorum enforces Epistemic Strictness Decoupling: lexical verification strictness $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \in [0, 100]$ is mathematically decoupled from downstream scoring strictness $\zeta_{ ext{score}} \in [0, 100]$. Sourcing lexical thresholds from scoring rigor conflated evidentiary proof with grading penalty: under that prior coupling, an evaluation setting enforcing strict score dampening ($\zeta_{ ext{score}} = 85$, $e(85) = 1.70$) inadvertently disabled morphological stemming and edit tolerance, causing false-negative quote rejections on valid grammatical inflections. Under decoupled governance, the lexical predicate $ ext{Lex}(\vec{\mathcal{C}}i, \mathcal{D}; \zeta{ ext{lex}})$ executes an independent, calibrated four-tier deterministic schedule whenever $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} < 100$: (i) exact normalized substring containment, (ii) length-stratified edit similarity against nominal threshold $ au_{ ext{base}} = 75.0\%$ scaled by piecewise tier multipliers $m(\zeta_{ ext{lex}})$ ($ au_{ ext{tier}}(\zeta_{ ext{lex}}) = au_{ ext{base}} imes m(\zeta_{ ext{lex}})$: $ imes 0.80 \implies 60.0\%$ for $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} < 30$, $ imes 0.90 \implies 67.5\%$ for $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \in [30, 50)$, $ imes 1.00 \implies 75.0\%$ for $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \in [50, 85)$, and $ imes 1.02 \implies 76.5\%$ for $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \in [85, 100)$), (iii) Stage 3 multilingual Snowball morphological stem-sequence verification accommodating grammatical case inflections across all $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} < 100$ regardless of $\zeta_{ ext{score}}$, and (iv) contiguous longest-common-substring coverage verification ($\ge 70\%$ unbroken contiguous substring containment). Whereas the downstream scoring exponent $e(\zeta_{ ext{score}})$ in Equation (18) is continuous and piecewise linear, the upstream lexical threshold $ au_{ ext{tier}}(\zeta_{ ext{lex}})$ operates as a piecewise-stratified step function with a $23.5 ext{ pp}$ step discontinuity from $76.5\%$ at $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} = 99.9$ to $100.0\%$ at $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \ge 100$. This discrete jump marks an intentional qualitative phase transition: setting $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} = 100$ (Absolute Zero-Trust Forensic Mode) completely deactivates all approximate branches, stemming, and fuzzy fallbacks, enforcing uncompromising character-for-character physical substring containment.

Interaction of Gate 2 and Gate 5 Across Strictness Regimes: The interaction between Gate 2 and Gate 5 is strictly hierarchical and conditioned on $\zeta_{ ext{lex}}$: * At $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} \ge 100$ (Absolute Zero-Trust): Gate 5 imposes an uncompromising exact-match filter (threshold $ au_{ ext{tier}} = 100.0$). If exact normalized containment (Gate 1) fails, Gate 5 immediately aborts with falsification ($\lambda_i = 0$), completely bypassing all approximate branches in Gate 2 and Gate 5 (stemming and longest-common-substring). In this regime, zero token reordering, character substitution, or word stitching is tolerated. * At $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} < 100$ (Calibrated Multi-Tier Cascades): When an extraction is not an exact substring, Gate 2 and Gate 5 cooperate as a multi-tier defense against chimera quotes. For short phrases ($< 30$ chars), Gate 2 enforces strict contiguous substring alignment. For longer phrases ($\ge 30$ chars), while Gate 2 permits token-set overlap to accommodate surface inflection and token reordering, Gate 5 requires that the citation also satisfy contiguous morphological stem-sequence alignment or achieve $\ge 70\%$ unbroken longest-common-substring coverage. This ensures that bag-of-words overlap cannot stitch disjoint sentences into a false continuous quote. * Decoupled Execution Independence: Workflows configure $\zeta_{ ext{lex}}$ and $\zeta_{ ext{score}}$ independently. A workflow may mandate strict scoring rigor ($\zeta_{ ext{score}} = 85$) while maintaining balanced lexical verification ($\zeta_{ ext{lex}} = 50$) to accept valid Finnish case declensions, or enforce absolute lexical verification ($\zeta_{ ext{lex}} = 100$) while maintaining linear scoring ($\zeta_{ ext{score}} = 0$). * Operational Strictness in Empirical Trials: Production audit runs were executed at baseline strictness $\zeta = 0$ ($\gamma(0) = 1.00$), whereas ablation stress tests evaluated the impact of the lexical firewall up to $\zeta_{ ext{lex}} = 100$ (see Sections 8.3 and 8.5).

Under this five-gate architecture, propositional grounding does not rely on unconstrained LLM self-evaluation. An atom $ au_i$ achieves physical citation anchoring ($\lambda_i = 1$) if and only if all five deterministic verification gates succeed, bounding the probability of accepting a fabricated or spliced citation by the physical string collision rate $\epsilon_{ ext{lexical}} o 0$.

docs.title: 4.2. Argumentative Structural Dependency Models (A-SCM) and Truth Maintenance
docs.text:
Ontological Scope and the Enthymeme Boundary: Unlike physical systems where variables $\mathbf{V}$ represent empirical data-generating mechanisms, natural discourse is inherently pragmatic, elliptical, and enthymematic (Toulmin, 1958; Grice, 1975). Human authors routinely omit common-sense warrants and intermediate mechanisms, while language models trained on autoregressive prediction behave as "causal parrots" conflating associative correlation with causation (Zečević et al., 2023). Therefore, Quorum does not claim that textual analysis discovers objective physical causality. Instead, Quorum formalizes the Argumentative Structural Causal Model (A-SCM), evaluating the internal explanatory sufficiency and structural evidentiary rigor of the authored thesis.

Definition 2 (Argumentative Structural Causal Model). An authored discourse is modeled as a five-tuple:

$$\mathcal{M}_{\text{arg}} = \langle \mathbf{U}, \mathbf{V}, \mathbf{W}, \mathbf{F}, P(\mathbf{U}) \rangle \tag{11}$$

where $\mathbf{V} = {V_1, \dots, V_n}$ represents explicit propositional claims grounded in verbatim text ($\lambda = 1$), $\mathbf{W}$ represents explicit Toulmin warrants (backing and explanatory transmission mechanisms), $\mathbf{U} = {U_{\text{enthymeme}}, U_{\text{context}}}$ represents unstated background assumptions and latent conversational confounders, and $\mathbf{F} = {f_1, \dots, f_m}$ defines structural argument dependencies:

$$V_i = f_i(\mathbf{PA}_i, \mathbf{W}_i, U_i), \quad \mathbf{PA}_i \subseteq \mathbf{V} \setminus { V_i } \tag{12}$$

Definition 3 (Context-Bounded Sliding-Window Proposition Linking, $\Phi_{\text{link}}$). Constructing the Argument DAG $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{deps}})$ directly from unconstrained discourse via exhaustive pairwise comparison requires an intractable $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ LLM context overhead. Quorum executes graph discovery through a two-tier neurosymbolic pipeline: 1. Lexically Anchored Proposition Atomization ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{claim}}$): Two-pass atomic decomposition extracts candidate propositions grounded in verbatim citations satisfying physical provenance verification ($\lambda_i = 1$). 2. Sliding-Window Dependency Prediction ($\mathcal{E}_{\text{deps}}$): Propositions are partitioned into sequential chunk packets and scanned through a sliding window of width $W{\text{win}}$ chunks with step overlap $O_{\text{win}}$. Within each window, atoms are assigned deterministic, short attention anchors ($a_0, a_1$) to eliminate token bloat and prevent system UUID hallucinations. The model predicts directed causal dependencies ($X \xrightarrow{\vec{\mathcal{W}}{XY}} Y$) along with an explicit Multi-Segment Toulmin Warrant Vector $\vec{\mathcal{W}}{XY} = (w_{XY,1}, \dots, w_{XY,m})$ ($1 \le m \le 3$) verified by the lexical firewall ($\lambda(\vec{\mathcal{W}}{XY}) = 1$) and expected precondition states. 3. Defensive Invariant Enforcement: Hallucinated or out-of-window aliases are rejected fail-fast, immediate self-dependencies ($X \to X$) are pruned, and directed cycles are detected prior to wave execution via Johnson's elementary cycle algorithm. If cycles are detected, participating nodes are marked by an indicator $\text{CycleDetected} = \text{True}$, immediately clamping downstream argument cohesion to the Novice floor ($L_1$). 4. Bounded Structural Hub & Frontier Header Protocol ($K_{\text{hub}}^{\max} = 8$, Bounded Deliverable Root Axiom Anchoring): To eliminate sliding-window horizon truncation of both foundational premises and intermediate multi-premise synthesis lemmas without context saturation, Quorum implements the Bounded Deliverable Root Axiom Anchoring and structural hub protocol. Mined candidate propositions originating from candidate-endorsed deliverables are partitioned into two priority pools in the cumulative prior-window subgraph $\mathcal{G}{<w}$: (i) Foundational Root Axioms ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{root}}$): Zero-in-degree deliverable premises ($\text{InDegree}{\text{deliv}}(v) = 0$) ranked deterministically by descending out-degree and ascending document sequence index ($index{\text{asc}}$, prioritizing foundational framing): $$\text{Rank}{\text{root}}(v) = \langle -\text{OutDegree}{\mathcal{G}{<w}}(v), \text{atom_index}{\text{asc}} \rangle \tag{12b}$$ (ii) Deductive Bridges & Frontier Syntheses ($\mathcal{V}_{\text{bridge}}$): Intermediate lemmas and multi-premise convergence claims satisfying $(\text{InDegree}(v) \ge 1 \land \text{OutDegree}(v) \ge 1) \lor \text{InDegree}(v) \ge 2$, ranked by Laplace-smoothed product scoring and descending document sequence index ($index_{\text{desc}}$, prioritizing recent frontier syntheses): $$\text{Rank}{\text{bridge}}(v) = \langle -(\text{InDegree}{\mathcal{G}{<w}}(v) \cdot (\text{OutDegree}{\mathcal{G}{<w}}(v) + 1)), \text{atom_index}{\text{desc}} \rangle \tag{12c}$$ Single-premise leaf claims ($\text{InDegree}(v) = 1 \land \text{OutDegree}(v) = 0$) are excluded from both pools. Up to $K_{\text{hub}}^{\max} = 8$ top-ranked anchors are dynamically allocated into a persistent anchor header $\mathcal{H}{\text{anchors}}$ prepended to downstream chunk packets. To guarantee adequate capacity for current-window proposition discovery, the effective anchor quota $K{\text{eff}}$ adapts dynamically to the current window size $W_{\text{current}}$ via a starvation-immune dynamic slack waterfall: $$K_{\text{eff}} = \min(K_{\text{hub}}^{\max}, \max(0, M_{\text{win}} - W_{\text{current}})), \quad W_{\text{min}} = 12, \quad M_{\text{win}} \le 20 \tag{12d}$$ dividing base quotas evenly ($\text{base_root} = \min(K_{\text{root}}, \lceil K_{\text{eff}} / 2 \rceil)$, $\text{base_bridge} = \min(K_{\text{bridge}}, \lfloor K_{\text{eff}} / 2 \rfloor)$) and transferring unconsumed slack bidirectionally. This reserves a guaranteed minimum quota $W_{\text{min}} = 12$ atoms for current-window claims while bounding total window size to $M_{\text{win}} \le 20$ atoms. Crucially, structural anchors participate in pairwise dependency extraction in a single deterministic topological pass without recursive graph traversal, preserving the Local Causal Markov Condition and enabling long-range inferential transitivity ($A \to B \to C$) across arbitrary document horizons.

Epistemic Demarcation: The Two-Pillar Causal Architecture: To resolve the foundational question of how computational systems evaluate causality in natural language discourse without circular re-prompting or conflating baseline grading with counterfactual stress-testing, Quorum establishes a decoupled Two-Pillar Causal Architecture:

  1. Pillar 1: Pure Stateless Baseline Evaluation (Section 4.2.1): Generates the 0-token evaluative BARS score for the causal reasoning matrix $\mathcal{M}{\text{Causal}}$ across hierarchical competence Tiers $L_1 \dots L_5$ (Equation 13). It evaluates static, unperturbed macroscopic topological invariants ($|\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}|$, $r_{\text{iso}}$, $r_{\text{LCC}}$, $r_{\text{conv}}$, acyclicity) under the Cumulative Guttman Invariant, functioning as a robust low-pass filter against stochastic extraction variance.
  2. Pillar 2: Discrete ATMS Truth Maintenance & Counterfactual Surgery (Algorithm 1): Operates on compiled graph instances to perform interactive counterfactual stress-testing (Rungs 2/3), forward wave precondition enforcement, backward root-cause isolation ($RC$), prescriptive remediation (actionable premise repair recommendations), and secondary fault dampening (fair fault-attribution scoring breakdowns).

Quiescent Baseline vs. Active Counterfactual Dynamics: In a clean baseline evaluation pass where all extracted discourse claims are validly grounded and acyclic, Algorithm 1 operates in its quiescent baseline state: $S^* = S_{\text{init}}$, $\text{Cascade} = \emptyset$, and $RC = \emptyset$. Its active perturbation dynamics are engaged conditionally: (i) dynamically when upstream processing errors or cycle defects occur during execution, (ii) prescriptively to deduplicate downstream cascading penalties, or (iii) interactively within the supervisory interface when an auditor simulates counterfactual premise retractions ($X \gets \text{RETRACTED}$) to audit warrant independence.

Operationalization of Premise Perturbation via Discrete Graph Surgery & Truth Maintenance: In Assumption-Based Truth Maintenance Systems (ATMS; Doyle, 1979; de Kleer, 1986), retracting or invalidating a premise $X$ is evaluated graph-theoretically by isolating the premise ($X \gets \text{RETRACTED}$) and severing incoming support edges in the dependency graph $\mathcal{G}_{\text{pruned}}$.

A foundational question in NLP argumentation is: Which computational system physically evaluates the downstream consequences of this structural intervention in discourse? If a secondary LLM is re-prompted to judge whether claim $Y$ survives without premise $X$, the pipeline relapses into second-order stochasticity and confirmation bias.

In Quorum, once $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{deps}})$ is compiled, structural interventions and downstream cascades are NOT executed via LLM prompts or statistical regression. Conditional on the compiled graph instance $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}}$, the extracted discourse is evaluated via deterministic graph surgery and Assumption-Based Truth Maintenance Systems (ATMS) (Doyle, 1979; de Kleer, 1986) evaluated over formal computational argumentation graphs (Dung, 1995), formalized in Algorithm 1 as the Unified Formal Specification:

Algorithm 1: Discrete Structural Argument Surgery & Truth Maintenance (ATMS)
================================================================================
Input  : Argument DAG G = (V, E, W), retracted node X in V, counterfactual state x* in {FAILED, BLOCKED},
         gate semantics mode in {Conjunctive, Disjunctive}
Output : Perturbed state mapping S*, Reachability Cascade Reach(X), Root Causes RC,
         Node Root Causes RC_node, Warrant/Edge Root Causes RC_edge
================================================================================
Helper Functions:
  BrokenSupport(v, E_ref) := { P in Parents(v, E_ref) | S*[P] != expected_status(P, v) or lambda(W_{Pv}) == 0 }
  expected_status(P', C)  := EdgeCondition(P', C).expected_state (defaults to PASSED)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1: S* <- InitialStateMap(V)                          // Base status from lexical grounding Gate
2: S*[X] <- x*                                       // Clamp intervened node to counterfactual state
3: Queue Q <- [ X ]
4: Visited Vis <- { X }
5: Cascade <- []
6: while Q is not empty do
7:     curr <- Q.pop_front()
8:     for each child C in Children(curr, E) do
9:         if C not in Vis then
10:            // Evaluate Precondition & Warrant Gate under active topology semantics:
11:            if mode == Conjunctive then
12:                // Deductive Reachability Gate: All antecedents and supporting warrants must be valid
13:                survives_gate <- forall P' in Parents(C, E):
14:                                 (S*[P'] == expected_status(P', C) and lambda(W_{P'C}) == 1)
15:            else
16:                // Corroborative Warrant Redundancy: Alternative valid warrant shields C
17:                survives_gate <- exists P' in Parents(C, E)
18:                                 such that S*[P'] == expected_status(P', C) and lambda(W_{P'C}) == 1
19:            end if
20:            if not survives_gate then
21:                S*[C] <- BLOCKED                      // (or unfulfilled on precondition mismatch)
22:                Vis.add(C)
23:                Cascade.append(C)
24:                Q.push_back(C)
25:            end if
26:        end if
27:    end for
28: end while
29: RC_node <- { v in V | S*[v] in {FAILED, BLOCKED} and BrokenSupport(v, E) == emptyset }
30: RC_edge <- { (P', v) in E | S*[v] == BLOCKED and S*[P'] == PASSED and (lambda(W_{P'v}) == 0 or S*[P'] != expected_status(P', v)) }
31: RC <- RC_node union { v in V | exists P' in Parents(v, E) such that (P', v) in RC_edge }
32: return (S*, Cascade, RC, RC_node, RC_edge)
================================================================================

Algorithmic Guarantees and Structural Properties of Algorithm 1: 1. Zero Second-Order LLM Calls & Linear Complexity Bound: Lines 6–28 operate in deterministic linear time $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}| + |\mathcal{E}|)$ over in-memory adjacency lists. While Lines 13–19 present explicit quantifier scans over $\text{Parents}(C, E)$ for declarative mathematical readability, standard operational implementations enforce $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}| + |\mathcal{E}|)$ linear complexity by maintaining an integer degree counter $\text{deg}{\text{valid}}[C]$ initialized in $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{E}|)$ and decremented in $\mathcal{O}(1)$ time per failed incoming edge. In conjunctive mode ($\bigwedge$), child $C$ short-circuits upon the first invalid parent ($\text{deg}{\text{valid}}[C] < \text{InDegree}(C)$); in disjunctive mode ($\bigvee$), $C$ transitions to an unfulfilled state $\text{BLOCKED}$ if and only if all corroborating parents fail ($\text{deg}{\text{valid}}[C] = 0$), guaranteeing that each edge $(P, C) \in \mathcal{E}$ is traversed at most once. No stochastic LLM sampling occurs during perturbation evaluation. 2. Equivalence to Pearl/ATMS Edge Severing on DAGs: In structural causal models (Pearl, 2000), an intervention $do(X = x^)$ severs incoming arrows to $X$. In Algorithm 1, clamping the state $S^[X] \gets x^$ (Line 2) and propagating reachability forward strictly to descendants along directed paths in $E$ is algebraically identical to explicit edge deletion, because in an acyclic graph (DAG), no directed path exists from any descendant $C \in \text{Descendants}(X)$ back to $X$ ($\text{Descendants}(X) \cap \text{Parents}(X) = \emptyset$). Backward fault attribution (Lines 29–31) evaluates parent failure and warrant grounding over the original dependency graph $E$ ($\text{BrokenSupport}(v, E) = \emptyset$), mirroring the production causal discovery engine where a node is categorized in $\text{RC}_{\text{node}}$ if and only if none of its true inbound parents in $E$ possess invalid state or broken inferential warrants. 3. Deductive Reachability Gating and Dual-Role Wave Pruning: Lines 11–15 enforce strict conjunctive precondition semantics ($\bigwedge$) during forward reachability evaluation. Every antecedent $P' \in \text{Parents}(C)$ is a necessary condition: child $C$ survives if and only if every antecedent satisfies its expected status and* its supporting inferential warrant is physically grounded in the discourse ($\lambda(W{P'C}) = 1$). If any parent enters a blocked or failed state or possesses an unverified warrant, child $C$ deterministically short-circuits to an unfulfilled state $\text{BLOCKED}$.

Architectural Demarcation of Dual-Role Wave Pruning: We explicitly disambiguate how this short-circuiting mechanism operates across Quorum's two distinct DAG execution domains: - (a) Mined Argument DAG ($\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}, \mathcal{E}_{\text{deps}})$ in Algorithm 1): Because all discourse propositions $v \in \mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}$ are extracted in Pass 1 and linked in Pass 2, Algorithm 1 executes purely in-memory in 0 additional LLM tokens ($\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}| + |\mathcal{E}|)$, $< 1.0\text{ ms}$). Here, short-circuiting prunes child nodes from the epistemic validity reachability set—accumulating them into $\text{Cascade}$ to quantify argument collapse and isolate root causes ($RC$) without further computation. Zero subsequent LLM verification passes are dispatched over $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}}$. - (b) Rubric Evaluation Poset ($\mathcal{A}_{\text{rubric}}$): Concurrently, the identical Kahn wave short-circuiting primitive is deployed during matrix evaluation over fixed BARS criteria ($a_i \in \mathcal{A}{\text{rubric}}$). When an antecedent rubric criterion fails its expected status (specifically Novice Level 1 baseline failure), dependent child criteria are transitioned to an unfulfilled state ($\text{N/A}$ or $\text{BLOCKED}$) prior to wave dispatch, completely pruning child nodes from generative model sensor evaluation batches, thereby eliminating redundant inference tokens and evaluation latency. 4. Harmonized Backward Fault Attribution & Dual Root Cause Isolation: Lines 29–31 execute backward graph traversal across inbound dependencies of evaluated argument structures over the original edge graph $E$. To prevent the logical edge case where downstream blocked nodes are misclassified as independent root causes due to inferential edge failures, blame attribution is harmonized with the forward reachability gate via: $$\text{BrokenSupport}(v, E) := \left{ P' \in \text{Parents}(v, E) \;\middle\vert{}\; S^[P'] \neq \text{expected_status}(P', v) \;\lor\; \lambda(W_{P'v}) == 0 \right}$$ The engine cleanly decomposes root causes into two mutually exclusive, strictly typed sets: - (a) Node Root Causes ($\text{RC}{\text{node}}$): Validating claims that failed intrinsic physical grounding or were directly intervened upon ($S^[v] \in {\text{FAILED}, \text{BLOCKED}}$) with zero broken parent supports ($\text{BrokenSupport}(v, E) = \emptyset$). - (b) Warrant/Edge Root Causes ($\text{RC}_{\text{edge}}$): Identifying inferential transmission breakdowns where parent premises are valid ($S^[P'] = \text{PASSED}$), but the connecting inferential warrant lacks physical lexical grounding ($\lambda(W_{P'v}) = 0$) or violates expected precondition states, transitioning child $v$ to $\text{BLOCKED}$. This ensures downstream consequences are never conflated with independent claim errors, and authors are not penalized for ungrounded warrants as if they had asserted false propositions. 5. Corroborative Redundancy & Counterfactual Surgery: Lines 16–19 formalize corroborative warrant redundancy (disjunctive reachability, $\bigvee$), where alternative valid evidentiary warrants preserve claim truth values. Because satisfying $S^[P'] == \text{expected_status}(P', C)$ already excludes any compromised parent in $\text{Vis}$ (since $\forall v \in \text{Vis}, S^[v] \in {\text{FAILED}, \text{BLOCKED}}$), checking $\text{Parents}(C, E)$ guarantees that only currently valid, uncompromised parent warrants can corroborate child $C$. In the execution architecture, real-time forward DAG evaluation over rubric criteria ($\mathcal{A}{\text{rubric}}$) and interactive counterfactual simulation over discourse graphs ($\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}}$) are cleanly decoupled: the forward wave scheduler maintains strict single responsibility over real-time sensor batch evaluation and mutation invariance, while interactive counterfactual surgery (Algorithm 1) operates on transient graph representations in 0 tokens. 6. Dynamic Multi-Parent Cascade Resolution: In disjunctive mode ($\bigvee$), child node $C$ is added to $\text{Vis}$ and $Q$ if and only if all corroborating parent paths collapse ($\text{survives_gate} = \text{False}$). If $C$ survives an initial parent failure due to an alternative valid parent, it remains outside $\text{Vis}$, ensuring that if subsequent upstream failures in the same wave sever its remaining warrants, $C$ is correctly re-evaluated, transitioned to $\text{BLOCKED}$, and propagated downstream without graph traversal leaks. 7. Instance-Conditional Determinism vs. Stochastic Extraction Non-Isomorphism: We formalize a strict architectural boundary: Algorithm 1's computational determinism and polynomial time bounds $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}| + |\mathcal{E}|)$ are strictly conditional on a compiled graph instance* $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})$. When extracting discourse graphs from unconstrained natural text via frontier autoregressive decoders, verbatim quote overlap between independent stochastic runs is bounded ($25.3\%–31.9\%$; Section 8.6, Point 5), meaning separate runs yield distinct node sets $\mathcal{V}_1 \neq \mathcal{V}_2$ and non-isomorphic micro-topologies ($\mathcal{G}_1 \not\simeq \mathcal{G}_2$). Consequently, executing Algorithm 1 across Run 1 versus Run 2 operates on disjoint node universes and yields distinct run-specific root-cause sets $RC_1 \neq RC_2$. Node-level premise retraction and root-cause isolation provide rigorous, deterministic local explainability for an individual compiled run, whereas end-to-end stability across runs is guaranteed at the macro-topological invariant level ($r{\text{iso}}$, acyclicity, and Guttman cohesion $\mathcal{C}_{\text{causal}}$) via topological low-pass filtering.

Scope Demarcation (Discrete ATMS Truth Maintenance vs. Observational Do-Calculus): As defined above, Quorum evaluates discrete computational argumentation graphs and Assumption-Based Truth Maintenance Systems (Doyle, 1979; de Kleer, 1986; Dung, 1995) rather than observational statistical distributions or backdoor adjustments. Algorithm 1 deterministically audits whether an author's conclusions retain surviving physical warrants ($\mathbf{W}$) or experience justification collapse when antecedent premises are retracted.

This maps structurally to the epistemic demands of the Three Rungs of Argument Rigor: * Rung 1 (Associative Co-occurrence & Fluff): Unidirectional linguistic correlation lacking explicit warrants ($\mathbf{W} = \emptyset$). Listing co-occurring industry trends without causal transmission mechanisms incurs severe passive delegation penalties. * Rung 2 (Intervention Audit & Warrant Isolation): Simulating structural interventions by pruning parent dependencies. The audit evaluates whether the text explicitly defines operational mechanisms $\mathbf{W}{XY}$ isolating the claim from common-cause confounding ($U{XY}$). * Rung 3 (Counterfactual Stress-Testing): Evaluating counterfactual boundary transitions. The audit examines whether the author subjected proposed strategies to "what-if" boundary conditions, failure thresholds, negative externalities, and resource exhaustion scenarios.

docs.title: 4.2.1. Pure Stateless Causal Cohesion Evaluation and the 0-Token Cumulative Guttman Invariant
docs.text:
In contemporary multi-agent reasoning systems, assessing whether an authored discourse forms a coherent, non-trivial argument is routinely delegated to secondary LLM evaluation passes (specifically LLM-as-a-Judge prompting with subjective instructions including "Rate the causal coherence from 1 to 5"; Zheng et al., 2023). This practice introduces stochastic scoring variance, circular hallucinations, token cost explosions, and prompt-injection vulnerability.

Quorum eliminates stochastic judge prompts for argument cohesion through the Pure Stateless Causal Cohesion Evaluator, a deterministic compute engine that evaluates macro-argument structure directly from the topology of the mined Argument DAG $\mathcal{G}{ ext{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}, \mathcal{E}_{ ext{deps}})$:

  1. The Cumulative Guttman Invariant and Multi-Factor Topological Predicates: Structural argument cohesion is formalized as a strictly cumulative, monotonic scale (Guttman, 1944) across Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) Tiers 1–5 ($L_1 \subset L_2 \subset L_3 \subset L_4 \subset L_5$). To eliminate graph-theoretic degeneracies where fragmented subgraphs trivially pass degree-based filters, Quorum defines three orthogonal topological metrics over $\mathcal{G}_{ ext{LAG}}$:

  2. Weakly Connected Components & Largest Component Ratio ($r_{ ext{LCC}}$): Let $ ext{WCC}(\mathcal{G}{ ext{LAG}}) = {\mathcal{C}_1, \dots, \mathcal{C}_k}$ be the set of weakly connected components in the underlying undirected projection of $\mathcal{G}{ ext{LAG}}$, with largest weakly connected component $\mathcal{V}{ ext{LCC}} = \arg\max{\mathcal{C} \in ext{WCC}} |\mathcal{V}(\mathcal{C})|$. The macro-reachability component ratio is defined as: $$r_{ ext{LCC}} = egin{cases} 1.0, & |\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \le 1 \ rac{|\mathcal{V}{ ext{LCC}}|}{|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}|}, & |\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| > 1 \end{cases}$$

  3. Isolated Concept Fraction ($r_{ ext{iso}}$): The fraction of propositions possessing degree zero ($ ext{InDegree}(v) + ext{OutDegree}(v) = 0$): $$r_{ ext{iso}} = rac{|{v \in \mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}} \mid ext{InDegree}(v) + ext{OutDegree}(v) = 0}|}{|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}|}$$
  4. Branch Convergence Ratio ($r_{ ext{conv}}$): The fraction of claims synthesizing multi-premise warrants ($ ext{InDegree}(v) \ge 2$), measuring convergent evidentiary branches: $$r_{ ext{conv}} = rac{|{v \in \mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}} \mid ext{InDegree}(v) \ge 2}|}{|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}|}$$

Dual-Track Evaluation Architecture (Continuous Metric Telemetry vs. Discrete Guttman Invariants): Structural argument evaluation operates across two cleanly decoupled tracks: 1. Continuous Metric Telemetry Scalar: For diagnostic reporting, dashboards, and analytical surfaces, structural logical cohesion is computed as a continuous scalar metric $ ext{CohesionScore} \in [0, 1]$: $$ ext{CohesionScore} = egin{cases} 1.0, & |\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| = 0 \ \left(1.0 - r{ ext{iso}} ight) \cdot \left( rac{1}{2} ight)^{\mathbb{I}( ext{CycleDetected})}, & |\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| > 0 \end{cases}$$ where the factor $(1/2)^{\mathbb{I}( ext{CycleDetected})}$ penalizes directed cycle defects in continuous telemetry, halving the displayed scalar score even when discrete grading is clamped to the Novice floor. 2. Discrete BARS Guttman Tier Invariants ($L_1 \dots L_5$): In contrast to continuous scalar reporting, discrete qualification across Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) tiers is governed by strictly cumulative, monotonic Boolean predicates. Because directed acyclicity $( eg ext{CycleDetected})$ is enforced as a strict prerequisite at Level 2 (and inherited monotonically by $L_3 \dots L_5$), $\mathbb{I}( ext{CycleDetected}) \equiv 0$ for all candidate acyclic graphs eligible to pass higher tiers, identically collapsing the scalar score to $ ext{CohesionScore} \equiv 1.0 - r{ ext{iso}}$. To eliminate algebraic redundancy between $ ext{CohesionScore} \ge heta_{Lk}$ and $r_{ ext{iso}} \le r^{\max}{Lk}$ (where $r{ ext{iso}} \le r^{\max}{Lk}$ strictly dominates $1.0 - r{ ext{iso}} \ge heta_{Lk}$), the hierarchical BARS predicates are formalized directly through non-redundant structural invariant bounds: $$ egin{aligned} L_1 &= (|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \ge 1) \quad ( ext{Novice floor requires non-empty discourse graph}) \ L_2 &= L_1 \;\land\; (|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \ge 2) \;\land\; ( eg ext{CycleDetected}) \;\land\; (r_{ ext{iso}} \le 1.0 - heta_{L2}) \;\land\; (r_{ ext{LCC}} \ge r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, L2}) \ L_3 &= L_2 \;\land\; (|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \ge 5) \;\land\; (r_{ ext{iso}} \le r^{\max}{L3}) \;\land\; (r{ ext{LCC}} \ge r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, L3}) \ L_4 &= L_3 \;\land\; (|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \ge 10) \;\land\; (r_{ ext{iso}} \le r^{\max}{L4}) \;\land\; (r{ ext{LCC}} \ge r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, L4}) \;\land\; (r{ ext{conv}} \ge r^{\min}{ ext{conv}, L4}) \ L_5 &= L_4 \;\land\; (|\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}| \ge 15) \;\land\; (r_{ ext{iso}} \le r^{\max}{L5}) \;\land\; (r{ ext{LCC}} \ge r^{\min}_{ ext{LCC}, L5}) \end{aligned} ag{13}$$

In the system configuration, thresholds are parameterized as: * $ heta_{L2} = 0.30 \implies 1.0 - heta_{L2} = 0.70$ and $r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, L2} = 0.35$ (minimum cohesion and component core for Level 2 emerging chains), * $r^{\max}{L3} = 0.20$ (baseline production default; satisfying $r^{\max}{L3} \le 1.0 - heta{L3} = 0.50$, dominating continuous thresholding) and $r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, L3} = 0.50$ (maximum 20% isolated claims and 50% majority component for Level 3 Toulmin warrant grounding; in exploratory cross-genre sensitivity analysis [Section 8.3], a calibrated configuration $r^{\max}{L3} = 0.30$ accommodates legitimate standalone scoping context [$\mathcal{V}{ ext{scoping}}$] in strategic discourse where background framing premises lacking downstream causal edges [$ ext{OutDegree}(v) = 0$] are counted in $r{ ext{iso}}$ under the 0-token stateless evaluation law), * $r^{\max}{L4} = 0.15$ (satisfying $r^{\max}{L4} \le 1.0 - heta_{L4} = 0.30$), $r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, L4} = 0.70$, and $r^{\min}{ ext{conv}, L4} = 0.05$ (requiring branch convergence and multi-premise synthesis for Level 4), * $r^{\max}{L5} = 0.05$ (satisfying $r^{\max}{L5} \le 1.0 - heta_{L5} = 0.15$) and $r^{\min}_{ ext{LCC}, L5} = 0.85$ (maximum 5% isolated claims and 85% unified macro-reachability for Level 5 mastery).

Graph-Theoretic Invariant Proof: Defense Against Dyad Fragmentation: We formalize why enforcing the orthogonal component threshold $r_{ ext{LCC}} \ge r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, Lk}$ in Equation (13) is mathematically necessary. Suppose an authored text produces a completely fragmented discourse graph consisting of $k = n/2$ disjoint, unconnected pairs ($v_1 o v_2, \; v_3 o v_4, \dots$). Under a naive degree-zero formulation ($1 - r{ ext{iso}}$), every node possesses $ ext{deg}(v) = 1 > 0$, yielding $r_{ ext{iso}} = 0.0$ and $\mathbb{I}( ext{CycleDetected}) = 0$. Consequently, a collection of disconnected two-node islands would trivially achieve a perfect raw $ ext{CohesionScore} = 1.00$ and potentially pass higher tiers if cohesion were evaluated without reachability gates, despite possessing zero global reachability, zero macro-coherence, and zero multi-premise synthesis. By enforcing $r_{ ext{LCC}} \ge r^{\min}{ ext{LCC}, Lk}$ as an independent Boolean conjunct at every level $L_2 \dots L_5$, the largest component size is bounded by $|\mathcal{V}{ ext{LCC}}| = 2$, yielding $r_{ ext{LCC}} = 2/n o 0$ as $n$ grows. For any non-trivial discourse ($n \ge 6$), $r_{ ext{LCC}} \le 0.33 < r^{\min}_{ ext{LCC}, L2} = 0.35$, which immediately fails Level 2 ($L_2 = ext{False}$) and deterministically clamps the fragmented discourse to the Novice floor ($L_1$), proving absolute mathematical defense against dyad fragmentation without double-penalizing component size in the scalar cohesion score.

Decoupling of Baseline Guttman Scoring from Perturbation Dynamics: Under Quorum's Two-Pillar Causal Architecture (Section 4.2), baseline Guttman scoring evaluates the invariant topological properties of the unperturbed base graph in 0 additional tokens, preserving test–retest stability. Conversely, Algorithm 1 acts as a decoupled diagnostic operator $\mathcal{T}_{X, x^*}$ for interactive counterfactual surgery, automated sensitivity audits, and cascading fault isolation.

  1. The 0-Token Evaluation Contract and Token Boundary Demarcation: We explicitly delineate the token boundaries of the causal pipeline. While upstream proposition extraction and sliding-window dependency linking operate as LLM-assisted cognitive steps (consuming bounded input and output tokens during Phase 1 DAG execution), the subsequent macro-argument evaluation and counterfactual graph surgery consume strictly zero additional LLM tokens ($0 ext{ tokens consumed}$). Instead of prompting an external LLM judge to subjectively rate coherence, the Pure Stateless Causal Cohesion Evaluator computes structural graph invariants (connected component ratio, acyclicity, isolated concept fraction $r_{ ext{iso}}$) in linear time $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}| + |\mathcal{E}|)$ and projects them deterministically into BARS Tiers 1–5 via the Cumulative Guttman Invariant (Equation 13). This completely insulates qualitative scoring from the stochastic token volatility, prompt injection risks, and cost explosions of secondary LLM-as-a-judge passes.

  2. Cycle Defect Quarantine: If the topological cycle detector detects directed cycles ($\mathcal{C}_{ ext{cycle}} eq \emptyset$), the graph violates DAG partial order invariants. The evaluator flags a structural cycle defect ($ ext{CycleDetected} = ext{True}$), immediately failing Level 2 ($L_2 = ext{False}$) and clamping the argument cohesion score to the Novice floor ($l = 1$).

  3. Idempotent Graph Fusion and Concurrency Guards: In multi-step or multi-model executions, redundant evaluations of identical causal sources are prevented via idempotent graph fusion guards, guaranteeing deterministic, replayable scoring.

  4. Multi-Document Ingress Scope, Dynamic Input Roles, and the Deliverable Subgraph Invariant: Enterprise workflows evaluate submissions composed of arbitrary dynamic input documents $\mathfrak{D} = {D_1, \dots, D_K}$. Rather than imposing rigid, static document triads or fixed file keys, Quorum classifies input documents dynamically through orthogonal typology predicates:

  5. Candidate Deliverables ($ ext{IsDeliverable}(D) = ext{True}$),
  6. Conversational Steering & Dialogue History ($ ext{IsDialogue}(D) = ext{True}$),
  7. Reference Instructions & Contextual Tasks ($ ext{IsTask}(D) = ext{True}$).

While the composite proposition graph $\mathcal{G}{ ext{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{ ext{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{ ext{deps}})$ is mined across the full concatenated multi-document payload to discover end-to-end provenance across inputs, evaluating structural argument cohesion ($\mathcal{M}{ ext{Causal}}$) requires formal deliverable subgraph induction to avoid construct validity confounding: * The Construct Validity Confound of Concatenated Ingress: In unpartitioned evaluation, conversational steering turns (specifically prompt formatting directives or conversational clarifications), authorial reflection documents, and contextual assignments do not form dense deductive chains with deliverable arguments, emerging predominantly as degree-zero nodes ($ ext{InDegree}(v) + ext{OutDegree}(v) = 0$). When pooled into a single global denominator, an operator who engages in thorough supervisory steering or self-reflection generates more non-deliverable nodes, artificially distorting global $r_{ ext{iso}}$ ($52.48\%$ in Pair A, $23.6\%–26.6\%$ in Pair B) and conflating conversational framing with substantive argument structure. * Deliverable Subgraph Induction and Denominator Invariant: Because Ingress Gate 3 tracks source document provenance for each extracted proposition atom via document index mapping $ ext{Prov}(v) \in \mathfrak{D}$ and parses structured document boundary capsules, the 0-token Pure Stateless Causal Cohesion Evaluator evaluates deliverable cohesion ($r_{ ext{iso}}^{ ext{deliv}}, r_{ ext{LCC}}^{ ext{deliv}}, r_{ ext{conv}}^{ ext{deliv}}$) strictly over the induced deliverable subgraph $\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}]$. Normalizing metric denominators strictly to deliverable node cardinality $N{ ext{deliv}} = |\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}|$ isolates the substantive topology of the candidate deliverable, preventing supervisory dialogue volume and authorial reflection text from contaminating deliverable argument cohesion. * Intrinsic Isolated Claims vs. Threshold Calibration: Inducing $\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}]$ separates non-deliverable dialogue noise from the author's substantive argument, exposing the true structural drivers of residual claim isolation: sliding-window horizon truncation ($\Delta_{\max} \le 20$ atoms across distant chapters; mitigated by the Bounded Structural Hub & Frontier Header protocol, $K_{ ext{hub}}^{\max} = 8$, Equations 12b–12d) and standalone introductory scoping axioms ($\mathcal{V}{ ext{scoping}}$). Calibrating the Level 3 tolerance ceiling to $r^{\max}{L3} = 0.30$ accommodates legitimate foundational scoping context and attention horizon bounds on substantive merit, while empirical case-specific node reductions are analyzed in Section 8.3. * Exogenous Boundary Axiom: Cross-document dependencies ($X_{ ext{dialogue}} \xrightarrow{\mathbf{W}} Y_{ ext{deliverable}}$) linking supervisory dialogue directives to deliverable assertions are preserved: when inducing $\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}]$, $X{ ext{dialogue}}$ is treated as an exogenous boundary axiom ($\mathcal{V}{ ext{axiom}}$). Deliverable node $Y$ receives a valid incoming warrant ($ ext{InDegree}{ ext{cross}}(Y) > 0$), meaning $Y$ receives incoming evidential support and is not classified as an isolated claim, while $X$ is not included in $\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}$ nor counted in the deliverable denominator $N{ ext{deliv}}$, cleanly preventing conversational dialogue volume from deflating deliverable argument cohesion. * 0-Token Cross-Document Steering Coupling Ratio ($\kappa_{ ext{steer}}$): Concurrently, the engine evaluates human–AI collaboration through an orthogonal 0-token metric: $$\kappa_{ ext{steer}} = egin{cases} 0.0, & | ext{Root}(\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}])| = 0 \ rac{|{ Y \in ext{Root}(\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}]) \mid \exists X \in \mathcal{V}{ ext{dialogue}}: X \xrightarrow{\mathbf{W}} Y }|}{| ext{Root}(\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{ ext{deliverable}}])|}, & | ext{Root}(\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}_{ ext{deliverable}}])| > 0 \end{cases} ag{13b}$$ measuring the fraction of the candidate deliverable's foundational root claims that are explicitly anchored by upstream supervisory human dialogue directives.

docs.title: 5. Two-Factor Orthogonal Matrix Scoring and Asymmetric Falsification
5.1. BARS Criteria Weighting and Division-by-Zero Protection
docs.text:
Evaluation matrices implement Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS) distributed across five hierarchical tiers $l \in {1, \dots, 5}$ with natural weight function $w(l) = l$. Across the evaluated rubric matrices, every pre-compiled criterion $a_i \in \mathcal{A}_{\text{rubric}}$ ($N = 110$) resolves to a discrete status $\omega(a_i) \in { \text{PASSED}, \text{FAILED}, \text{DLQ} }$ through the formal piecewise transfer function:

$$\omega(a_i) = \begin{cases} \text{DLQ}, & \text{if processing exception } \xi_i = 1 \ \text{PASSED}, & \text{if } \xi_i = 0 \;\land\; [(\pi_i = +1 \;\land\; \lambda_i = 1 \;\land\; \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1) \;\lor\; (\pi_i = -1 \;\land\; \neg(\lambda_i = 1 \;\land\; \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1))] \ \text{FAILED}, & \text{if } \xi_i = 0 \;\land\; [(\pi_i = +1 \;\land\; (\lambda_i = 0 \;\lor\; \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 0)) \;\lor\; (\pi_i = -1 \;\land\; \lambda_i = 1 \;\land\; \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1)] \end{cases} \tag{14}$$

where $\xi_i \in {0, 1}$ indicates unresolvable processing exceptions (routing to Dead-Letter Queue). Equation (14) formalizes the asymmetric epistemic polarity of the rubric: for positive capability criteria ($\pi_i = +1$), discovering verified physical citation evidence ($\lambda_i = 1$) that semantically satisfies the rubric criteria under parallel Best-of-3 ensemble consensus ($\tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1$) yields $\omega(a_i) = \text{PASSED}$, incrementing achieved tier hits $h_l$ in Equation (15). If the citation fails physical verification ($\lambda_i = 0$) or the model's reasoning concludes that the cited evidence falls short of the strict rubric threshold ($\tau_{\text{val}, i} = 0$), the atom resolves to $\text{FAILED}$. Conversely, for negative anti-pattern criteria ($\pi_i = -1$), finding no verified violation citation ($\neg(\lambda_i = 1 \land \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1)$) confirms clean performance ($\omega(a_i) = \text{PASSED}$, accruing zero capability points), whereas verifying both physical evidence and semantic confirmation of an anti-pattern ($\lambda_i = 1 \land \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1$) confirms a violation ($\omega(a_i) = \text{FAILED}$, registering a penalty deduction $p_k$ in Equation 17).

For positive capability atoms ($\pi_i = +1$), achieved points $A$ and effective maximum points $M$ are computed over all tiers up to the matrix's maximum scale tier $L_{\max}^{(m)}$ ($L_{\max}^{(m)} = 5$ for standard BARS rubrics; $L_{\max}^{(m)} = 6$ for the six-tier Bloom cognitive taxonomy $\mathcal{M}_{\text{Bloom}}$):

$$A = \sum_{l=1}^{L_{\max}^{(m)}} l \cdot h_l, \quad M = \sum_{l=1}^{L_{\max}^{(m)}} l \cdot (t_l - d_l) \tag{15}$$

where $h_l$ is passed hits, $t_l$ is total criteria count, and $d_l$ is DLQ exceptions at tier $l$. The weighted linear ratio $\rho$ is safeguarded against division-by-zero singularities:

$$\rho = \begin{cases} \frac{A}{M}, & M > 0 \ 0.0, & M \le 0 \end{cases} \tag{16}$$

docs.title: 5.2. Asymmetric Popperian Falsification Multiplier
docs.text:
Negative anti-pattern atoms ($\pi_i = -1$) act as non-additive gatekeeping falsifiers. If an anti-pattern violation is confirmed ($\omega(a_i) = \text{FAILED}$ relative to clean performance), a penalty deduction $p_k \in (0, 1)$ is registered. The composite multiplier is formed multiplicatively over the set of confirmed violations:

$$\Pi_{\text{penalty}} = \begin{cases} \max\left( 1 - P_{\max}, \; \prod_{k=1}^{K_{\text{pen}}} (1 - p_k) \right), & K_{\text{pen}} > 0 \ 1.0, & K_{\text{pen}} = 0 \end{cases} \tag{17}$$

where $K_{\text{pen}}$ is the count of confirmed anti-pattern violations and $P_{\max} = 0.40$ is the hard-coded ceiling capping total cumulative deductions at $40\%$. This $P_{\max} = 0.40$ ceiling is intentionally coupled with Kahn wave precondition short-circuiting (Section 4.2, Guarantee 3b): non-fatal cognitive anti-patterns ($\pi_i = -1$) are bounded multiplicatively ($\Pi_{\text{penalty}} \ge 0.60$) to preserve Lipschitz score stability, whereas non-negotiable regulatory or domain prerequisites are encoded as Level 1 baseline preconditions whose failure deterministically clamps dependent upper-tier criteria ($L_2 \dots L_5$) to an unfulfilled state ($\text{BLOCKED}$ or $\text{N/A}$), restricting the positive capability ratio $\rho$ directly.

docs.title: 5.3. Continuous Piecewise Power-Curve Damping
docs.text:
Within each cell, raw fulfillment ratios are modulated by a continuous, piecewise-linear strictness exponent $\gamma(\zeta_{\text{score}})$ parameterized by the evaluative scoring strictness setting $\zeta_{\text{score}} \in [0, 100]$ (which operates orthogonally to the lexical verification strictness parameter $\zeta_{\text{lex}} \in [0, 100]$ defined in Section 4.1.1):

$$\gamma(\zeta_{\text{score}}) = \begin{cases} 1.00, & \zeta_{\text{score}} \le 0 \ 1.00 + \left(\frac{\zeta_{\text{score}}}{50}\right) \cdot 0.25, & 0 < \zeta_{\text{score}} \le 50 \ 1.25 + \left(\frac{\zeta_{\text{score}} - 50}{35}\right) \cdot 0.45, & 50 < \zeta_{\text{score}} \le 85 \ 1.70 + \left(\frac{\zeta_{\text{score}} - 85}{15}\right) \cdot 0.50, & 85 < \zeta_{\text{score}} \le 100 \ 2.20, & \zeta_{\text{score}} > 100 \end{cases} \tag{18}$$

The final mapped score across the range $[S_{\min}, S_{\max}]$ is calculated as:

$$\text{Score}(\rho; \zeta_{\text{score}}) = \begin{cases} S_{\min} + \left( \rho^{\gamma(\zeta_{\text{score}})} \cdot \Pi_{\text{penalty}} \right) \cdot (S_{\max} - S_{\min}), & M > 0 \ S_{\min}, & M \le 0 \end{cases} \tag{19}$$

Mathematical Property 1 (Score Monotonicity and Lipschitz Stability): Continuous power-curve damping is an architectural design choice formulated to eliminate the "cliff-edge failure" characteristic of discrete zero-trust gates (where a single missing token triggers a discontinuous score collapse). From an analytical standpoint, the scoring function exhibits two key mathematical properties for any calibrated exponent $\gamma \ge 1.0$ and penalty multiplier $\Pi_{\text{penalty}} \in (0, 1]$: 1. Monotonicity: $\frac{\partial \text{Score}}{\partial \rho} = \gamma \rho^{\gamma - 1} \Pi_{\text{penalty}} (S_{\max} - S_{\min}) \ge 0$ everywhere on $[0, 1]$. Validating an additional capability atom monotonically improves or maintains total score. 2. Lipschitz Stability: Because $\frac{\partial^2 \text{Score}}{\partial \rho^2} \ge 0$, the maximum rate of change is attained at the upper boundary $\rho = 1$, yielding the optimal Lipschitz constant $K_L = \gamma \Pi_{\text{penalty}} (S_{\max} - S_{\min})$. By the Mean Value Theorem, $|\text{Score}(\rho_1) - \text{Score}(\rho_2)| \le K_L |\rho_1 - \rho_2|$, ensuring that bounded evidence noise cannot trigger unbounded diagnostic volatility.

  A = ∑ l · h_l              Π_penalty = ∏(1 - p_k)

docs.title: 5.4. Multi-Matrix Orthogonal Scoring Space, Polarity Mechanics, and Two-Tier Governance
docs.text: While Equations (14)–(19) formulate the scoring kernel for an individual Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) matrix, Quorum's neurosymbolic evaluation engine is not bounded by a single evaluative lens. The platform implements a Holistic Multi-Matrix Audit, wherein an arbitrary set of process-, structural-, and domain-specific matrices are scheduled concurrently within the cognitive graph ($\mathcal{G}_{\text{DAG}}$) under Zero-Code Domain Extensibility.

docs.title: 5.4.1. Two-Tier Scoring Hierarchy: Sovereign Kernel vs. Macro Governance
docs.text:
To preserve mathematical purity and prevent cross-phase architectural pollution, Quorum enforces a strict separation of concerns through a two-tier scoring hierarchy:

  1. Tier A: Sovereign Intra-Matrix Scoring Kernel: Equation (19) represents the sovereign intra-matrix scoring kernel. It computes a pure mathematical evaluation bounded strictly by the evaluated matrix prompt block's scale extrema $[S_{\min}, S_{\max}]$. The kernel operates exclusively on atomic criteria within that single matrix, computing weighted capability ratio $\rho$ and intra-matrix anti-pattern falsification multiplier $\Pi_{\text{penalty}}$ under continuous strictness damping $\gamma(\zeta)$. The kernel returns an immutable scoring record containing the normalized score, per-level breakdown, and structured explainable AI (XAI) audit trace. The intra-matrix kernel does not access external workflow state, execute secondary data lookups, or apply macro-level penalties.

  2. Tier B: Macro-Workflow Governance and Multi-Matrix Aggregation: Multi-matrix scoring consolidation and workflow-level penalty governance are decoupled into the post-execution governance pipeline:

  3. Commensurate Normalization: Each evaluated matrix block projects its raw score into a normalized $[0.0, 100.0]$ scale via linear min-max projection: $$\text{Normalized_Score}m = \left( \frac{S_m - S{\min}^{(m)}}{S_{\max}^{(m)} - S_{\min}^{(m)}} \right) \times 100.0$$
  4. Macro-Workflow Penalty Governance: The consolidated global score is calculated as the unweighted arithmetic mean of normalized matrix scores across all $D$ evaluated matrices, subjected to workflow-level deduction penalties: $$\text{average_score} = \frac{1}{D} \sum_{d=1}^D \text{Normalized_Score}d \tag{20}$$ $$\text{effective_penalty} = \min(\text{total_penalty}, P{\max})$$ $$\text{global_score} = \text{round}\left( \max(0.0, \; \text{average_score} \times (1.0 - \text{effective_penalty})), \; 1 \right)$$ where $P_{\max} = 0.40$ (40% maximum cumulative workflow deduction). Workflow penalties encompass three sovereign modalities: security prompt injection penalty ($P_{\text{security}}$), post-hoc rationalization penalty ($P_{\text{post_hoc}}$), and behavioral passivity penalty ($P_{\text{passivity}}$).
  5. Observer Protocol for Behavioral Passivity: Behavioral passivity detection is decoupled from intra-matrix scoring math. The passivity observer inspects aggregated matrix outputs. If an evaluation resolves to its mathematical floor ($S_{\min}$) with zero positive capability assertions verified above baseline, the protocol triggers a passivity flag. When observed, the macro-governance layer applies the configured passivity penalty ($P_{\text{passivity}}$) at Tier B aggregation.

docs.title: 5.4.2. Holistic Multi-Matrix Audit in Orthogonal Vector Space ($\mathbf{\Psi}$)
docs.text:
Restricting AI evaluation to a single diagnostic dimension produces structural blind spots. If auditing is confined strictly to the final artifact ($\sigma_i = \text{ASSISTANT}$), fluent autoregressive prose can achieve high marks even if the human operator acted as a completely passive passenger. Conversely, analyzing only conversational interaction ($\sigma_i = \text{USER}$) risks an Illusion of Control, wherein concise, confident prompting yields an epistemically hollow, Rung 1 deliverable.

Quorum formalizes holistic evaluation as a $D$-dimensional orthogonal matrix vector $\mathcal{M} = (\mathcal{M}_1, \mathcal{M}_2, \dots, \mathcal{M}_D)$, where each matrix $\mathcal{M}_d$ interrogates discourse $\mathcal{D}$ from a distinct epistemic stance anchored to an XML-isolated speaker capsule ($\sigma_i \in {\text{USER}, \text{ASSISTANT}}$):

$$\mathbf{\Psi}(\mathcal{D}; \zeta) = \begin{bmatrix} \text{Score}{\mathcal{M}_1}\left(\rho_1, \Pi{\text{penalty}}^{(1)}; \zeta\right) \ \text{Score}{\mathcal{M}_2}\left(\rho_2, \Pi{\text{penalty}}^{(2)}; \zeta\right) \ \vdots \ \text{Score}{\mathcal{M}_D}\left(\rho_D, \Pi{\text{penalty}}^{(D)}; \zeta\right) \end{bmatrix} \in \prod_{d=1}^D \left[ S_{\min}^{(d)}, S_{\max}^{(d)} \right] \tag{21}$$

In a comprehensive audit workflow, execution graph $\mathcal{G}_{\text{DAG}}$ partitions evaluation across three cross-validating epistemic layers executed concurrently via asynchronous coroutines within the same Kahn topological wave $\mathcal{W}_j$:

  1. Human Agency & Collaboration Matrix ($\mathcal{M}_{\text{HACM}}, \sigma_i = \text{USER}$): Targets the human provenance capsule $\mathcal{K}_{\text{user}}$, evaluating cognitive steering responsibility, boundary definition, adversarial challenging of AI drafts, and iterative refinement.
  2. Epistemic & Causal Architecture Matrix ($\mathcal{M}_{\text{Causal}}, \sigma_i \in {\text{USER}, \text{ASSISTANT}}$): Evaluates the macro-topological proposition graph $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{deps}})$ mined across the multi-document submission payload ($\mathcal{D}{\text{dialogue}} \circ \mathcal{D}{\text{deliverable}} \circ \mathcal{D}{\text{reflection}}$). Under the Capsule-Partitioned Subgraph Invariant (Section 4.2.1), deliverable argument coherence, reachability ($r_{\text{LCC}}^{\text{deliv}}$), isolated claim ratio ($r_{\text{iso}}^{\text{deliv}}$), and multi-premise convergence ($r_{\text{conv}}^{\text{deliv}}$) are evaluated over the induced deliverable subgraph $\mathcal{G}[\mathcal{V}{\text{deliverable}}]$ (with supervisory dialogue inputs treated as exogenous boundary axioms $\mathcal{V}{\text{axiom}}$), paired with the orthogonal Cross-Capsule Steering Coupling Ratio ($\kappa_{\text{steer}}$), all computed in 0 tokens under the Cumulative Guttman Invariant (paired with substantive Toulmin warrant criteria in $\mathcal{M}{\text{Toulmin}}$ which strictly isolate candidate model drafts in $\mathcal{K}{\text{draft}}$ with $\sigma_i = \text{ASSISTANT}$, and interactive ATMS counterfactual stress testing).
  3. Domain Substance Matrix ($\mathcal{M}_{\text{Domain}}, \sigma_i \in {\text{USER}, \text{ASSISTANT}}$): Evaluates specialized task constraints—spanning legal claim management, strategic foresight, and statutory compliance—using the identical mathematical scoring kernel.

While the macro-governance layer computes a commensurate scalar average for high-level governance, the declarative presentation pipeline preserves vector $\mathbf{\Psi}(\mathcal{D}; \zeta)$ intact, exposing the Agency-to-Outcome Divergence:

$$\Delta_{\text{agency-outcome}} = \left\vert{} \hat{S}(\mathcal{M}{\text{HACM}}) - \hat{S}(\mathcal{M}{\text{outcome}}) \right\vert{} \tag{22}$$

where $\hat{S}(\cdot) \in [0, 1]$ represents the normalized matrix score. In multi-matrix audit workflows where $D > 2$ matrices are active, the substantive outcome term $\hat{S}(\mathcal{M}_{\text{outcome}})$ is formalized as the unweighted arithmetic mean across all active non-agency substantive/structural matrices:

$$\hat{S}(\mathcal{M}{\text{outcome}}) = \frac{1}{D - 1} \sum{d \neq \text{HACM}} \hat{S}(\mathcal{M}_d)$$

(specifically averaging the substantive deliverable evaluation matrices $\mathcal{M}{\text{Toulmin}}, \mathcal{M}{\text{Causal}}, \mathcal{M}{\text{Transp}}, \text{ and } \mathcal{M}{\text{Bloom}}$ in the empirical benchmark). In workflows configured with a dedicated Studio presentation profile, $\hat{S}(\mathcal{M}{\text{outcome}})$ optionally evaluates targeted pairwise divergence against a specific designated target block $\hat{S}(\mathcal{M}{\text{target}})$ (specifically a designated reference matrix block $\hat{S}(\mathcal{M}{\text{target}})$). An elevated divergence $\Delta{\text{agency-outcome}}$ diagnoses either uncritical automation complacency (high outcome without human agency) or ineffective steering (active dialogue failing to materialize as structural deliverable quality).

docs.title: 5.4.3. Matrix-Specific Polarity Mechanics and Classical Theoretical Grounding
docs.text:
Within every matrix $\mathcal{M}_d$, positive capability assertions ($\pi_i = +1$) and negative anti-pattern falsifiers ($\pi_i = -1$) enforce a two-sided lexical proof burden grounded in contrastive pair enforcement (acceptable demonstration vs. rejected distractor):

  1. Positive Capability Assertions ($\pi_i = +1$):
  2. Epistemic Role: Measures constructive cognitive and professional competence across hierarchical BARS levels $l \in {1, \dots, 5}$.
  3. Evidentiary Proof Burden: The default state is unproven ($h_l = 0$). An assertion is accepted ($\omega(a_i) = \text{PASSED}$) only if the sensor extracts an exact verbatim quote $\mathcal{C}_i$ from target speaker $\sigma_i$ matching the positive anchor, avoiding the negative distractor, and passing all five deterministic physical validation gates ($\lambda_i = 1$).

  4. Mathematical Impact: Accrues additively into weighted capability ratio $\rho = A / M$ (Equations 15–16) and is softened via piecewise power-curve damping $\rho^{\gamma(\zeta)}$ (Equation 18).

  5. Negative Anti-Pattern Assertions ($\pi_i = -1$, Inverse Polarity):

  6. Epistemic Role: Acts as a Popperian gatekeeper, actively searching for cognitive shortcuts, argumentation fallacies, uncritical delegation, and superficial fluency.
  7. Evidentiary Proof Burden (Defense Against Hallucinated Penalties): The default state is clean performance ($\Pi_{\text{penalty}} = 1.0$). The LLM cannot penalize by stochastic estimation: deduction $p_k \in (0, 1)$ triggers only if the sensor extracts an exact verbatim citation passing all five physical validation gates ($\lambda_i = 1$) proving the violation occurred. If lexical grounding fails ($\lambda_i = 0$), the penalty is dropped.
  8. Mathematical Impact & Decoupled Inverse Badging: Verified anti-patterns deduct from the matrix score multiplicatively via $\Pi_{\text{penalty}} = \max(1 - P_{\max}, \prod_{k=1}^{K_{\text{pen}}} (1 - p_k))$ (Equation 17), capped at $P_{\max} = 0.40$. Crucially, anti-pattern assertions do not award positive capability points ($A = 0$ pts). In the presentation and tabular export tiers, passing an anti-pattern displays as clean performance ($0\text{ pts}$, unviolated) rather than misleadingly awarding positive score points (which would falsely conflate the mere absence of error with positive competence), while verified violations are badged distinctly with dedicated numeric indicators.
  9. Atomic Export Invariant & Empirical Hit Distribution: Tabular exports project evaluated atoms $1:1$ without synthetic record aggregation. Matrix summary tables format the empirical hit distribution ($k/N$ ratio) per BARS tier, while dynamic causal graph propositions are mapped transparently under an explicit causal reasoning module.

In the system evaluation design, assertions are anchored to classical theoretical literature across two mutually exclusive rubric tracks:

docs.title: 5.4.4. Design-Time Human Curation and Empirical Scope Boundaries
docs.text:
The rigorous mapping above demonstrates why Quorum matrices are compiled through Design-Time Human Curation rather than unconstrained runtime LLM generation:

  1. Bounding Semantic Drift and the Entailment Gap: As established in Section 2.1, general semantic entailment ($\mathcal{C}_i \models \tau_i$) over unrestricted text is fundamentally undecidable by purely computational means (Rice's Theorem). Pre-compiling closed BARS rubrics with explicit contrastive pairs converts open-ended generation into a bounded verification task, constraining the hypothesis space. Residual semantic ambiguity is systematically bounded by role-asymmetric Popperian falsification and isolated via causal graph reachability pruning (see Section 2.1).
  2. Psychometric Invariance and Regulatory Auditability: Because evaluation matrices exist as versioned, immutable schema entities, every execution is scored against an identical Lipschitz-stable benchmark (Equation 19), guaranteeing longitudinal repeatability across evaluation cohorts.
  3. Classical Theories as Cognitive Compilers: Domain architects need not invent evaluative dimensions ad-hoc in the evaluation design interface. Sheridan–Verplank, Toulmin, Pearl, Bloom / Anderson–Krathwohl, Popper, and Kahneman provide an established five-tier competence continuum ($\pi_i = +1$) and a canonical error taxonomy ($\pi_i = -1$). Domain experts map specialized terminology directly into these established structures, after which automated schema verification suites guarantee lexical anchorability and prevent overfitting.
