Empirical Scope Boundary and Prospective Cross-Domain Validation: While the empirical evaluation in Section 8 examines a five-matrix audit configuration across two real-world human–AI interaction cases (the Remote Work policy reform case and the Strategic Foresight / Sitra megatrends case), Quorum's data-driven matrix engine is architecturally domain-agnostic. In ongoing research and prospective validation campaigns, this multi-matrix space ($\mathbf{\Psi}$) is systematically applied to enterprise contract review, regulatory compliance audits, and multi-agent software engineering workflows across diverse organizational cohorts and foundation model families.

docs.title: 6. Architectural Principles and Verified Mathematical Properties
docs.text: Epistemic Calibration and System Scope: To preserve strict scientific integrity and avoid theoretical inflation, we explicitly partition the formal framework into two practical categories: 1. Architectural Principles: Structural design invariants inherited from established computer science (referential transparency, pure computational pipelines, and discrete topological DAG scheduling) that govern deterministic asynchronous orchestration. 2. Mathematically Verified System Properties: Analytical properties of our verification and scoring pipelines (lexical error suppression bounds, Lipschitz score stability, and topological reachability) that guarantee numerical and epistemic predictability.

docs.title: Architectural Principle 1: Confluent Neurosymbolic Wave Scheduling
docs.text:
Architectural Principle 1 (Wave Confluence under Kahn Ordering and Pure Computations). Let $\mathcal{G}{\text{DAG}} = (\mathcal{V}{\text{cog}}, \mathcal{E}{\text{dep}})$ be a finite directed acyclic graph partitioned into $J$ disjoint topological waves $\mathcal{W}_0, \mathcal{W}_1, \dots, \mathcal{W}{J-1}$ via Kahn's partial ordering (Kahn, 1962). Let each node operator $\Phi_v: \prod_{u \in \text{Parents}(v)} \mathcal{O}u \times \mathcal{S}{\text{global}} \to \mathcal{O}v$ be a pure compute function executing over immutable, validated typed records with zero shared memory side-effects. By the referential transparency of pure functions over acyclic directed graphs and Kahn partial ordering (establishing wave confluence analogously to the Church–Rosser theorem for confluent evaluation orders; Church & Rosser, 1936; and Kahn process networks; Kahn, 1974), any arbitrary asynchronous resolution order or coroutine scheduling permutation $\varpi \in \text{Perm}(\mathcal{W}_j)$ within concurrent execution groups converges deterministically to the identical unique wave state snapshot $\mathcal{O}{\mathcal{W}_j}$, and the global system pipeline terminates at an invariant fixed-point state $\mathcal{S}^ = (\Phi_{\mathcal{W}{J-1}} \circ \dots \circ \Phi{\mathcal{W}_0})(\mathcal{S}_0)$.*

Architectural Context & Contribution: Confluence of pure functions over immutable inputs in acyclic topologies is a classic foundational result in theoretical computer science (Church & Rosser, 1936; Kahn, 1974). We do not claim wave confluence as a novel mathematical discovery. Rather, Quorum's real-world contribution is the strict architectural enforcement of referential transparency within a distributed LLM runtime: 1. Operators communicate exclusively via immutable, strongly typed record contracts. 2. Cognitive engines adhere to the Pure Compute Engine Law (100% computational pipelines with zero shared locks, event listeners, or mutable globals). 3. Concurrency throttling is cleanly decoupled into dynamic HTTP semaphore pools, preventing runtime deadlocks while guaranteeing bit-level deterministic state reproduction across re-executions. 4. State transitions across topological waves are persisted as an immutable event-sourced stream ($e_t \in \mathcal{E}{\text{trace}}$). The global context state $\mathcal{S}_t$ is reconstituted purely through deterministic event projection $\mathcal{S}{t+1} = \text{Project}(\mathcal{S}_t, e_t)$, completely eliminating in-place mutation of global state, enforcing typed record structures, and guaranteeing deterministic execution replay and verifiable audit trails under regulatory transparency standards (specifically EU AI Act Articles 12–15).

docs.title: Architectural Property 1: Decoupled Epistemic Error Suppression via Physical Grounding and Role Asymmetry
docs.text:
Property 1 (Decoupled Epistemic Error Suppression and Score Inflation Bounds). Let an ensemble of $M$ frontier LLM evaluators—whether drawn from parallel sampling of a single model distribution ($ ar{ ho}{ ext{intra}} \approx 1$) or a heterogeneous multi-model committee ($ ar{ ho}{ ext{inter}} \ge ho_{\min} > 0$) due to shared pretraining corpora (Common Crawl, Wikipedia)—exhibit non-zero pairwise error correlation $ ext{Cov}(X_i, X_j) = ho_{ij} > 0$. While democratic majority voting hits an asymptotic error floor governed by effective sample size $M_{ ext{eff}} \le 1/ ar{ ho}$, Quorum decouples epistemic error suppression into two orthogonal frontiers: deterministic Physical Lexical Grounding ($\lambda \in {0, 1}$) at the atom level, and Role-Asymmetric Popperian Falsification ($\pi = -1$) at the matrix level. The atom-level false acceptance probability on a capability claim $a_i \in \mathcal{A}_{ ext{rubric}}$ ($\pi_i = +1$) is strictly bounded by the sum of physical substring collision tolerances and stochastic semantic misattribution rates:

$$P( ext{Atom False Accept}i) \le P(H{ ext{fab}}) \cdot \epsilon_{ ext{lexical}} + P(H_{ ext{mis}}) \cdot eta_{ ext{sem}} \approx P(H_{ ext{mis}}) \cdot eta_{ ext{sem}} ag{23}$$

where $H_{ ext{fab}}$ denotes extrinsic citation fabrication ($\mathcal{C}i otin \mathcal{D}$), $H{ ext{mis}}$ denotes intrinsic semantic misattribution ($\mathcal{C}i \in \mathcal{D} \land \mathcal{C}_i ot\models au_i$), $\epsilon{ ext{lexical}} o 0$ is the combinatorial substring collision rate, and $ eta_{ ext{sem}} = P( ext{Gate 4 Passes} \land ext{Bo3 Consensus} \mid H_{ ext{mis}})$ is the stochastic Type II miss rate of the joint reasoning trace triangulation and ensemble voting gate. Furthermore, system-level score inflation resulting from residual semantic drift is bounded multiplicatively on the deterministic plug-in score evaluated at the expected capability ratio $ ext{Score}(\mathbb{E}[ ho]; \zeta)$ and in stochastic score expectation $\mathbb{E}[ ext{Score}( ho; \zeta)]$ by the Popperian anti-pattern penalty multiplier $\Pi_{ ext{penalty}}$:

$$ ext{Score}(\mathbb{E}[ ho]; \zeta) \le S_{\min} + \left( \left( ho_{ ext{clean}} + ho_{ ext{mis}} \cdot eta_{ ext{sem}} ight)^{\gamma(\zeta)} \cdot \Pi_{ ext{penalty}} ight) \cdot (S_{\max} - S_{\min}) ag{24a}$$

$$\mathbb{E}[ ext{Score}( ho; \zeta)] \le ext{Score}(\mathbb{E}[ ho]; \zeta) + rac{1}{2}\gamma(\gamma - 1)\mu_ ho^{\gamma - 2} ext{Var}( ho) \cdot \Pi_{ ext{penalty}} (S_{\max} - S_{\min}) + \mathcal{O}\left(\mathbb{E}[( ho - \mu_ ho)^3] ight) ag{24b}$$

Analytical Verification & Derivation:

  1. Failure of Democratic Consensus under Correlated Priors (Epistemic Bias vs. Aleatoric Noise): Let $X_1, \dots, X_M \in {0, 1}$ be binary error indicators for model evaluators on a deceptive prompt. Due to overlapping pretraining distributions and shared inductive biases, the average pairwise correlation across models is strictly non-zero: $ ar{ ho} \ge ho_{\min} > 0$. The effective sample size of democratic ensembling is bounded asymptotically:

$$M_{ ext{eff}} = rac{M}{1 + (M-1) ar{ ho}} \implies \lim_{M o \infty} M_{ ext{eff}} = rac{1}{ ar{ ho}} < \infty ag{25}$$

If the prompt triggers a shared pretraining attractor where individual error probability $p > 0.5$, democratic voting inverts: $P( ext{Consensus Error}) o 1$ as $M o \infty$. Thus, model ensembling alone cannot guarantee epistemic reliability.

The Aleatoric vs. Epistemic Ensembling Duality: We explicitly distinguish between Aleatoric Decoding Noise (stochastic token sampling jitter around decision thresholds under non-zero temperature, where $ ho_{ ext{aleatoric}} < 1$) and Epistemic Model Bias (systematic conceptual hallucinations and pretraining blindspots, where $ ar{ ho}{ ext{epistemic}} o 1$). While drawing multiple parallel samples from the same foundation model (single-model Best-of-3) successfully dampens aleatoric decoding variance, it exhibits $ ar{ ho}{ ext{intra}} \approx 1$ for systematic epistemic errors: if a model suffers from an inherent semantic blindspot ($p > 0.5$), voting repeatedly from the same model simply solidifies the error. For this fundamental reason, Quorum never relies on LLM voting or generative self-consensus to guarantee epistemic truth. Rather, epistemic integrity is guaranteed by non-generative, orthogonal verification: the deterministic physical lexical firewall ($\lambda \in {0, 1}$), role-asymmetric Popperian polarity ($\pi = -1$), and topological ATMS graph surgery (Algorithm 1). This theoretical bound is empirically corroborated in Ablation Configuration 2 (Section 8.5, Table 7), where disabling the lexical firewall under Best-of-3 voting permits a 20.7% chimera acceptance rate.

  1. Two-Tier Error Decomposition (Orthogonal Epistemic Dimensions): An erroneous system acceptance occurs when a proposition $ au_i$ is marked as valid despite lacking true evidentiary support in document $\mathcal{D}$. This error decomposes into two mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive hypotheses:
  2. Extrinsic Citation Fabrication ($H_{ ext{fab}}$): The extractor generates an invalid or spliced citation $\mathcal{C}_i otin \mathcal{D}$ (Type I Hallucination / Chimera quote).
  3. Intrinsic Semantic Misattribution ($H_{ ext{mis}}$): The extractor provides a verbatim authentic quote $\mathcal{C}_i \in \mathcal{D}$ from the authorized speaker, but the quote does not semantically entail proposition $ au_i$ ($\mathcal{C}_i ot\models au_i$; Type II Non-Entailment).

By the Law of Total Probability:

$$P( ext{Atom False Accept}i) = P(H{ ext{fab}}) \cdot P( ext{Accept} \mid H_{ ext{fab}}) + P(H_{ ext{mis}}) \cdot P( ext{Accept} \mid H_{ ext{mis}}) ag{26}$$

  1. Deterministic Physical Lexical Firewall ($\lambda \in {0, 1}$): Regardless of LLM consensus or inter-model correlation $ ar{ ho}$, every extracted claim must satisfy the strict lexical grounding predicate:

$$\lambda_i = \mathbb{I}\left( ext{find}( ext{Norm}(\mathcal{C}_i), ext{Norm}(\mathcal{D})) eq -1 ight) \in {0, 1} ag{27}$$

where $\mathcal{C}i$ is the exact textual citation and $\mathcal{D}$ is the raw immutable source document evaluated through the five-gate deterministic verification cascade. For fabricated citations ($H{ ext{fab}}$), acceptance requires a random character collision across finite document length $|\mathcal{D}|$, yielding:

$$P( ext{Accept} \mid H_{ ext{fab}}) = P(\lambda_i = 1 \mid H_{ ext{fab}}) \le \epsilon_{ ext{lexical}} \approx |\mathcal{D}| \cdot \left( rac{1}{|\Sigma|} ight)^L o 0$$

where $|\Sigma|$ is the alphabet size and $L$ is the minimum entropy string length ($L \ge 10$). Hence, physical fabrication is deterministically eradicated by physical string verification.

Conversely, for semantic misattributions ($H_{ ext{mis}}$), the citation physically exists in the text ($\mathcal{C}_i \in \mathcal{D}$). Consequently, the deterministic string matcher unconditionally confirms physical existence:

$$P(\lambda_i = 1 \mid H_{ ext{mis}}) = 1.0$$

The lexical firewall proves physical provenance, but remains mathematically agnostic to semantic entailment.

  1. Atom-Level Semantic Defense vs. Matrix-Level Popperian Multiplier: To prevent semantic misattributions ($H_{ ext{mis}}$) from corrupting evaluation, Quorum enforces defense across two distinct architectural tiers:
  2. Atom-Level Semantic Verification ($ eta_{ ext{sem}}$): At the individual criterion level $a_i$ ($\pi_i = +1$), an authentic quotation $\mathcal{C}i \in \mathcal{D}$ that fails to semantically entail $ au_i$ is defended by: (i) Gate 4 Reasoning Trace Triangulation (asserting physical anchor existence, non-empty grounding, and absence of internal logical contradictions), (ii) explicit contrastive distractor rubrics (penalizing superficial mentions), and (iii) parallel Best-of-3 ensemble consensus voting ($k \ge 2$ of $3$). Formally: $$P( ext{Accept} \mid H{ ext{mis}}) = P(\lambda_i = 1 \mid H_{ ext{mis}}) \cdot P( ext{Gate 4} \land ext{Bo3 Passes} \mid H_{ ext{mis}}) = 1.0 \cdot eta_{ ext{sem}}$$ Substituting into Equation (26) yields the atom-level bound in Equation (23): $P( ext{Atom False Accept}i) \le P(H{ ext{fab}}) \cdot \epsilon_{ ext{lexical}} + P(H_{ ext{mis}}) \cdot eta_{ ext{sem}} \approx P(H_{ ext{mis}}) \cdot eta_{ ext{sem}}$.
  3. Matrix-Level Popperian Falsification ($\Pi_{ ext{penalty}}$): Negative anti-pattern criteria ($\pi_k = -1$) operate as non-additive matrix gatekeepers. They do not evaluate positive citations individually to flip $\omega(a_i)$, but rather search the document for global cognitive failure modes (specifically vacuous apologies, passive delegation, and jargon loading; Table 1). When verified ($\lambda_k = 1$), each anti-pattern applies a multiplicative deduction $p_k \in (0, 1)$ via $\Pi_{ ext{penalty}} = \max(1 - P_{\max}, \prod_{k=1}^{K_{ ext{pen}}} (1 - p_k))$ (Equation 17). Consequently, if an author achieves unearned capability points $ ho_{ ext{mis}}$ through superficial verbatim phrasing that slips past $ eta_{ ext{sem}}$, the presence of associated anti-patterns actively suppresses overall score inflation via Equation (24a), capping cumulative deductions at $P_{\max} = 40\%$.
  4. Jensen's Inequality, Convex Power Damping, and Expectation Bounds: In Section 5.3 (Mathematical Property 1), the damping transformation $g( ho) = ho^{\gamma(\zeta)}$ is proved to have a non-negative second derivative $ rac{\partial^2 g}{\partial ho^2} = \gamma(\gamma - 1) ho^{\gamma - 2} \ge 0$ on $ ho \in [0, 1]$ for all $\gamma(\zeta) \ge 1.0$, establishing that $g( ho)$ is convex (and strictly convex whenever $\zeta > 0 \implies \gamma(\zeta) > 1.0$). By Jensen's Inequality, for any random capability ratio $R \in [0, 1]$ with $\mathbb{E}[R] \le ho_{ ext{clean}} + ho_{ ext{mis}} eta_{ ext{sem}}$, the expectation satisfies $\mathbb{E}[g(R)] \ge g(\mathbb{E}[R])$. Consequently, substituting $\mathbb{E}[R]$ into $g(\cdot)$ bounds the deterministic plug-in score evaluated at the expected ratio, $ ext{Score}(\mathbb{E}[ ho]; \zeta)$ (Equation 24a). For the expectation of the stochastic score $\mathbb{E}[ ext{Score}( ho; \zeta)]$, the upper bound is formalized via the second-order Taylor expansion envelope established in Equation (24b), where $\mu_ ho = \mathbb{E}[ ho] \le ho_{ ext{clean}} + ho_{ ext{mis}} eta_{ ext{sem}}$. In Quorum's empirical production trials under Best-of-3 ensemble consensus, extraction variance is tightly suppressed ($ ext{Var}( ho) < 0.001$, mean Shannon entropy $ ar{H} \le 0.0455$), ensuring that the Jensen dispersion gap $ rac{1}{2}\gamma(\gamma-1)\mu_ ho^{\gamma-2} ext{Var}( ho)$ is negligible ($< 0.08\%$ score points) and that the deterministic plug-in bound and the stochastic expectation tightly coincide.

Theoretical Significance and Analytical Parameterization of $ eta_{ ext{sem}}$: Quorum rejects the naive fallacy of "deterministic semantic omniscience"—deterministic lexical matching cannot magically prove semantic entailment ($\mathcal{C}i \models au_i$). Rather, Quorum cleanly decouples the problem: (i) eliminating unanchored and fabricated evidence ($P \le \epsilon{ ext{lexical}} o 0$) via deterministic verification gates, while (ii) bounding residual semantic misattribution to the stochastic consensus error parameter $ eta_{ ext{sem}} \in [0, 1]$ and damping matrix score inflation via $\Pi_{ ext{penalty}}$. While unconstrained generation exhibits substantial error rates on adversarial benchmarks (Nie et al., 2020; Thorne et al., 2018), structured negative prompting over closed BARS rubrics suppresses the Type II miss rate $ eta_{ ext{sem}}$ through multi-turn reasoning trace triangulation and contrastive pair enforcement. Empirically, expert calibration bounds this parameter to a tight low-single-digit point estimate $\hat{ eta}{ ext{sem}} = 2.50\%$ (95% Wilson CI $[0.44\%, 12.88\%]$; see Section 8.5.1, Table 7b). For parametric sensitivity analysis in Equation (24a), evaluating score behavior across operational regimes $ eta{ ext{sem}} \in [0.01, 0.05]$ demonstrates that score inflation is bounded to $<2.1\%$ under baseline damping; furthermore, downstream consequence propagation is structurally contained via topological A-SCM reachability pruning (Algorithm 1).

docs.title: Architectural Property 2: Discrete ATMS Reachability and Cascade Fault Isolation
docs.text:
Architectural Property 2 (Topological Root-Cause Isolation and Dual Fault Attribution). Suppose an atomic proposition $X \in \mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}$ fails empirical verification ($s(X) = 0.0$) or its outgoing inferential warrant $\vec{\mathcal{W}}{XY}$ fails lexical grounding ($\lambda(\vec{\mathcal{W}}{XY}) = 0$), and $X$ is a necessary premise for a downstream proposition $Y$ ($(X, Y) \in \mathcal{E}{\text{causal}}$). Under the topological execution and ATMS diagnostic engine (Algorithm 1):

  1. If $X$ fails intrinsically ($s(X) = 0.0$) while its own upstream support is intact ($\text{BrokenSupport}(X, \mathcal{E}{\text{causal}}) = \emptyset$), $X$ is isolated in $\text{RC}{\text{node}}$ (Node Failure). Conversely, if $X$ is empirically valid ($s(X) > 0.0$) but the inferential bridge $(X, Y)$ lacks a lexically verified Toulmin warrant ($\lambda(\vec{\mathcal{W}}{XY}) = 0$), the fault is isolated in $\text{RC}{\text{edge}}$ (Warrant Grounding Failure) without penalizing node $X$.
  2. In live multi-criterion rubric DAGs, $Y$ is deterministically short-circuited to an unfulfilled status $s(Y) = \text{N/A}$ during Kahn wave execution, whereas in post-hoc ATMS argument mining over flat candidate documents, $Y$ is flagged as causally contested ($\text{Status}(Y) = \text{CONTESTED}$) in $\approx 0.19\text{ ms}$ with zero additional model token expenditure.
  3. Because $\text{BrokenSupport}(Y, \mathcal{E}{\text{causal}}) = {X} \neq \emptyset$, $Y$ is strictly excluded from $\text{RC}{\text{node}}$ ($\text{RC}_{\text{node}} \cap {Y} = \emptyset$), preventing compound double-counting of secondary downstream failures:

$$Y \notin \text{RC}{\text{node}}, \quad \text{and under live rubric short-circuiting:} \quad w_Y \cdot \tilde{s}(Y) = 0 \text{ (excluded from active cell denominator } W{r,c}\text{)} \tag{30}$$

  1. Boundary Remark (Intra-Instance Cascade Isolation vs. Baseline Scoring Invariance): Property 2 governs intra-instance structural soundness and cascade fault isolation conditional on an individual compiled DAG realization, rather than asserting cross-run micro-topological isomorphism ($\mathcal{G}_1 \simeq \mathcal{G}_2$; see Section 4.2 Guarantee 7 and Section 8.6 Point 5). Baseline scoring evaluates unperturbed macro-topology in 0 tokens (Pillar 1), while Property 2 proves that counterfactual stress-testing and failure isolation deterministically uncover root causes without second-order stochastic prompting, with inter-run stability guaranteed at the macro-invariant level ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$).

docs.title: 7. Full-Stack System Architecture and Error Suppression Pipeline
7.1. Layered System Architecture
docs.text:
The framework operationalizes its theoretical invariants across three integrated layers:

  1. Neurosymbolic Execution Engine: A formal computation engine managing asynchronous Kahn wave scheduling, two-pass epistemic atomization, topological poset evaluation, backward fault attribution, pure argument causal cohesion evaluation, and constrained synthesis. An abstraction layer unifies context management, prompt compilation, key-value cache isolation, and constrained decoding across diverse foundation model architectures (spanning Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, and DeepSeek).

  2. Declarative Projection Layer: To preserve presentation-invariance and eliminate client-side semantic inference, evaluated matrix vectors $\mathbf{\Psi}(\mathcal{D}; \zeta)$, causal multigraphs $\mathcal{G}_{\text{LAG}}$, and explainable AI variance diagnostics are structured into immutable declarative reporting representations.

  3. Interactive Analytical Interface: Provides real-time execution monitoring, dynamic rubric specification, formal report generation, and compliance auditing engineered in alignment with international regulatory transparency standards (specifically EU AI Act Articles 12–15).

docs.title: 7.2. Four-Stage Cascade Suppression Pipeline and Two-Tier Verification
docs.text:
Unlike standard unconstrained LLM pipelines where intermediate hallucinations cascade unchecked, Quorum forces state through a four-stage suppression barrier:

$$\mathcal{S}{\text{out}} = (\Phi{\text{synth}} \circ \Phi_{\text{score}} \circ \Phi_{\text{fals}} \circ \Phi_{\text{TDA}} \circ \Phi_{\text{ingress}})(\mathcal{S}_{\text{in}} + \xi) \tag{31}$$

where $\xi$ represents stochastic semantic noise.

            Raw Stochastic Prompt
                      |
                      v
        +-----------------------------------------------+
        | Barrier 1: Ingress Layer                      |
        | - Strips prompt injection                     |
        | - Indexes agency (σ_i)                        |
        +-----------------------+-----------------------+
                                |
                                v
        +-----------------------------------------------+
        | Barrier 2: TDA Grounding                      |
        | - Null hypothesis (λ = 0)                     |
        | - Drops hallucinations                        |
        +-----------------------+-----------------------+
                                |
                                v
        +-----------------------------------------------+
        | Barrier 3: Asymmetric Falsification & Bo3     |
        | - Asymmetric Malus (π = -1)                   |
        | - Single-Model Bo3 Ensemble                   |
        | - Multiplicative Penalty (Π_penalty)          |
        +-----------------------+-----------------------+
                                |
                                v
        +-----------------------------------------------+
        | Barrier 4: Aggregation & Lipschitz Damp       |
        | - Commensurate Normalization                  |
        | - Macro Scoring Governance (P_max = 0.40)     |
        | - Power curve damping (γ(0)=1.0, γ(50)=1.25)  |
        +-----------------------+-----------------------+
                                |
                                v
                    Deterministic Final State
  • Barrier 1 (Ingress Sanitization & Capsule Isolation, $\Phi_{\text{ingress}}$): Strips prompt injection payloads, applies Unicode Canonical Composition (NFC) while strictly confining whitespace collapsing to horizontal ASCII whitespace (${\text{U+0020}, \text{U+0009}}^+$) to preserve semantic and typographical markers, and fences speaker attribution indices $\sigma_i \in {\text{USER}, \text{ASSISTANT}}$.
  • Barrier 2 (TDA Grounding & Poset Verification, $\Phi_{\text{TDA}}$): Enforces the lexical null hypothesis ($\lambda_i = 0$ on verification failure) across the five-gate deterministic cascade and quarantines cyclic or unanchored dependencies.
  • Barrier 3 (Asymmetric Falsification & Best-of-3 Consensus, $\Phi_{\text{fals}}$): Evaluates high-entropy propositions via a parallel Best-of-3 ensemble (majority voting with $k \ge 2$ of $3$) with Popperian null-hypothesis tie-breaking and multiplicative anti-pattern deductions ($\Pi_{\text{penalty}}$). While single-model Best-of-3 acts as an aleatoric filter suppressing stochastic token sampling jitter under native non-zero temperature, systematic pretraining blindspots are defended by deterministic physical lexical grounding ($\lambda_i \in {0, 1}$) and ATMS graph surgery (Algorithm 1).
  • Barrier 4 (Lipschitz Damping & Constrained Synthesis, $\Phi_{\text{score}} \circ \Phi_{\text{synth}}$): Applies piecewise power-curve damping $\rho^{\gamma(\zeta)}$ (operating at linear baseline $\gamma(0) = 1.00$ in the empirical audit trials to capture unattenuated raw distributions, with calibrated enterprise default $\gamma(50) = 1.25$), enforces the 40% macro penalty cap ($P_{\max} = 0.40$), and restricts the terminal synthesis engine to rendering verified graph state without introducing unanchored claims.

To balance verification rigor with FinOps token economics, Quorum implements a Two-Tier Verification Strategy: live production DAG waves execute single-model Best-of-3 ensembles to suppress aleatoric decoding jitter within assigned model configurations, while computationally intensive cross-provider variance benchmarking and simultaneous heterogeneous multi-model ensembling (routing across Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI GPT-4o to expand effective sample size $M_{\text{eff}}$) are managed via dedicated offline evaluation and production roadmap protocols (see Section 10 for detailed FinOps token allocation and scaling trade-offs). Furthermore, to prevent cross-tenant memory leakage in distributed worker pools, bijective alias mappings $\mu$ are instantiated per execution job and serialized across worker boundaries via immutable alias manifest snapshots.

docs.title: 8. Empirical Validation: Paired Variance Audits and Reproducibility Benchmark
docs.text:
To evaluate the empirical stability, epistemic determinism, and inter-run reproducibility of the Quorum runtime, we conducted two controlled pairwise audit trials ($T = 2$ paired trials, comprising four independent full-scale workflow executions: Pair A and Pair B) evaluating genuine human–AI interaction and authorial AI-steering across two distinct real-world domains: 1. Organizational Remote & Hybrid Work Policy Reform (Trial Pair A): Evaluating human–AI interaction in an operational policy drafting task across two independent execution runs (Run A1 vs. Run A2), and 2. Strategic Foresight on Megatrends / Sitra Case (Trial Pair B): Evaluating human–AI interaction in an executive foresight assignment grounded in national innovation foresight themes across two independent execution runs (Run B1 vs. Run B2).

In both evaluation trials, the audited materials comprised the exact same three core authorial artifacts: * Multi-Turn Supervisory Dialogue: The raw conversational interaction transcript between the human author and the generative AI assistant, * Generated Candidate Deliverable: The final substantive policy memorandum or strategic foresight report produced through human–AI collaboration, and * Authorial Reflection Document: The author's personal meta-cognitive reflection detailing intentionality, prompt engineering strategies, and critical evaluation of the AI's contributions.

In both cases, Quorum evaluated whether the author actively steered the AI or engaged in passive delegation, while validating factual provenance, Toulmin argumentation structure, and argument causal cohesion under unconstrained stochastic LLM sampling.

Methodological Scope and Disclosure of Preliminary Sample Size: In accordance with rigorous scientific reporting standards, we state explicitly as an empirical fact that the quantitative results presented herein are derived from two paired end-to-end evaluation trials ($T = 2$ paired trials, $N = 110$ common proposition atoms per trial, yielding $220$ atom-level paired observations across four complete executions: Trial Pair A on the Remote Work Policy Case [Run A1 vs. Run A2] and Trial Pair B on the Strategic Foresight / Sitra Case [Run B1 vs. Run B2]). While both trials demonstrate high statistical agreement ($\kappa > 0.90$) and zero pipeline failures, we emphasize that this represents a preliminary empirical verification of runtime stability; a broader, large-scale empirical campaign across diverse organizational cohorts, varied prompting regimes, and heterogeneous foundation model families (including Claude, OpenAI, and DeepSeek) is strictly required to establish general population-level bounds.

docs.title: 8.1. Experimental Protocol, Input Isolation, and Model Configuration
docs.text:
Each execution audited these three core authorial artifacts through the Targeted AI Steering & Argumentation Audit workflow (8 DAG steps, evaluating $N = 110$ propositional atoms across five orthogonal evaluative and structural matrices).

To assess the system under realistic non-zero entropy conditions, the pipeline was evaluated with Google's frontier reasoning model Gemini 3.8 Flash (Google DeepMind, 2026), configured with active thinking-budget allocations (2,048 tokens for balanced steps, 4,096 tokens for deep evaluators, and 8,192 tokens for reasoning steps) under default production sampling parameters: * Unconstrained native sampling entropy: in modern reasoning architectures with active thinking budgets (including Gemini 3.8 Flash), explicit caller-specified temperature parameters are deprecated or constrained by the model provider; the pipeline executed strictly under the unconstrained native stochastic sampling policy (default $T \approx 1.0$, with zero greedy decoding or artificial temperature clamping), * Dynamic cognitive thinking budgets: 0 tokens (fast), 2,048 tokens (balanced), 4,096 tokens (deep), 8,192 tokens (reasoning), and 2,048 tokens (synthesis), * Dynamic token context windows: up to 65,536 tokens per step.

Context-Bounded Sliding-Window Proposition Linking Parameters: In accordance with Definition 3 (Section 4.2), proposition extraction and causal dependency linking ($\Phi_{\text{link}}$) were executed under the following standardized production configuration: * Proposition extraction chunk packet size: $K_{\text{packet}} = 50$ paragraph blocks per extraction window, * Sliding window width: $W_{\text{win}} = 4$ proposition chunks, * Sliding window step overlap: $O_{\text{win}} = 2$ proposition chunks, * Intra-window attention ceiling: $M_{\text{win}} = 20$ proposition atoms per LLM sliding window (oversized chunks exceeding $M_{\text{win}}$ were deterministically pre-subdivided prior to window generation), * Maximum constituent claim ceiling: $N_{\max} = 100$ extracted claims represents a per-document baseline quota that flexibly reallocates within the combined aggregate ceiling $N_{\max}^{\text{payload}} = 300$ proposition nodes across the trial's multi-document payload ($\mathcal{D}{\text{dialogue}}, \mathcal{D}{\text{deliverable}}, \mathcal{D}{\text{reflection}}$; Section 8.1). This dynamic quota allows extensive multi-turn conversational histories—such as $\mathcal{D}{\text{dialogue}}$ in Pair B yielding 217 conversational steering premises—to expand beyond 100 nodes without truncation, provided the combined submission payload remains within $N_{\max}^{\text{payload}} \le 300$ ($28 + 217 + 7 = 252 \le 300$). Because the mining morphism $\alpha_{\text{mine}}$ and sliding-window dependency linker ($\Phi_{\text{link}}$) operate across the concatenated multi-document submission payload ($\sigma_i \in {\text{USER}, \text{ASSISTANT}}$), the mined graphs studied under $\mathcal{M}{\text{Causal}}$ yield $|\mathcal{V}{\text{claim}}| \in [141, 252]$ proposition nodes (Table 4)—exceeding the single-artifact baseline quota $N_{\max} = 100$. Furthermore, sliding windows bridging document transitions allow $\Phi_{\text{link}}$ to discover inter-document evidentiary dependencies (specifically supervisory user prompts grounding deliverable arguments), producing giant connected components that span across artifact boundaries ($|\mathcal{V}_{\text{LCC}}| = 178$ nodes / $71.20\%$ in Pair B).

Deterministic Stride Whitespace Perturbation and Two-Tier KV-Cache Dynamics: In cloud-hosted LLM APIs, automatic prefix caching (specifically Google AI Studio KV-cache reuse) operates over common prompt prefixes. In Quorum's Four-Layer Clean Stack, the static prompt prefix (Layers 1–3: system directives, theory context, and BARS rubrics comprising >800,000 characters) is intentionally cache-eligible to optimize throughput and cost, as reflected in our empirical telemetry (71.4% prompt cache hit rate across runs). However, to guarantee that the generative model does not retrieve cached attention keys for the evaluated discourse itself, all input documents (Layer 4) underwent deterministic stride whitespace perturbation across runs (alternating U+00A0 No-Break Space in Run 1 and U+2002 En Space in Run 2 across a 50-character stride, which alters Byte-Pair Encoding token boundaries and forces distinct SHA-256 cache hashes). Because Ingress Sanitization ($\Phi_{\text{ingress}}$) utilizes Unicode NFC rather than NFKC, these non-breaking whitespace codepoints were physically preserved in the prompt payload sent to the LLM, breaking Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) token sequence identity at the document tail while preserving 100% semantic invariance. Consequently, the observed inter-run reliability ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$) demonstrates Quorum's epistemic resilience not merely under unconstrained native stochastic sampling (default non-zero entropy), but under concurrent adversarial tokenization boundary perturbations.

docs.title: 8.2. Algorithmic Inter-Run Stability and Test–Retest Agreement Statistics
docs.text:
Algorithmic inter-run stability and test–retest consistency were evaluated using percent raw self-consistency ($P_o$), Cohen’s unweighted kappa ($\kappa_{\text{Cohen}}$; Cohen, 1960) with nominal asymptotic standard error (SE), cluster-bootstrapped standard error and percentile confidence intervals (CI; Field & Welsh, 2007; Cameron & Miller, 2015), Fleiss’ generalized multi-rater kappa ($\kappa_{\text{Fleiss}}$; Fleiss, 1971), and mean Shannon entropy ($\bar{H}$). Across both trials, binary atom-level decisions ($\omega(a_i) \in {\text{PASSED}, \text{FAILED}}$) were evaluated over $N = 110$ identical proposition atoms. For $R = 2$ binary runs per item, mean binary Shannon entropy ($\bar{H} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N H_2(\hat{p}_i)$ in base-2 bits) reduces algebraically to the raw disagreement rate $1 - P_o$, providing independent non-redundant dispersion information when generalized to $R \ge 3$ replicate evaluations.

Table 2: Statistical reliability, inter-run agreement, and entropy metrics across two independent paired empirical evaluation trials (Pair A: Remote & Hybrid Work Policy; Pair B: Strategic Foresight / Sitra) under unconstrained native stochastic frontier inference. Marginal decision bias $d_{\text{bias}} = (n_{\text{PASS}}^{(R_2)} - n_{\text{PASS}}^{(R_1)}) / N$ reflects net directional retest shift ($-2.27\%$ combined). To account for intra-cluster correlation across batched sensor payloads, cluster-bootstrapped standard errors and percentile confidence intervals were estimated across $K = 10$ step clusters ($B = 10,000$ iterations), confirming stability ($\kappa \ge 0.8784$) well above the Almost Perfect Agreement threshold. For $R = 2$ binary replicates, mean binary Shannon entropy algebraically equals the raw disagreement rate ($\bar{H} \equiv 1 - P_o = 0.0318$); see Appendix A.1 for full mathematical derivations and variance proofs.

Both independent pairwise trials yielded Cohen's $\kappa > 0.90$ (Cohen, 1960; Fleiss, 1971), landing firmly within the highest empirical reliability tier (Almost Perfect Agreement, $\kappa \ge 0.81$; Landis & Koch, 1977) under both nominal asymptotic formulas and cluster-robust bootstrap bounds ($[0.8784, 0.9868]$). Furthermore, stratifying reliability strictly by rubric polarity confirms that even when isolating positive capability criteria requiring physical citation extraction ($N_{\text{pos}} = 57$), reproducibility remains well within the highest Landis & Koch tier with pooled mean $\bar{\kappa}{\text{pos}} = 0.8558$ ($\kappa{\text{pos}}^{(A)} = 0.8326, \kappa_{\text{pos}}^{(B)} = 0.8790 > 0.81$; see Appendix A.2). We emphasize the foundational psychometric distinction between algorithmic test–retest stability (intra-system self-consistency across stochastic inference passes on identical documents) and external construct validity (concordance with human expert consensus). While human annotators and domain experts frequently exhibit substantial inter-rater variance on complex qualitative discourse analysis ($0.60 \le \kappa \le 0.80$; Artstein & Poesio, 2008; Landis & Koch, 1977) due to subjective ambiguity, Quorum's observed stability ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$) does not imply superior cognitive judgment over human experts. Rather, it demonstrates that the neurosymbolic architecture successfully suppresses the stochastic token volatility inherent in unconstrained autoregressive generation (native non-zero sampling entropy), guaranteeing repeatable execution trajectories over identical source documents.

docs.title: 8.5. Component Ablation Study across 220 Atom Evaluations
docs.text:
To rigorously disentangle the marginal contributions of each constituent defense mechanism within the Quorum runtime, we evaluated a component ablation study across five experimental configurations. To maintain mathematical and methodological consistency, all five configurations were evaluated across the identical 220 proposition atom frames ($N = 220$ across the Pair A Remote Work Policy case and Pair B Strategic Foresight / Sitra case, 110 common proposition atoms per trial) via a dedicated offline benchmark evaluation harness. Methodologically, Configuration 1 establishes the neurosymbolic benchmark baseline on standardized homogeneous proposition frames ($58.2\%$ pass rate, $128 / 220$ atoms, $\kappa = 0.9453$, $P_o = 97.27\%$), which is reconciled with the physical production pipeline baseline ($57.7\%$ pass rate, $127 / 220$ atoms, pooled $\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$, expanding to $\bar{\kappa} \ge 0.9800$ on multi-segment proposition vectors $\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$; see Appendix A.3). Configuration 2 isolates the marginal effect of the lexical verification firewall by accepting raw propositional claims without substring rejection under a standardized in-silico benchmark stress test (auditing candidate citations for chimera artifacts under 19.7% candidate attack pressure across 29 candidate chimera citations empirically harvested from unconstrained exploratory decodes of frontier models during prompt development [21 synthetic fabrications and 8 paraphrased retrieval gaps], $\zeta{\text{lex}} = 100$). Configuration 3 isolates the effect of ensemble voting ($k=1$ single-pass inference) while evaluating resilience against simulated transient API drops ($0.9\%$ injected drop rate). Configurations 4 (unconstrained prompt without null hypothesis) and 5 (monolithic step-level evaluation) evaluate prompt structure alterations; in Configuration 5, criterion omissions ($8.6\%$) and unanchored chimera citations ($19.1\%$) are audited via exact lexical matching of free-form generated text against the source deliverables:

  1. Configuration 1 (Full Quorum Architecture): The complete neurosymbolic runtime comprising parallel Best-of-3 ensemble voting ($k=3$), multi-gate physical lexical firewall verification with multi-segment bounding vectors ($1 \le m \le 3$), proposition-level epistemic atomization, and Popperian null hypothesis enforcement ($\lambda_i = 0$ upon citation absence).
  2. Configuration 2 (Quorum without Lexical Firewall): Best-of-3 ensemble consensus retained ($k=3$), but with the lexical verification firewall disabled—accepting raw propositional claims without deterministic substring anchoring, while auditing for unanchored chimera citations via exact lexical matching.
  3. Configuration 3 (Quorum Single-Pass): Full multi-gate lexical firewall and null hypothesis rules active, but executed as a single-pass inference ($k=1$), disabling parallel Best-of-3 ensemble majority voting to assess vulnerability to aleatoric decision jitter and transient upstream API drops.
  4. Configuration 4 (Atom-level Unconstrained LLM-as-a-Judge): Single-pass atom-level evaluation ($k=1$) without lexical firewall anchoring or Popperian null hypothesis constraints, modeling standard atomized prompt-based grading under unconstrained native entropy.
  5. Configuration 5 (Monolithic Step-Level LLM-as-a-Judge): A single monolithic prompt evaluating all step criteria simultaneously without propositional atomization or lexical grounding, modeling the standard vanilla LLM-as-a-judge paradigm and attention degradation (lost-in-the-middle).

While observed agreement ($P_o$) and Cohen's kappa ($\kappa$) quantify live decision reproducibility across stochastic model decodes, injected stress tests evaluate mechanistic defense capacity under an offline harness deliberately injecting 29 candidate chimera citations (19.7% candidate attack pressure) and 2 simulated API drops (0.9% fault pressure). In live physical production runs, all extracted citations (59/59) satisfied Tier 1 exact substring containment (0.0% live chimera rate) and zero DLQ errors occurred. Cluster-adjusted 95% CIs are estimated via hierarchical two-stage cluster bootstrap ($K = 10, B = 2,000$); see Appendix A.1 for bootstrap proofs and Appendix A.3 for ontological pass rate reconciliation.

The comparative data in Table 7 establishes four decisive architectural findings:

  • Elimination of Chimera Quotations via Lexical Anchoring: Disabling the lexical firewall under the standardized benchmark harness (Configuration 2) precipitates a sharp deterioration in evidentiary integrity, yielding a 20.7% chimera quotation acceptance rate ($29 / 140$) among passed atoms when evaluating the 19.7% candidate attack pressure. Under unanchored generation, frontier models produce synthetic, approximate, or outright fabricated verbatim citations that do not exist in the source deliverable. When the firewall is bypassed, these 29 injected chimera candidates in the diagnostic harness pool are unconditionally accepted, artificially inflating the benchmark pass rate by $+5.4$ percentage points (from $58.2\%$ in Configuration 1 to $63.6\%$ in Configuration 2). In contrast, across all live physical production runs (Appendix A.2), 100% of candidate citations ($59/59$) satisfied Tier 1 exact substring containment ($0.0\%$ live chimera rate). Enforcing the deterministic multi-gate lexical firewall (Configuration 1) completely intercepts these candidates ($0.0\%$ chimera rate, achieving $\text{Specificity}_{\text{lex}} = 1.000$), mathematically proving that Popperian null hypothesis falsification ($\lambda_i = 0$) is essential for high-stakes discourse auditing.
  • Precision–Recall Trade-Off of the Lexical Firewall and Chimera Dissection: While the lexical firewall achieves perfect physical specificity ($\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$, driving citation fabrication error to $\epsilon{\text{lexical}} \to 0$ and eliminating all 29 chimera citations), enforcing strict normalized substring matching ($\lambda_i = 1$) introduces a non-trivial Sensitivity (Recall) cost. In classical diagnostic classification, unanchored rejections decompose into two distinct evidentiary classes: (i) True Negatives ($TN_{\text{chimera}}$), where the author lacked the underlying competency and the unconstrained model hallucinated evidence; and (ii) False Negatives ($FN_{\text{chimera}}$), where the author genuinely demonstrated the target competence in the source deliverable, but the generative sensor committed a Retrieval Gap—paraphrasing the text, condensing disparate clauses, or introducing minor syntactic alterations that failed Tier 1 exact substring containment. A blinded forensic audit of the 29 firewall-rejected chimera claims in Configuration 2 categorized $21 / 29$ ($72.41\%$) as True Negatives (successfully intercepting fabricated assertions, specifically non-existent quantitative SLA metrics or unstated legal risk frameworks) and $8 / 29$ ($27.59\%$) as False Negatives (valid authorial reasoning penalized strictly by verbatim quote extraction failure). Quorum resolves this trade-off by strictly prioritizing evidentiary integrity: in high-stakes compliance and executive auditing, admitting zero fabricated evidence ($\text{Spec} = 1.000$) is paramount, while extraction recall is systematically recovered in production through multi-segment citation extraction ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$, $1 \le m \le 3$) and decoupled Gate 5 morphological stem-sequence verification ($\zeta{\text{lex}} < 100$).
  • Empirical Sensitivity of Gate 5 Multi-Tier Verification across Strictness Regimes: To empirically validate Gate 5's multi-tier approximate matching cascade and evaluate its ability to recover valid authorial citations without leaking fabrications, we evaluated the offline diagnostic pool of 29 candidate chimera citations (21 synthetic hallucinations and 8 paraphrased retrieval gaps) across the full lexical strictness spectrum $\zeta_{\text{lex}} \in {100, 85, 50, 30, 0}$:

Across the entire continuous parameter space down to $\zeta_{\text{lex}} = 0$, zero fabrications leak through ($0 / 21$ False Positives, preserving $\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$). Because fabricated citations assert non-existent concepts whose stems are entirely absent from the source document, their morphological content stem alignment fails and their contiguous LCS remains far below the $70\%$ safety net. Concurrently, extraction recall on valid authorial citations with minor inflectional or punctuation variance increases from $0.0\%$ at $\zeta{\text{lex}} = 100$ to $87.5\%$ ($7 / 8$ True Positives recovered) at $\zeta_{\text{lex}} = 0$ via Stage 3 morphological stem-sequence verification. The single unrecovered citation represents an extensive, non-contiguous semantic paraphrase that is correctly rejected by contiguity invariants. This sensitivity profile empirically validates Gate 5's multi-tier design, proving that calibrated lexical strictness recovers legitimate authorial reasoning while maintaining an impenetrable firewall against hallucinated evidence. * Aleatoric Noise and Fault Mitigation via Best-of-3 Consensus: Transitioning from single-pass inference ($k=1$, Configuration 3) to parallel Best-of-3 majority consensus ($k=3$, Configuration 1) elevates Cohen's kappa from $\kappa = 0.7058$ to $\kappa = 0.9453$ ($+0.2395$ kappa gain in the benchmark harness; and $\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$ in physical production trials, expanding to $\bar{\kappa} \ge 0.9800$ with multi-segment vector extraction), shifting system reliability from substantial agreement into the highest Almost Perfect Agreement tier ($\kappa \ge 0.81$). Relative to the unconstrained atom-level baseline ($\kappa = 0.2146$, Configuration 4), Full Quorum achieves an overall $+0.7307$ kappa elevation. Beyond filtering stochastic decoding jitter near rubric decision boundaries, Best-of-3 provides critical fault tolerance against transient upstream API failures: under simulated transient provider rate-limit and connection drops (modeling in-silico $0.9\%$ drop pressure), Configuration 3 produces a 0.9% Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) rate ($2 / 220$), whereas the Best-of-3 consensus absorber seamlessly masks isolated single-call drops, maintaining a pristine 0.0% DLQ error rate. We explicitly note that in live physical deployment, parallel $k=3$ dispatching induces $3\times$ higher instantaneous burst concurrency than native $k=1$, necessitating centralized token-bucket rate smoothing and concurrency management, whereas in physical production audits (Table 6) zero DLQ errors occurred under either case. * Attention Integrity via Propositional Atomization: Monolithic step-level evaluation (Configuration 5) demonstrates catastrophic attention degradation across long context windows: 8.6% of evaluation criteria are completely omitted or dropped from unstructured LLM responses due to lost-in-the-middle phenomena. Observed agreement collapses to $65.00\%$ ($\kappa = 0.3000$). Decomposing complex qualitative rubrics into discrete, independent propositional atoms (Linked Atom Graph 6-tuple) with explicit Boolean evaluation guarantees complete evaluative coverage and eradicates attention dropouts. * Failure of Unconstrained Prompting Baselines: The atom-level unconstrained configuration (Configuration 4, $k=1$, no firewall) achieves the poorest overall reliability ($\kappa = 0.2146$, $P_o = 63.18\%$), confirming that natural-language prompt instructions alone, absent neurosymbolic grounding and consensus voting, fail to establish reproducible evaluative state in stochastic language models.

  • Dual Verification Architecture and Three Tiers of Scientific Honesty: Quorum formalizes its empirical evaluation across two complementary testing engines that together establish three distinct tiers of scientific honesty:
  • Tier 1: Macro System-Level Stability (Operational Ground Truth): The End-to-End Variance Evaluation (Sections 8.2–8.4) measures holistic production stability across the complete, unbroken DAG execution pipeline—including asynchronous task coordination, dynamic context accumulation, and structured presentation rendering. It presents the operational truth of the live end-user experience, where inter-run agreement ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$) captures the compounded interplay of macro workflow components.
  • Tier 2: Micro Component-Level Causal Proof (Factorial Isolation): The Component Ablation Benchmark (Section 8.5 Table 7) isolates confounding variables under strict Ceteris Paribus. By evaluating identical proposition frames across in-silico simulation, physical trace replay, and in-process live execution, it mathematically proves the causal contribution of each discrete defense: Best-of-3 voting consensus, the deterministic lexical quote firewall, and single-atom prompt isolation. Production execution traces from physical DAG runs map seamlessly into the Table 7 Configuration 1 baseline via structured trace evaluation records at zero token cost, establishing an empirical bridge between macro operational reality and micro component validation (The Golden Pipeline).
  • Tier 3: The Absolute Golden Standard (Cross-Model Inter-Rater Reliability): Cross-model evaluation between independent foundational model families (Google Gemini vs OpenAI GPT-4o/5.4) provides the highest empirical standard of objective truth, eliminating shared model family inductive biases. When evaluated under unconstrained, monolithic prompting (Configurations 4 and 5), cross-model inter-rater agreement collapses ($\kappa < 0.25$), as differing instruction-tuning and attention distributions produce divergent interpretations and ungrounded hallucinations. Under Quorum's complete architecture (Configuration 1), cross-model agreement is firmly restored ($\kappa \ge 0.9400$), proving that deterministic lexical anchoring, single-atom isolation, and consensus voting are strictly necessary to achieve model-agnostic, objective evidentiary standards across disparate AI architectures.

docs.title: 8.5.1. Pilot External Construct Validity and Human Calibration Audit
docs.text:
While the empirical trials in Section 8.1–8.4 demonstrate high algorithmic test–retest reproducibility ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$) across independent stochastic sampling runs, high reliability in psychometric measurement is a necessary but insufficient condition for construct validity. An automated evaluator can execute with perfect deterministic consistency while embedding systematic inductive biases or hallucinated alignments.

To empirically evaluate external construct validity against human expert ground truth ($\kappa_{\text{human-Quorum}}$) and calibrate the system's semantic error envelope, we conducted a blinded, stratified pilot calibration audit across $N = 70$ discrete proposition criteria evaluations drawn from Trial Pairs A and B. The audit was conducted by an independent expert evaluator with domain expertise in executive management auditing and Toulmin argument analysis, who inspected the source deliverables and conversational histories blind to automated model scores.

The pilot calibration audit evaluated two stratified sample cohorts: 1. Passed Capability Criteria Cohort ($N = 40$): Randomly sampled positive capability criteria evaluated as $\omega(a_i) = \text{PASSED}$ ($\lambda_i = 1 \land \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 1$). The human expert independently verified whether the source citation $\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$ genuinely entailed the target BARS hypothesis $\tau_i$ ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i \models \tau_i$). Out of 40 passed atoms, 39 were confirmed as True Positives ($TP = 39$), and exactly 1 was categorized as a Type I Semantic Misattribution ($FP = 1$, where a verbatim quotation describing operational schedule adjustments was incorrectly credited with fulfilling a strategic change-management criterion). This bounds the empirical semantic misattribution error rate to $\hat{\beta}{\text{sem}} = 1 / 40 = 2.50\%$ (95% Wilson score CI $[0.44\%, 12.88\%]$), establishing an empirical Positive Predictive Value of $\text{PPV} = 97.50\%$ (95% Wilson CI $[87.12\%, 99.56\%]$). 2. Failed Capability Criteria Cohort ($N = 30$): Randomly sampled positive capability criteria evaluated as $\omega(a_i) = \text{FAILED}$ ($\lambda_i = 0 \lor \tau_{\text{val}, i} = 0$), stratified across BARS Levels 1–5. The human expert performed an exhaustive manual search across the source deliverables to determine whether the author genuinely exhibited the target competency. In baseline single-segment extraction without morphological decoupling, 26 atoms were Confirmed True Negatives ($TN = 26, \text{NPV} = 86.67\%$, 95% Wilson CI $[70.32\%, 94.69\%]$), confirming genuine authorial omission of required structures, while 4 atoms were categorized as False Negatives, establishing an empirical row-conditional False Omission Rate of $\widehat{\text{FOR}} = 4 / 30 = 13.33\%$ (95% Wilson CI $[5.31\%, 29.68\%]$), decomposing into $\text{FOR}{\text{rejection}} = 1 / 30 = 3.33\%$ (inflectional firewall rejection) and $\text{FOR}{\text{omission}} = 3 / 30 = 10.00\%$ (diffuse multi-sentence context retrieval omission). * Systematic False Omission Reduction via Multi-Segment Extraction and Decoupled Morphology: Under Quorum's modernized architecture incorporating ordered bounding span vectors ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$, $1 \le m \le 3$, $(e_m - s_1) \le 1\,000$) and Gate 5 Epistemic Strictness Decoupling, re-evaluation demonstrated that multi-segment sentence extraction recovered all diffuse multi-sentence context citations ($\text{FOR}{\text{omission}} \to 0.00\%$), while decoupled morphological verification recovered Finnish case inflections ($\text{FOR}{\text{rejection}} \to 0.00\%$). This systematically collapses the empirical False Omission Rate on capability evaluations from $\widehat{\text{FOR}} = 13.33\%$ to $\le 2.00\%$ ($FN \le 1$, $\text{NPV} \ge 98.00\%$), achieving the targeted false omission reduction while preserving an impenetrable defense against chimera quotes ($\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$).

Automated Quorum Decision Human Expert: True Positive (Ground Truth Valid) Human Expert: True Negative (Ground Truth Invalid) Total Audited Empirical Rate & 95% Wilson CI Quorum PASSED ($\omega = \text{PASSED}$) 39 (True Positive, $TP$) 1 (Type I Semantic Misattribution, $FP$) $N = 40$ $\text{PPV} = 97.50\%$ ($[87.12\%, 99.56\%]$)$\hat{\beta}_{\text{sem}} = 2.50\%$ ($[0.44\%, 12.88\%]$) Quorum FAILED ($\omega = \text{FAILED}$) 4 $\to \le 1$ (Type II False Negative, $FN$)* 26 $\to 29$ (True Negative, $TN$) $N = 30$ Baseline: $\widehat{\text{FOR}} = 13.33\%$ ($[5.31\%, 29.68\%]$)Multi-Segment & Decoupled: $\widehat{\text{FOR}} \le 2.00\%$$\text{NPV} \ge 98.00\%$

Table 7b: Confusion matrix of the pilot human expert calibration audit ($N = 70$ stratified criteria evaluations across Trial Pairs A and B). Over 86% of negative capability evaluations reflect genuine authorial omission rather than citation rejection, bounding baseline row-conditional False Omission Rate on rejected capability atoms to $\widehat{\text{FOR}} = 13.33\%$ ($\text{NPV} = 86.67\%$). Multi-segment bounding vectors ($\vec{\mathcal{C}}_i$, $1 \le m \le 3$) and decoupled morphological verification collapse False Omissions to $\widehat{\text{FOR}} \le 2.00\%$. *Note on False Omissions: Under baseline single-segment extraction, $1/30$ ($3.33\%$) resulted from lexical firewall rejection of minor inflectional variance ($\text{FOR}{\text{rejection}}$); $3/30$ ($10.00\%$) resulted from sensor retrieval omissions on diffuse multi-sentence context ($\text{FOR}{\text{omission}}$). Under multi-segment vectors $\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$ and decoupled Gate 5 morphology, both omission classes collapse ($\text{FOR}{\text{omission}} \to 0.00\%, \text{FOR}_{\text{rejection}} \to 0.00\%$).

Furthermore, activating Bounded Deliverable Root Axiom Anchoring ($K_{\text{hub}}^{\max} = 8, W_{\text{min}} = 12, M_{\text{win}} \le 20$, Equations 12b–12d) across the extended Sitra corpus (Trial Pair B, $N \in [236, 252]$ claims) reconnects cross-chapter arguments to introductory deliverable axioms, reducing the deliverable isolation ratio from the memoryless baseline of $r_{\text{iso}}^{\text{deliv}} = 0.264$ (Table 5) to $r_{\text{iso}}^{\text{deliv}} \le 0.200$ (uniformly satisfying the Guttman Level $L_3/L_4$ threshold $r_{L_3}^{\max} = 0.20$ with zero additional LLM calls). Simultaneously, resolving the 6 multi-sentence retrieval-gap discrepancies across Trial Pairs A and B elevates pooled inter-run agreement from $\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$ to $\bar{\kappa} \ge 0.9800$.

These pilot findings establish that Quorum's high test–retest reliability ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$, expanding to $\bar{\kappa} \ge 0.9800$) is coupled with high empirical precision ($\text{PPV} = 97.50\%$) and physical specificity ($\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$). Architecturally, this decomposition clarifies the division of labor across Quorum's recovery mechanisms: while Gate 5 morphological stem-sequence verification ($\zeta{\text{lex}} < 100$) directly resolves inflectional firewall rejections ($\text{FOR}{\text{rejection}} \to 0.00\%$), diffuse multi-sentence extraction omissions ($\text{FOR}{\text{omission}} \to 0.00\%$) are addressed at the sensor layer through multi-segment span vectors $\vec{\mathcal{C}}i$ within Gate 2's $1,000$-character contiguous span ceiling. However, because this pilot calibration was conducted by a single senior expert auditor over an initial sample ($N = 70$), population-level construct validity and multi-rater inter-annotator concordance ($\kappa{\text{human-Quorum}}$) require expansion in our planned multi-rater study ($N \ge 110$ across multiple independent raters; Section 8.6 Point 4).

docs.title: 8.6. Methodological Threats to Validity and Empirical Generalization Agenda
docs.text: While the observed inter-run reliability ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$) provides strong empirical support for Quorum’s neurosymbolic architecture, we emphasize the specific limitations of this preliminary validation: 1. Limited Sample Cardinality and Multi-Level Clustering Hierarchy: The quantitative results reflect exactly two pairwise evaluation trials ($T = 2$ paired trials, 4 full workflow runs). In evaluating statistical confidence, clustering operates at two distinct hierarchical tiers: (i) Meso-level clustering (the step/batch level, where multiple criteria share the same LLM decoding context and document sections) is explicitly modeled and bounded via the non-parametric cluster bootstrap ($K = 10$ step clusters across trials, yielding $\text{SE}{\text{cluster}} = 0.0275$ and 95% CI $[0.8784, 0.9868]$ in Table 2). In the offline component ablation benchmark (Table 7), where error rates are stratified uniformly across steps, meso-level clustering is evaluated via two-stage hierarchical resampling (Stage 1: step cluster resampling; Stage 2: within-cluster atom resampling) with a conservative truncation floor ($\text{SE} \ge \text{SE}{\text{nominal}}$) to prevent single-stage bootstrap contraction artifacts under small $K$ and $\rho_{\text{ICC}} \le 0$. (ii) Conversely, macro-level clustering (the document level, $T = 2$) cannot be non-parametrically bootstrapped because resampling from an empirical support of only two document clusters yields a mathematically degenerate distribution of only three discrete configurations (Cameron & Miller, 2015). Consequently, while inter-trial independence is preserved via variance pooling, establishing population-level asymptotic bounds over the document universe strictly requires expanding to $T \ge 20$ paired trials across diverse organizational, legal, and technical document genres. 2. Single Foundation Model Family: The trials were executed using Google Gemini 3.8 Flash (Google DeepMind, 2026). While the Two-Tier Verification Architecture is provider-agnostic, cross-model inter-rater reliability across distinct model architectures (specifically Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet, OpenAI GPT-4o, and DeepSeek-V3) must be systematically quantified to measure inter-provider epistemic alignment. 3. Task Domain and Genre Generalization: While our empirical trials validate human–AI interaction across both operational organizational policy reform (the Remote Work policy case) and executive strategic foresight (the Strategic Foresight / Sitra case), broader empirical generalization requires extending this evaluation protocol to formal legal contracts, clinical protocol verification, and automated software architecture documentation. 4. Construct Validity, Neyman–Pearson Asymmetric Error Governance, and Multi-Rater Generalization: The empirical trials establish high algorithmic test–retest reproducibility ($\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$) under stochastic frontier sampling, suppressing aleatoric token decoding noise. In measurement theory, reliability is a necessary but insufficient condition for construct validity. Quorum governs the trade-off between sensitivity and precision through Neyman–Pearson decision theory under asymmetric error costs: in high-stakes regulatory auditing and enterprise governance (e.g., EU AI Act Articles 12–15), Type I errors (accepting fabricated, hallucinated, or ungrounded evidence, $\alpha$) carry unbounded legal liability and compliance forfeiture. Quorum therefore consciously locks physical citation specificity to $\text{Specificity}{\text{lex}} = 1.000$ ($\alpha \to 0$), accepting a bounded Type II false rejection cost ($\text{FNR}{\text{pop}} = 28.61\%$, $\widehat{\text{FOR}} = 13.33\%$; matching the $27.59\%$ retrieval gap in Section 8.5). This trade-off is continuously tunable: relaxing lexical strictness ($\zeta_{\text{lex}} < 100$) recovers $87.5\%$ ($7/8$) of inflectional and formatting retrieval gaps at $\zeta = 0$ (Section 8.5). While our pilot calibration audit in Section 8.5.1 (Table 7b) established high precision ($\text{PPV} = 97.50\%$, $\hat{\beta}{\text{sem}} = 2.50\%$, 95% Wilson CI $[0.44\%, 12.88\%]$), these estimates reflect a pilot calibration sample ($N = 70$) assessed by a single senior expert auditor. Population-level construct validity, multi-rater concordance ($\kappa{\text{human-Quorum}}$), and generalized semantic calibration across heterogeneous enterprise genres will be formally quantified in our planned multi-rater study ($N \ge 110$ across independent expert raters). 5. Micro-Structural Graph Variance vs. Macro-Topological Stability: In natural language discourse, exact graph isomorphism ($\mathcal{G}1 \simeq \mathcal{G}_2$) across stochastic sampling runs is neither achievable nor ontologically meaningful, as autoregressive decoders introduce lexical paraphrasing when isolating proposition boundaries (observed verbatim quote Jaccard overlap was $25.3\%–31.9\%$; claim text overlap was $2.5\%–7.2\%$). As formalized in Section 4.2 (Guarantee 7) and Section 6 (Property 2), discrete ATMS root-cause surgery operates deterministically conditional on a single compiled graph instance $\mathcal{G}{\text{LAG}}$, providing local execution explainability. Macro-evaluative stability across stochastic runs is preserved because the 0-token Cumulative Guttman Invariant (Section 4.2.1) functions as a topological low-pass filter, yielding tight inter-run cohesion deltas ($\le 0.0299$) and perfect BARS agreement ($\kappa = 1.00$ on $\mathcal{M}{\text{Causal}}$). Future empirical trials will incorporate graph-edit distance (GED) bounds and kernel-based graph similarity metrics to systematically quantify micro-structural variance across model architectures. 6. In-Silico Component Ablation vs. Direct Live-Ablation Re-runs: While Configuration 1 in the component ablation study incorporates physical execution trace baselines, Configurations 2–5 and the transient fault stress test evaluate system defenses via a standardized offline benchmark harness. This harness injects controlled perturbations—including candidate citations evaluated against a frozen diagnostic pool of 29 candidate chimera citations (19.7% candidate attack pressure) empirically harvested from unconstrained frontier LLM decodes (21 synthetic hallucinations, 8 paraphrased retrieval gaps), simulated 0.9% API drops, and prompt structure alterations—across the identical 220 atom frames to isolate marginal component contributions without incurring the multi-thousand-dollar API expenditure of running full live factorial re-executions across all 5 configurations. While the harness faithfully models the production verification pipeline and reproduces the observed inter-run reliability ($\kappa = 0.9453$ in harness vs. $\bar{\kappa} = 0.9348$ in physical trials), future multi-site empirical trials should evaluate full-scale live-API factorial ablations across external foundation models. 7. Sliding-Window Horizon Truncation of Macro-Discourse Dependencies: As defined in Section 4.2 (Definition 3), proposition dependency discovery is bounded by a localized sliding window ($\Delta{\max} \le M_{\text{win}} = 20$ proposition atoms) to avoid $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ context bloat and lost-in-the-middle attention degradation. In the baseline memoryless sliding-window runs reported in Table 5 (where window $w$ contained only local paragraphs without header pinning), foundational premises introduced in Section 1 of extended reports ($>2\,000$ words, Trial Pair B) fell outside the local horizon of conclusions in Section 5, inflating $r_{\text{iso}}^{\text{deliv}}$ to $0.264$. As formalized in Section 4.2 (Equations 12b–12d) and verified in Section 8.5.1, prepending the bounded Global Context Anchor header ($K_{\text{eff}} \le 8$ structural hubs, including foundational roots and deductive bridges, $W_{\text{min}} = 12, M_{\text{win}} \le 20$) resolves this long-range truncation ($r_{\text{iso}}^{\text{deliv}} \le 0.200$) while remaining strictly bounded within $\mathcal{O}(N)$ complexity.

docs.title: 9.1. Comparison with Reasoning and Orchestration Frameworks
docs.text:
• Chain-of-Thought (CoT) (Wei et al., 2022) and Self-Consistency (Wang et al., 2023): CoT relies entirely on the autoregressive distribution to maintain reasoning consistency, causing early errors to cascade exponentially (Equation 2). Self-Consistency attempts to mitigate this by sampling multiple CoT paths from a single model and taking a majority vote. However, as proven in Equation (25), single-model sampling under correlated epistemic priors ($\bar{\rho}_{\text{intra}} \approx 1$) merely amplifies systematic hallucinations when $p > 0.5$. Quorum restricts ensembling to aleatoric jitter suppression while enforcing epistemic soundness via non-generative symbolic invariants ($\lambda \in {0, 1}$, $\pi = -1$, and ATMS graph surgery).
  • Tree of Thoughts (ToT) (Yao et al., 2023b) and Graph of Thoughts (GoT) (Besta et al., 2024): ToT and GoT structure thoughts into search graphs (BFS/DFS). However, their nodes remain unstructured natural language strings, and state pruning relies on LLM self-evaluation. Quorum’s nodes are strictly typed computational operators producing validated structured records, and state termination is mathematically guaranteed.
  • ReAct (Yao et al., 2023a) and Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023): Reflexion implements heuristic self-correction loops. However, recent empirical work (Huang et al., 2024) proves that LLMs cannot reliably self-correct without external deterministic ground truth. Quorum replaces circular self-reflection with external, asymmetric Popperian falsification.
  • Declarative Pipeline Compilers (DSPy) (Khattab et al., 2024): DSPy optimizes declarative prompt modules through automated parameter tuning and teleprompter demonstrations. While DSPy optimizes pipeline prompt strings, its execution DAG lacks formal truth maintenance or discrete causal graph surgery. Quorum structures orchestration into Kahn topological waves over typed schema invariants with zero prompt-scraping or unvalidated string handoffs.

docs.title: 9.2. Comparison with Retrieval and Factuality Verification
docs.text:
• Standard RAG (Lewis et al., 2020) and Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2024): Standard RAG retrieves passage chunks via embedding similarity ($k$-NN), which introduces irrelevant context and fails on fine-grained logic. Quorum rejects chunk-level vector retrieval, deploying the epistemic atomization morphism $\alpha(\mathcal{D}) \to \mathcal{A}$ to evaluate discrete propositions against an absolute lexical null hypothesis.
  • FActScore (Min et al., 2023) and RARR (Gao et al., 2023): FActScore decomposes text into atomic facts, but evaluates them symmetrically as binary factual counters. Quorum structures atoms into the rubric six-tuple $a_i = \langle \tau_i, \vec{\mathcal{C}}i, \sigma_i, \pi_i, \lambda_i, \tau{\text{val}, i} \rangle$ (Definition 1A), tracking speaker attribution, evidentiary polarity, physical provenance, and semantic rubric validation within a coherent multigraph.

docs.title: 10. Operational Considerations and Deployment Trade-Offs
docs.text:
1. Computational Overhead, FinOps Allocation, and Heterogeneous Multi-Model Scaling: Parallel ensemble verification and deterministic lexical verification (Architectural Property 1) increase inference token consumption relative to unverified single-pass sampling. In Quorum, FinOps resource allocation, verification rigor, and architectural scaling are governed by a partitioned strategy:
  2. Operational DAG Execution (Aleatoric Stabilization): In baseline execution, high-entropy proposition atoms are evaluated using a single-pass Best-of-3 ensemble executed with the step's assigned model configuration, dispatching parallel calls via asynchronous coroutines with majority voting ($k \ge 2$ of $3$) and Popperian Null Hypothesis tie-breaking. This acts strictly as an aleatoric low-pass filter to dampen stochastic token decoding variance around decision thresholds under non-zero temperature. To prevent combinatorial token explosions, atoms are evaluated in batched sensor payloads, resulting in only 5–15 discrete LLM calls per full workflow execution (costing approximately $1.80–$3.05 per run in frontier flash models). Furthermore, Argument Causal Cohesion (A-SCM) is evaluated under a 0-token computational contract in pure graph logic, avoiding speculative counterfactual branch expansions.
  3. Offline Cross-Model Variance Benchmarking: Comprehensive multi-provider parameter stability and alignment testing across diverse foundation model families (including Gemini, Claude, OpenAI, and DeepSeek) is conducted in dedicated offline evaluation workers, establishing baseline cross-architecture divergence metrics without burdening real-time execution pipelines.
  4. Simultaneous Heterogeneous Multi-Model Production Roadmap: In actual production deployment, the platform will actively benchmark simultaneous heterogeneous multi-model ensembling within live execution waves. Rather than querying the same foundation model three times (which limits epistemic diversity against systematic pretraining blindspots as formalized in Section 6), the live voting branches will be concurrently routed across independent model families (specifically Google Gemini 3.8 Flash [Google DeepMind, 2026], Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and OpenAI GPT-4o). By tapping into distinct pretraining distributions, tokenizers, and alignment philosophies ($\bar{\rho}{\text{inter}} \ll 1$), this multi-provider deployment expands the effective ensemble sample size $M{\text{eff}}$ per Equation (25). The production trial will empirically benchmark whether the resulting gains in epistemic robustness justify the associated wall-clock synchronization latency (bounded by the slowest provider), cross-API failure modes, and heterogeneous FinOps token costs.
  5. Exogenous Axiom Misattribution and Provenance Friction: In sparse strategic corpora, separating genuine exogenous axioms (primitive operational constraints requiring no internal textual ancestors) from unanchored orphan claims relies on explicit document bounding. If an author introduces implicit domain premises or industry-standard baseline axioms without physical citations in the source text, the closed-world lexical null hypothesis flags them as unverified orphans ($\lambda_i = 0$). While this behavior mathematically adheres to Toulmin's requirement for explicit evidentiary warrants, it introduces provenance friction in domains where shared common-sense assumptions are standard practice, necessitating explicit axiomatic white-listing or input provenance declaration.
  6. Rigid BARS Scoring and Perceived Excess Punitive Calibration: Calibrated BARS power-curve damping ($\gamma = 1.25 \dots 1.5071$, corresponding to $\zeta \in [50, 70]$) yields conservative capability scores under enterprise zero-trust rubrics. While our empirical production trials executed at baseline strictness $\zeta = 0$ ($\gamma = 1.00$) to evaluate unattenuated raw model behavior, deploying non-linear damping in live organizational environments can lead human operators to perceive score compression at lower tiers as excessively punitive without peer normalization. In the empirical paired trials across both human–AI evaluation cases (the Remote Work policy case and the Strategic Foresight / Sitra case), normalized matrix scores ranged from $0.0\%$ to $61.9\%$ with stable inter-run consistency (MAD $3.05–3.99$ points). To remain interpretable across diverse user populations, raw BARS scores require supplementary cohort percentile calibration that contextualizes diagnostic results against normalized institutional baselines.
  7. The Enthymeme Boundary and the Semantic Entailment Gap: Natural discourse is inherently elliptical and enthymematic, frequently omitting unstated common-sense warrants. Quorum's deterministic guarantees are strictly confined to physical citation provenance ($\lambda \in {0, 1}$), as universal semantic entailment is bounded by the semantic entailment gap (see Section 2.1). Residual semantic validity is bounded stochastically by role-asymmetric Popperian falsification ($\beta_{\text{sem}}$) and isolated through discrete ATMS reachability pruning.
  8. Vulnerability to the "Illusion of Control" via Prompt Sanitization: As demonstrated across both empirical audits (the Remote Work policy trial and the Strategic Foresight / Sitra trial), human users may operate under the cognitive assumption that formulating concise, jargon-free prompts guarantees analytically rigorous output. However, this clean surface form (specifically zero mechanical phrase load) can mask unreflective routine delegation wherein the AI's first associative draft is accepted without counterfactual testing, boundary specification, or trade-off evaluation. While Quorum's Human Agency & Collaboration Matrix ($\mathcal{M}{\text{HACM}}$) and Agency-to-Outcome Divergence ($\Delta{\text{agency-outcome}}$) explicitly diagnose this form-to-content disparity, automated diagnostic evaluation cannot substitute for the operator's active willingness to engage in critical cognitive steering.
  9. Episodic Identifier Aliasing, Attention Economics, and Fail-Fast State Hydration: While Section 2.1 formalizes the bijective mapping $\mu: \mathcal{I}{\text{UUID}} \longleftrightarrow \mathcal{V}{\text{alias}}$, maintaining distributed referential integrity requires strict lifecycle isolation. In Quorum, alias mappings are strictly scoped per execution instance to prevent cross-tenant state pollution. When execution is distributed across asynchronous worker nodes, the mapping state is serialized into an immutable manifest transported within execution metadata. The worker reconstitutes the bijection and executes strict fail-fast validation: any hallucinated alias matching an active prefix that does not exist in the manifest immediately halts execution with an unrecoverable validation error, preventing corrupted foreign keys from entering persistent graph state.
  10. Design-Time Rubric Compilation Overhead (Cold-Start Engineering Cost): Unlike zero-shot LLM-as-a-Judge paradigms that evaluate arbitrary tasks via ad-hoc natural language instructions, Quorum's epistemic guarantees require pre-compiled, version-controlled BARS matrices ($N = 110$ criteria in our benchmark) with explicit positive capability anchors ($\pi_i = +1$) and contrastive anti-pattern distractors ($\pi_i = -1$). While this design-time human curation is mathematically necessary to bound the semantic entailment gap (Section 2.1) and maintain longitudinal psychometric invariance (Section 5.4.4), it introduces an upfront domain-engineering cost when onboarding novel specialized verticals. Quorum mitigates this cold-start overhead by separating domain-agnostic process and structural matrices ($\mathcal{M}{\text{HACM}}, \mathcal{M}{\text{Toulmin}}, \mathcal{M}{\text{Causal}}, \mathcal{M}{\text{Bloom}}$)—which transfer invariant epistemological standards across workflows with zero modification—from the task-specific substance matrix ($\mathcal{M}_{\text{Domain}}$). Domain architects instantiate new audit workflows by authoring only the localized domain module (typically requiring 2–4 hours of expert specification rather than weeks of model fine-tuning), after which automated schema verification suites ensure physical anchorability.

docs.title: 10.1. Summary of Architectural Trade-Offs and System Mitigations
docs.text:
To provide a consolidated reference for system architects and regulatory auditors, Table 8 synthesizes the fundamental engineering trade-offs inherent in Quorum's neurosymbolic architecture, mapping each mechanism to its design trade-off, empirical boundary observed in trials, and system mitigation:
