If any record fails validation, the process halts immediately with an explicit validation error, leaving PostgreSQL 19 tables untouched. - Authoritative Relational Upsert & 10-Table Count Verification: Once in-memory validation succeeds, the seeder opens an atomic QuorumUnitOfWork transaction and executes parameterized $1, $2 batch upserts (seed_collection_batch) across all 7 seeded tables (organizations, users, system_configs, prompt_blocks, steps, workflows, output_profiles), followed by verify_seed_table_counts across all 10 core PostgreSQL 19 tables (organizations, users, system_configs, prompt_blocks, steps, workflows, output_profiles, executions, report_artifacts, report_binaries), failing fast with AppException if any of the 7 seeded tables reports zero rows.

docs.title: 2.5. Atomic Master Seed Persistence & PostgreSQL 19 ACID/MVCC Concurrency
docs.text: Master seed file persistence and runtime database storage enforce atomic durability and transactional concurrency: - Temporary Replacement Writes: Master seed file persistence writes serialized JSON to isolated temporary files, flushes and synchronizes disk buffers (os.fsync), verifies complete re-loadability in memory, and replaces the target file via atomic OS replacement operations. - PostgreSQL 19 ACID Transactions & MVCC: Runtime database concurrency relies exclusively on PostgreSQL 19 ACID transactions (repeatable_read isolation in PostgresUnitOfWork) and Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) over asyncpg connection pools, eliminating OS-level file locking across concurrent execution runs.

docs.title: 2.6. Single-Entity Router SSOT, Universal Blueprint CRUD + Clone Lifecycle & Three-Layer Delete Protection
docs.text: Runtime persistence repositories and ingress API routers maintain ontology state through a single-entity router topology and a standardized lifecycle contract: - Single-Entity Router Sovereignty (1 Entity = 1 Router SSOT): Every domain entity possesses one authoritative API router mounted at a single canonical /api/v2/... endpoint prefix. Route handlers for a single entity never split across separate router packages, never attach duplicate shadow route decorators, and never mount simultaneously under multiple prefixes or legacy /api/v1 paths. Automated OpenAPI route-table verification enforces zero /api/v1 routes, zero doubled /api/v2/system/system prefixes, zero shadow prefixes (/api/v2/execution/reports, /api/v2/execution/workflows, /api/v2/studio/profiles, /api/v2/studio/system-configs), and zero duplicate path-and-method combinations across the application. - Standardized 5-Operation CRUD + Draft + Clone Blueprint Contract: All six configurable ontology blueprint entities—specifically and exhaustively: Workflow (/api/v2/studio/workflows, including GET /{id}/ui_schema, simulation, and extension discovery), Step (/api/v2/studio/steps), PromptBlock (/api/v2/studio/prompt-blocks), OutputProfile (/api/v2/output-profiles), SystemConfigModelRegistry (/api/v2/studio/model-registry), and SystemConfigMCPGateways (/api/v2/studio/mcp-gateways)—expose the complete 5-operation lifecycle (GET /, POST /, GET /{id}, PUT /{id}, DELETE /{id}, and POST /{id}/clone): 1. HTTP Boundary Identifier & Payload Parity: Path parameters bind OPAQUE_STRIPE_ID_REGEX (^([a-z]{2,5})_[a-fA-F0-9]{32}$) at the router boundary, and PUT /{id} endpoints enforce Fail-Fast ErrorCodes.ID_MISMATCH (400) validation before delegating to the service layer. 2. Dynamic Polymorphic Draft Instantiation: POST /api/v2/studio/prompt-blocks/ accepts a typed category_id: PromptBlockCategory query parameter (defaulting to PromptBlockCategory.SYSTEM_RULE). Requesting category_id=PromptBlockCategory.MATRIX dynamically instantiates a valid MatrixPromptBlock draft with an initial MatrixScale(score=1) level, enabling interactive creation of both system rules and evaluation matrices in Quorum Studio. 3. Immutable Entity Cloning & Specialist Step Unlocking: POST /{id}/clone executes pure .model_copy(update={...}) with a freshly generated 32-hex RFC 9562 UUIDv7 identifier (generate_opaque_id(EntityPrefix.<TYPE>)), localized copy suffix (original.name.with_copy_suffix()), and zero dictionary round-trips. Cloning a Step resets is_system_core=False while preserving its informational slug, allowing authors to clone locked system-core steps into freely editable and deletable specialist step blueprints. 4. Forensic & Identity Demarcation: Entities governed by append-only forensic immutability or identity uniqueness—specifically ExecutionRecord, ReportArtifact, User, and Organization—never expose /clone endpoints, operating instead through deterministic state-machine transitions within their respective single-entity routers. - Three-Layer Fail-Fast Delete Protection: All blueprint DELETE /{id} operations enforce three sequential verification layers before repository deletion: 1. Layer 1 (RBAC & Tenant Isolation — 403 PermissionDeniedError): Blocks MEMBER and VIEWER roles, cross-tenant deletions, and any non-ROOT attempt to mutate or delete ROOT_SYSTEM entities (allow_system=False on SystemConfigMCPGateways and SystemConfigModelRegistry). 2. Layer 2 (System-Core & Cardinality Guard — 403 ErrorCodes.SYSTEM_PROTECTED_RESOURCE): Blocks deletion of foundational steps (Step.is_system_core == True), protocol prompt blocks (PromptBlockCategory.PROTOCOL when not force_delete), and the last remaining SystemConfigModelRegistry. 3. Layer 3 (Referential Integrity Guard — 400 ErrorCodes.DELETE_BLOCKED_BY_USAGE): Blocks deletion of any Step actively referenced in Workflow.steps (rule.task_blueprint), any PromptBlock or MatrixPromptBlock referenced in V2 Step fields (role_block_id, extraction_protocol_block_id, execution_persona_block_id, criteria_block_ids), or any OutputProfile configured as Workflow.default_profile_id. - In-Place Upsert & Polyfactory Identifier Parity: Runtime persistence repositories maintain state through in-place atomic upsert operations keyed by canonical Opaque Stripe IDs without creating duplicate shadow instances. Authoritative PostgreSQL 19 seeded entity prefixes (EntityPrefix.WORKFLOW, EntityPrefix.OUTPUT_PROFILE, EntityPrefix.PROMPT_BLOCK, EntityPrefix.STEP, EntityPrefix.EXECUTION, EntityPrefix.REPORT, EntityPrefix.ORGANIZATION) are aligned 1:1 with centralized Polyfactory test model factories (WorkflowFactory, SystemRulePromptBlockFactory, OutputProfileFactory, MatrixPromptBlockFactory, ExecutionStepFactory, ExecutionRecordFactory, and ReportArtifactFactory), routing all generated entity and organization identifiers exclusively through generate_opaque_id(EntityPrefix.<TYPE>) and enforcing canonical 32-character lowercase hexadecimal RFC 9562 UUIDv7 Opaque Stripe ID formatting (^([a-z]{2,5})_[a-fA-F0-9]{32}$) under static AST guardrail QGR030 across both production and test suites.

docs.title: 2.7. Y-Funnel Pre-Hook Normalization
docs.text: Data transformations during initialization utilize a Y-Funnel architecture where pre-hooks normalize heterogeneous input shapes before domain validation. This keeps core Pydantic V2 domain models pure and focused strictly on business invariants rather than ingestion gymnastics.

docs.title: 2.8. Semantic Localization via Performative Lexicons
docs.text: System personality traits, terminology standards, and vocabulary constraints are governed as data rather than code. Declarative lexicons defined in seed data are injected dynamically during prompt compilation, supporting multilingual enforcement without code modifications.

docs.title: 2.9. Universal Bilingual Localization (I18nText)
docs.text: User-facing dynamic strings across the ontology (profile titles, layout descriptions, preambles) utilize the strictly typed I18nText model in both Python and Flutter. The schema mandates complete baseline translations (en and target locale) with structured fallback resolution, ensuring bilingual parity across backend services, frontend widgets, and PDF generators.

docs.title: 2.10. Workflow Context Governance & Step Protection
docs.text: Pipeline step definitions declare explicit system core protections (is_system_core: true) for foundational operations (document ingestion, scoring, synthesis, forensic reporting). Studio interface and API guardrails prevent unauthorized deletion or mutation of protected resources. Step blueprints (Step) and workflow step rules (NodeStrategy) embed an authoritative StepZone enum (zone_a, zone_b, zone_c), establishing 1:1 cross-language enum parity between backend and frontend. Steps in Zone A govern raw document ingestion (with deletion locked), Zone B hosts dynamic analytical specialists, and Zone C anchors downstream aggregation funnels (scoring, synthesis, XAI reporting). This server-driven zone classification powers Dumb Painter presentation in Quorum Studio with zero heuristic branching or client-side index calculations. Step definitions additionally declare synthesis source flags (is_synthesis_source), enabling deterministic context boundary governance between upstream text extraction and downstream qualitative synthesis.

docs.title: 2.11. Epistemic Separation (TheoryGrounding SSOT)
docs.text: Bibliographic references and academic provenance metadata are strictly decoupled from operational prompting instructions. PromptBlock.theory_grounding (TheoryGrounding) is the sole Single Source of Truth for academic citations (citation_reference) and source URLs (source_url). PromptBlock.ai_description contains purely operational prompt text, allowing presentation layers and PDF reports to consume structured academic citations without prompt-scraping or token bloat.

docs.title: 2.12. Structured Few-Shot Calibration Schema (ContrastivePairDTO)
docs.text: Evaluation assertions and rubrics across the ontology define structured few-shot grounding via ContrastivePairDTO, encapsulating acceptable and rejected exemplars with enforced minimum length boundaries and equality conflict rejection. This eliminates unstructured string delimiters and manual prefix conventions from the seed vault, guaranteeing that every matrix atom provides a pristine, strongly typed boundary definition ready for prompt compilation and direct production deployment across all environments without runtime parsing shims.

docs.title: 2.13. Matrix Seed Vault Hardening & Anti-Pattern Standards
docs.text: High-entropy evaluation atoms across the 14 canonical matrices enforce deterministic anti-patterns and disambiguated multi-step acceptance criteria to eliminate subjective evaluation drift: - Scaffolding and Prompt Parameter Disqualification: Explicit anti-patterns disqualify user task briefings, problem constraints, headcount allocations, and external AI dispatch instructions from satisfying cognitive competence criteria. - Cognitive Theory Hardening: Atoms evaluating Bloom's Revised Taxonomy and Kahneman's Dual Process Theory enforce rigorous ontological boundaries. System 1 claims require demonstrated rule-of-thumb judgment rather than textbook definitions, while System 2 claims require active step-by-step cognitive calculation rather than passive retrospective review. - Multi-Step Deductive Criteria: High-entropy triage atoms specify sequential acceptance criteria requiring multi-stage causal mediators and empirical scrutiny of proxy performance indicators, ensuring consistent interpretation across multi-provider evaluation fleets.

docs.title: 2.14. Dual-Track Matrix Schema & TDA Assertion Polarity Standards
docs.text: All 15 canonical matrices in the seed vault inherit from PromptBlockBase as strongly typed MatrixPromptBlock entities (category_id: "matrix", type: "float"), organizing assessment criteria into hierarchical MatrixScale levels containing Test-Driven Assertion (TDAAssertion) models: - MatrixPromptBlock Structure: Defines scale extrema (computed_min, computed_max), localizable labels (I18nText), target evidence inputs (target_input_key: product_text, chat_log, or all), academic theory grounding (TheoryGrounding), evaluative scoring participation (is_evaluative: bool), and an ordered collection of MatrixScale objects (scales). - Evaluative Scoring Participation (is_evaluative: bool) & Relational Identifier Invariant: - Opaque Identifier Relational Invariant: Entity slugs (specifically: matrix_bloom, matrix_toulmin) are strictly human-readable diagnostic labels and editorial aliases. Slugs MUST NEVER be used as relational keys, foreign keys, step criteria references (criteria_block_ids), output profile selectors (variance_target_block), or state dictionary keys (evaluative_matrices). ALL relational bindings and state transit across the system are keyed strictly and sovereignly by canonical opaque block IDs (blk_...). - Evaluative Matrices (10 matrices, is_evaluative: true): Directly participate in the global holistic score average (global_score). Encompasses 4 Track A developmental matrices (blk_f921c7c0989b47e8 [Bloom], blk_f6e286f050c94d60 [TaskXAI Clarity], blk_7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e [HACM], blk_c0a1e50000000001 [Causal Cohesion]) and 6 Track B diagnostic matrices (blk_440a5fef9331451b [Toulmin], blk_109dab5b6b3f403a [Kahneman], blk_c5804a9143c34cb1 [Causal Analyst], blk_b476f89fb732448c [Falsifier], blk_22e3598e06414409 [Epistemic Humility], blk_c3bc5f3eb8e74110 [Causal & Abductive Integrity]). - Specialized Role Matrices (5 matrices, is_evaluative: false): Serve specialized non-averaging architectural functions: blk_53f32679aa514fcb [Goodhart] (Cartesian variance X-axis), blk_80732a33fe1947ee [Taskguard] (security containment guard triggering security_penalty), blk_fb15f8dcf23f4865 [Archivist] (statutory compliance checklist), blk_ff72c2d79edb4ebf [Supreme Adjudicator] (supervisory steering discipline), and blk_6b8c766185294f7e [XAI Reporter] (multi-specialist consensus reporting). - MatrixScale Hierarchy: Each scale level defines a numerical score (specifically 1 to 5, or 1 to 6 for Bloom), localized scale names (I18nText), an evaluator directive (ai_label), and constituent claims grouping underlying TDAAssertion criteria. - TDAAssertion Schema & Mandatory Polarity Constraints: - Track A (Developmental Competence Matrices: 7 matrices): Level 1 designates foundational Novice capability (Alustava / Noviisi / Tunnistava). All constituent TDA assertions enforce inverse_evidence: false and aggregation_mode: "ALL_MUST_COMPLY". Level 1 measures the presence of baseline capability and awards positive capability points. Higher levels build cumulatively under the Cumulative Guttman Invariant ($L_1 \subset L_2 \subset L_3 \subset L_4 \subset L_5$). Inverting Level 1 into an error detector is strictly prohibited (Inverted Rubric Paradox ban). - Track B (Diagnostic Error Radar Matrices: 8 matrices): Levels 1 and 2 operate strictly as error radars (Kriittinen virhe / Vakava harhaluulo / Fatal Flaw). All Level 1–2 TDA assertions enforce inverse_evidence: true and aggregation_mode: "EXISTS". Zero positive assertions are permitted on Levels 1–2. Under the Null Hypothesis, clean baseline passes on Levels 1–2 award zero positive capability points, while detected errors trigger deterministic malus deductions. Positive capability points accrue exclusively from affirmative criteria on Levels 3–5 (inverse_evidence: false), allowing evaluative Track B matrices to achieve up to 100% normalized scores feeding directly into global_score.

docs.title: 2.15. Deterministic Causal Cohesion Metric Matrix & Holistic Workflow Topology
docs.text: The static ontology includes pure system-evaluated metric matrices that assess structural reasoning rather than LLM text generation. The Causal Cohesion BARS Matrix (matrix_causal_cohesion, blk_c0a1e50000000001) defines a 5-level developmental competence scale evaluated deterministically from graph telemetry: - 0-Token Execution Contract: The matrix is strictly excluded from LLM criteria_block_ids. It consumes topological graph metrics (logical_cohesion_score, cycle_detected, isolated_concept_count) directly from upstream causal discovery step outputs, eliminating model token consumption and latency overhead for structural graph scoring. - Topological BARS Grounding: Scale levels reflect structural reasoning integrity under the Cumulative Guttman Invariant ($L_1 \subset L_2 \subset L_3 \subset L_4 \subset L_5$). Cyclic dependencies trigger immediate defect grounding at Level 1 (Novice), and empty proposition graphs ground safely at the Novice floor without arithmetic faults. - Holistic Workflow Step Integration: Workflows integrate causal discovery as a first-class execution step positioned in Zone B, establishing causal provenance for downstream specialist steps and funneling structural cohesion scores into synthesis comparison groups.

docs.title: 2.16. Declarative MCP Gateway Ontology & Tool Capabilities
docs.text: External tool permissions and capabilities are configured declaratively in the static data vault under system_config (entity sys_8172bda70c8641c5): - Full-Duplex Contract Parity: Gateway configurations and tool definitions enforce 1:1 schema parity between backend SystemConfigMCPGateways / AllowedMCPTool and frontend SystemConfigMcpGatewaysDto / AllowedMcpTool models. Models define gateway transport types (MCPTransportType: STREAMABLE_HTTP, SSE), authentication methods (MCPAuthType: NONE, API_KEY, BEARER), endpoint URLs, and discovered tools with authoritative ToolCapability attributes (search, document_reader, action). - Recursive JSON Schema DTO Contracts: External tool parameters adhere to recursive schema definitions (MCPToolInputSchemaDTO and MCPToolSchemaPropertyDTO), completely eradicating untyped JSON dictionaries across tool contracts. - Namespaced Tool Declarations: Tools are declared under deterministic namespaced aliases combining gateway slug and tool identifier (specifically: {gateway_slug}__{tool_id}), preventing naming collisions across independent gateway providers. - Dynamic Studio Governance: Tool definitions expose bilingual labels, live discovery actions, schema preview tables, and per-tool allowlist toggles in Quorum Studio, enabling administrators to configure and constrain external MCP capabilities per gateway with immediate schema validation. - Authoritative Seeding & Lossless lz4-Compressed JSONB Persistence: System configuration documents (specifically and exhaustively: SystemConfigMCPGateways, SystemConfigModelRegistry, and SystemSettingsDTO) are seeded into the system_configs table with canonical opaque stripe IDs (sys_...) via seed_collection_batch and reconstituted via polymorphic AnySystemConfig validation. Step-level tool bindings and parameter overrides (allowed_mcp_tools and mcp_tool_params) are persisted on steps, and runtime tool audit traces (MCPAuditTrace) are persisted inside executions.trace_events and executions.execution_trace using lz4-compressed JSONB columns serialized via the binary pydantic_core \x01 codec with zero schema loss.

docs.title: 3. Logical Data Flow
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Central Static Data Vault] --> B[Two-Phase Pre-Flight In-Memory Verification]
    B -- Schema Violation --> C[Fail-Fast & Abort Seeding]
    B -- 100% Valid --> D[Atomic Persistence & Reseed Engine]
    D --> E{Polymorphic Router}
    E -- Type: system_config --> F[System Config Registries]
    E -- Type: prompt_blocks --> G[AnyPromptBlock Domain Union]
    E -- Type: steps --> H[Step Blueprints & Governance]
    E -- Type: workflows --> I[DAG Orchestrator Workflows]
    E -- Type: output_profiles --> J[Output Profile Layouts]
    F & G & H & I & J --> K[Repository Reconstitution & In-Place Upsert Layer]
    K --> L[In-Memory / Database State]
    L --> M[Cognitive Execution Engine]

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: The Cognitive Orchestration Engine capability is the computational "Brain" of the Compound AI System. It is responsible for taking declarative ontology from the database (PromptBlocks, Workflows, Steps, OutputProfiles), binding it with validated user input, and executing it against foundational language models. This capability is engineered for deterministic reasoning, fault tolerance, low latency, and prefix-matching context caching, utilizing parallel consensus patterns, acyclic topological graph execution, and multi-tier output governance to guarantee robust operation across model providers.

docs.title: 2. Architectural Mechanisms & Invariants
docs.text: The Cognitive Orchestration Engine combines declarative database ontology with runtime state to execute tasks against foundational language models:

docs.title: 2.1. Consensus Evaluation via Best-of-Three Flash
docs.text: Critical reasoning and evaluation tasks dispatch three concurrent lightweight LLM requests (utilizing the fast strategy tier) wrapped in a structured asyncio.TaskGroup. The system aggregates the parallel responses and resolves the outcome through 2/3 majority consensus: - Consensus Resolution: Requires at least two valid results out of three parallel calls, establishing consensus whenever a 2/3 majority is reached. - Epistemic Null Hypothesis Tie-Breaker: For inconclusive split votes (specifically: 1 PASS, 1 FAIL, 1 ERROR), the tie is resolved using an $O(1)$ polarity mapping (is_inverse_map). Inverse assertions (is_inverse=True, evaluating the absence of error) resolve to PASSED under the presumption of innocence, while standard positive assertions (is_inverse=False, requiring affirmative proof) resolve to FAILED under the Null Hypothesis. - Forensic Guarantee: Preserves valid evidence quotes on winning consensus while strictly forbidding quote hallucination on tie-broken or failed atoms.

docs.title: 2.2. Provider-Agnostic Static-First Context Caching
docs.text: To maximize context cache survival across foundational model providers (specifically Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI), prompt compilers assemble context payloads using a strict "Static-First, Dynamic-Last" topology. Static components (system instructions, structural schemas, performative lexicons, and source texts) are positioned at the beginning of the prompt as an unbroken, mathematically identical prefix. Dynamic data (execution variables, dynamic parameters, and atom queries) is placed at the absolute end of the payload within dedicated <execution_parameters> or <user_payload> blocks. The caching layer computes deterministic SHA-256 composite signatures across the static prefix to verify cache hits across requests. Cache lifecycles are hoisted to the orchestrator layer (pre-caching documents before entering parallel tasks, with teardown wrapped in a try...finally block after task completion) to prevent premature cache eviction during concurrent execution.

docs.title: 2.3. Unified Model Multiplexing & Sovereign Provider Routing
docs.text: Domain services do not hardcode specific model strings, provider SDKs, or vendor-specific API parameters. All requests route through a centralized, database-driven Model Registry: - Abstract Cognitive Tiers: Services request performance tiers (fast, balanced, deep, reasoning), and the registry dynamically resolves the active provider adapter, temperature, top_p, and routing configuration from database system configuration (SystemConfigModelRegistry). - Sovereign Provider Decoupling: Google Cloud Vertex AI (LLMProvider.VERTEX_AI) and Google AI Studio (LLMProvider.AI_STUDIO) are completely decoupled across models, settings, adapters, and UI. Vertex AI routes through GCP Application Default Credentials (ADC) with explicit regional routing (europe-north1 Hamina in production), while AI Studio routes through standalone environment keys (google_api_key). - Typed Relation Invariants: Provider resolution, adapter factory lookup (LLMCacheAdapterFactory), and credential binding are executed strictly via typed enum relations (provider_type: LLMProvider or config.provider). Substring parsing, keyword marker lists, and string-prefix heuristics (startswith("vertex_ai/")) are prohibited. - Provider Adapter Encapsulation: Vendor-specific behaviors (Vertex cached contents with distributed Redis locks via VertexAICacheAdapter, Google AI Studio caching via AIStudioCacheAdapter, Anthropic cache control headers, and OpenAI automatic caching) are encapsulated within concrete provider adapter implementations. - Live Model Garden Discovery Hub: Available models are discovered dynamically via LLMHandler. For Vertex AI, models are discovered via a two-stage dynamic query: Stage 1 queries Google's primary master catalog from settings.discovery_location (DISCOVERY_LOCATION in .env, defaulted and stored as us-central1) via client.models.list(config={'query_base': True}), and Stage 2 validates operational availability against the configured target region (settings.vertex_location, specifically europe-north1 Hamina) with resilient genai_errors.APIError handling that gracefully skips models not yet available in the target region without service disruption. For AI Studio and OpenAI, discovery queries their authoritative APIs directly. - Pricing Registry SSOT: Token unit rates and cost metrics are resolved strictly from the authoritative LiteLLM model pricing registry, providing unified FinOps cost accounting and savings estimates without secondary shadow pricing tables. - Observability & GenAI Semantic Conventions: Outbound model executions automatically trace under OpenTelemetry and Logfire semantic conventions, preserving active trace context across provider adapters, capturing unit token usage and latency metrics, recording explicit context cache hit indicators on active spans, and instrumenting external Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls. - Zero Silent Fallback Guarantee: If an API call fails, credentials are missing, or retry limits are exhausted, the engine halts immediately with an explicit AppException rather than silently substituting an alternate model, preserving longitudinal consistency and audit baselines. - Modular Provider Package Architecture: Foundational model execution and provider instantiation are partitioned across single-responsibility modules in the provider package: * Factory Resolution (provider_factory.py): Maps typed LLMProvider enums to concrete provider instances based on system configuration and model parameters. * Foundational LiteLLM Execution Engine (litellm_provider.py): Manages direct model interaction, dynamic RPM semaphore pooling, and pacing delays. * Response & Error Telemetry Stage (litellm_response_stage.py): Isolates response parsing, token usage extraction, and structured LiteLLM exception classification into typed AppException domain hierarchies. * Transient Retry & Backoff Policy (transient_retry_policy.py): Evaluates transient network and provider status codes (429, 500, 502, 503, 504), extracts Retry-After header specifications, and executes adaptive exponential jitter backoff. * Environment & Schema Adaptation (env_and_schema_utils.py): Enforces secure runtime environment variable injection with configuration validation and normalizes OpenAPI schemas for model tool calling. * Base & Mock Simulation (base_and_mock_provider.py): Defines the abstract LLMProvider contract and provides zero-deployment test simulation with simulated token tracking and structured validation. * Package Facade (__init__.py): Exposes public provider interfaces via explicit redundant PEP 484 exports.

docs.title: 2.4. Two-Tier Concurrency Architecture & Micro-Throttling Isolation
docs.text: Parallel execution enforces strict concurrency bounds across decoupled tiers: - Macro-Level Workflow Concurrency: Background workers in the Arq daemon govern simultaneous workflow execution jobs (settings.max_concurrent_workflows). - Micro-Level Provider Dynamic Throttling: The foundational model provider (LiteLLMProvider) manages an internal dynamic semaphore pool (semaphore_low_rpm_threshold, semaphore_low_rpm_limit, semaphore_max_concurrency, semaphore_rpm_divisor) based on provider RPM tiers, dynamically protecting external model APIs from rate-limit exhaustion. - Synthesis Fan-Out: Phase 2 parallel synthesis fan-out is governed by central limits (settings.max_concurrent_llm_steps). - Pure Stateless Computation: Execution engines (PromptEngine, SynthesisEngine, TDAEngine) and sub-executors operate as pure computational pipelines with zero semaphore or event primitives, eliminating recursive locks, lock starvation, and priority inversions under peak loads.

docs.title: 2.5. Data Ingestion & Context Preflight
docs.text: External inputs (documents, web resources, uploaded files, and conversational transcripts) are processed through dedicated ingestion providers that extract, sanitize, and flatten raw text. Before model execution, context preflight validates token consumption against window constraints, applying deterministic pagination and chunking where required to ensure that model input limits are never exceeded.

docs.title: Dynamic Input Provenance & Context Packaging
docs.text: Ingestion and prompt packaging adhere to dynamic input provenance without hardcoded document enums, fixed triads, or static file counts: - Dynamic Topology Agnosticism: Workflows configure arbitrary dynamic input keys (input_key: str). Processing pipelines support any number of inputs ($1, \dots, N$) deterministically. - Unconditional Ingress Directive Packaging: SourceDocumentPacker wraps every targeted dynamic input payload unconditionally in an <ai_context_directive document="{input_key}"> XML block. When input metadata lacks explicit descriptions or instructions, the directive envelope remains present with empty directive content, ensuring consistent document identification downstream. - Paragraph Directive Stripping & Provenance Tracking: In CausalDiscoveryEngine, incoming text is split into sequential paragraphs [B{i}]. Directive tags are stripped from emitted paragraph texts to prevent models from generating spurious claims from packaging headers, while each paragraph is tagged with its originating source_input_key. - Dynamic Role Resolution: Input roles and ownership boundaries are resolved dynamically via ExpectedInput schema attributes: * is_endorsed_deliverable: Marks candidate-authored work product, defining the subject population for deliverable subgraph induction and documentation volume metrics. * is_chat_history: Identifies conversational dialogue, separating candidate turns from assistant responses. * is_assignment: Quarantines evaluator task directives and task constraints into <assignment_context> capsules, preventing external normative instructions from being quoted as candidate work.

docs.title: 2.6. Two-Pass Atomization & Topological DAG Execution
docs.text: Complex evaluation workflows decompose tasks into atomic units and structured matrix assertions: 1. Pass 1 (Ontology Extraction): Extracts global domain entities, document themes, and semantic anchors into a unified GlobalOntologyMap injected into evaluation contexts. 2. Matrix Causal DAG (Pre-compiled Assertions): Operates on pre-compiled matrix assertions carrying pre-defined causal dependencies (FlattenedAtom.depends_on). Local chunk claim extraction (Pass 2) and the Sliding Window Linker operate as decoupled exploratory knowledge extraction services (specifically during RAG Preflight). These units form a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) whose dependencies, edge constraints, and topological order are resolved before dispatching to specialized cognitive engines.

docs.title: Document Paragraph Indexing & Boundary Monotonicity
docs.text: Ingested source text across discovery and preflight engines (CausalDiscoveryEngine, TDAEngine, RAGPreflightService) is indexed using strictly sequential, 0-indexed integer identifiers ([B{i}] {paragraph}). Because paragraph markers represent physical geometric positions rather than deduplicated domain entities, natural-language prose is never passed to AliasEngine for block registration. If an ingestion payload lacks valid paragraph structure, the engine triggers immediate Fail-Fast with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Content.

docs.title: Packet Boundary Defense & Fault-Tolerant Atom Filtering
docs.text: In TwoPassAtomizer, chunk packet boundaries enforce contiguous ranges (start_block_id to end_block_id), validated by format verification (key.startswith("B") and key[1:].isdigit()). When an extraction task produces an atom citing a block identifier outside the assigned packet bounds, TwoPassAtomizer logs a structured warning (corrupted_atom_dropped) and continues processing remaining valid atoms in the chunk rather than raising an unhandled ValueError that terminates the parallel asyncio.TaskGroup.

docs.title: Modular DAGExecutor Package & Two-Lock Concurrency State Isolation
docs.text: Macro DAG orchestration is partitioned across single-responsibility modules in the dag_executor package, isolating execution-scoped mutable state and dual lock primitives inside an explicit WorkflowExecutionState container (update_lock: asyncio.Lock for in-memory record and global context transitions, and commit_lock: asyncio.Lock for serialized repository checkpointing) while keeping DAGExecutor, NodeExecutor, and ExecutionCommitter stateless across concurrent coroutines: - Leaf Causal-TDA Fusion (causal_tda_fusion.py): Pure functions (transform_causal_nodes_to_atoms, compute_causal_tda_fusion_result) transforming causal discovery proposition nodes into FlattenedAtom instances and computing composite CausalTdaFusionResultDTO outputs (Visual XAI data projection, Root Cause Attribution via CausalCohesionEvaluator.diagnose_root_causes, Anti-Fluff Shield with Deliverable Subgraph Induction and Exogenous Boundary Axiom, Prescriptive Remediation, and Fair Scoring Deduplication). - Event-Sourced Persistence Committer (execution_committer.py): Encapsulates ExecutionCommitter.commit_trace, projecting and checkpointing Event-Sourced TraceEvent arrays and ExecutionRecord snapshots into persistent storage via NodeExecutionUpdateDTO.to_execution_update_dto(). - Isolated Single-Node Executor (node_executor.py): Encapsulates NodeExecutor and _hydrate_step_definition, executing individual workflow steps inside an OpenTelemetry dag.node.{step.id} span, filtering scoring post-hooks when no evaluative matrices exist, normalizing input_mappings via ContextRouter.normalize_and_validate_variable, resolving pure ExecutionEngine instances via build_execution_engine, enforcing execution quota (assert_quota), and routing runtime or validation failures to _dlq_record_node_error (ErrorTraceEvent). - Workflow Bootstrap & RAG Pre-Flight Stage (workflow_bootstrap_stage.py): Encapsulates WorkflowExecutionState, Dead Letter Queue helpers (dlq_record_step_failure, dlq_handle_progress_commit_error, dlq_fallback_step_exceptions), bootstrap_workflow_execution_state, safe_commit_execution_state, and execute_rag_preflight_stage (atomizing source documents into __GLOBAL_ATOM_BLACKBOARD__ via RAGPreflightService). - Step Preparation & Retry Wrapper Stage (step_execution_stage.py): Encapsulates prepare_step_strategy_context (injecting upstream causal discovery shuffled_atoms and gating MatrixReducer.reduce_matrix into __MATRIX_REDUCER_OUTPUT__) and execute_dag_step_wrapper (verifying upstream depends_on statuses, transitioning steps synchronously to ExecutionStatus.RUNNING, executing node_executor.execute inside a Tenacity AsyncRetrying transient LLM error loop with lock-guarded progress_callback updates under _update_lock = state.update_lock, and routing step failures to the Dead Letter Queue). - Post-Step Finalization & Topological Wave Orchestrator (wave_orchestrator_stage.py): Encapsulates finalize_step_output_and_commit and execute_topological_waves_stage along with focused wave helpers (_extract_evaluated_atoms, _commit_record_snapshot, _append_causal_fusion_and_cohesion_events, _merge_global_context_vars, _deduplicate_mcp_traces, _apply_step_events, _fail_wave_and_commit, _fail_running_steps), orchestrating Kahn topological waves inside asyncio.TaskGroup under the root OpenTelemetry span dag.orchestration. - Package Coordinator Facade (__init__.py): Exposes DAGExecutor as a pure coordinator delegating execute_workflow to bootstrap_workflow_execution_state and execute_topological_waves_stage, accompanied by explicit PEP 484 redundant re-exports (Symbol as Symbol and __all__).

docs.title: MatrixReducer Pre-Evaluation Gating
docs.text: In prepare_step_strategy_context (step_execution_stage.py), invocation of MatrixReducer.reduce_matrix(exec_record) is strictly gated on the presence of evaluated atoms across step execution records. If an execution terminates prior to atom evaluation (specifically during preflight validation failures), MatrixReducer is bypassed, eliminating synthetic empty reductions and duplicate execution warnings.

docs.title: Wave-Based Topological TaskGroup Execution & DLQ Recording
docs.text: Macro step execution within execute_topological_waves_stage (wave_orchestrator_stage.py) organizes workflow steps into Kahn's topological waves. Independent steps within each wave execute concurrently inside a structured asyncio.TaskGroup. When a step fails or is cancelled, the wave traps the failure via PEP 758 bracketless except* handlers, deterministically terminates sibling coroutines, transitions active wave steps to ExecutionStatus.FAILED (WAVE_TASKGROUP_CANCELLED) and downstream wave steps to ExecutionStatus.BLOCKED (DOWNSTREAM_WAVE_BLOCKED), and commits all cancelled and unreached steps to the Dead Letter Queue (DLQ) via dlq_record_step_failure, guaranteeing that no step remains stranded in an unresolved PENDING state.

docs.title: Atomic Step Transitions & Lock-Guarded State Synchronization
docs.text: All DAG step state transitions are centralized in the atomic ExecutionRecord.transition_step(step_id, status, progress, label, last_error, has_warning) method. Stage functions bind _update_lock = state.update_lock and acquire async with _update_lock: to atomically synchronize both the step_states mapping and the steps list representation in an immutable model copy without in-place mutation, while safe_commit_execution_state serializes repository writes under async with state.commit_lock:, eliminating split-brain desynchronization and lock starvation without holding update locks across network requests or database commits.

docs.title: Pure State Reduction, Event-Sourced Context Updates & Wave Propagation
docs.text: Post-hook cognitive updates and pipeline deltas are processed through pure functional state reduction (state_reducer.py). Hook deltas (specifically MatrixHookResultDTO and PassivityDetectionResultDTO) map directly into typed fields on GlobalContextVarsDTO (including evaluative_matrices and passivity_detected) and merge into ExecutionInputsDTO without untyped dictionary accumulators or wrapper classes. When cognitive state is updated, the reducer emits a decision TraceEvent carrying metadata.is_context_update = True. Within finalize_step_output_and_commit (wave_orchestrator_stage.py), the atomic _update_lock processes these events via _merge_global_context_vars, validates the incoming payload using GlobalContextVarsDTO.model_validate, updates state.global_context_vars, and commits them to ExecutionRecord.metadata.global_context_vars. Subsequent topological waves inherit this cumulative global context on their step HookState, ensuring deterministic, typed transit across wave boundaries. In LLMNodeStrategy, post-hook matrix scorecard outputs and evaluative matrices are preserved in the execution result to guarantee uninterrupted delivery to downstream domain parsers and state projectors.

docs.title: TopologicalEvaluator Wave Crash Recovery
docs.text: Micro-level graph evaluation within TopologicalEvaluator shields batch evaluation callbacks against unhandled exceptions. Catching BaseException (including ExceptionGroup, AppException, and runtime cancellations) during batch execution marks all pending nodes in that wave and all unreached downstream children as ExecutionStatus.SYSTEM_ERROR or ExecutionStatus.BLOCKED with explicit crash reasoning, guaranteeing that graph evaluation never halts in an unrecoverable corrupted zombie state. Nodes marked N_A, BLOCKED, or SYSTEM_ERROR are completely pruned from subsequent batch dispatch.

docs.title: Causal Cohesion BARS Evaluation & Idempotent DAG Fusion
docs.text: When a specialist step in Zone B binds an upstream causal discovery source (step_obj.causal_source_step_id), finalize_step_output_and_commit executes argument causal fusion via compute_causal_tda_fusion_result. Graph telemetry is evaluated into a unified BARS score through the pure, stateless service CausalCohesionEvaluator: - Canonical Universal Causal Blueprint, Direct Cohesion Matrix Binding & Dynamic Ingress Agnosticism: Causal discovery executes across workflows via the canonical causal discovery step (StepType.CAUSAL_DISCOVERY, engine_type: "causal_discovery"), designated as foundational system core (is_system_core: true). The step binds its BARS causal cohesion matrix (MatrixPromptBlock) directly in Step.criteria_block_ids, allowing Workflow.get_allowed_prompt_block_targets and wave finalization (_append_causal_fusion_and_cohesion_events) to resolve the cohesion matrix identifier and its five BARS TDAAssertion definitions directly from the hydrated step blueprint without side-channel parameters or hardcoded constants. Downstream Zone B specialist steps reference the causal discovery step via causal_source_step_id, ensuring that graph fusion and BARS evaluation operate on unified proposition graphs across all workflow topologies. - Server-Driven Step Segregation & Scope Filtering: Step blueprints and workflow steps are partitioned into specialist steps versus system core step definitions via the StepFilterScope SSOT enum (specialists, system_core, all). Workflow services and API routers perform server-side filtering, preventing foundational infrastructural steps from cluttering specialist authoring views while allowing comprehensive architectural inspection when needed. - Idempotent Evaluation Guard (state.evaluated_causal_sources): To prevent race conditions and duplicate atom emission during concurrent DAG waves, WorkflowExecutionState tracks evaluated causal sources within an execution-scoped evaluated_causal_sources set. When multiple Zone B specialist steps reference the same causal discovery source, cohesion evaluation executes exactly once. Subsequent steps reuse the upstream causal graph and fusion results without duplicate atom generation or execution trace pollution. - Topological BARS Scale Derivation & Counterfactual Retraction: CausalCohesionEvaluator maps zero-token topological metrics from AntiFluffAuditDTO (logical_cohesion_score, cycle_detected, isolated_concept_count, largest_component_ratio $r_{\text{LCC}}$, branch_convergence_ratio $r_{\text{conv}}$, and steering_coupling_ratio $\kappa_{\text{steer}}$) into BARS 1–5 scale levels. It enforces the Cumulative Guttman Invariant ($L_1 \subset L_2 \subset L_3 \subset L_4 \subset L_5$) against composite thresholds defined in central configuration (causal_cohesion_l2_threshold through causal_cohesion_l5_threshold, causal_cohesion_l2_min_nodes through causal_cohesion_l5_min_nodes, causal_cohesion_l2_lcc_min through causal_cohesion_l5_lcc_min, and causal_cohesion_l4_convergence_min). Cyclic dependencies ground the evaluation immediately at Level 1 (Novice), and zero-node graphs ground at the Novice floor without arithmetic faults. Additionally, CausalCohesionEvaluator.simulate_counterfactual_retraction executes deterministic $\mathcal{O}(|\mathcal{V}| + |\mathcal{E}|)$ breadth-first counterfactual retraction across conjunctive and disjunctive dependency semantics, returning an immutable CounterfactualSimulationResultDTO (retracted_root_id, collapsed_node_ids, surviving_node_ids, collapse_ratio, max_cascade_depth). - Atomic Context Reconciliation: Cohesion evaluation emits individual AtomResultDTO output events and a decision TraceEvent with metadata.is_context_update = True carrying GlobalContextVarsDTO(evaluative_matrices={matrix_id: score}). finalize_step_output_and_commit reconciles these updates within async with _update_lock: directly into state.global_context_vars and commits them to exec_record.metadata.global_context_vars without requiring state reducer mutations, ensuring subsequent topological waves inherit the cumulative global context deterministically.

docs.title: Bounded Deliverable Root Axiom Anchoring & Dual Fault Attribution
docs.text:
In autonomous causal discovery (SlidingWindowLinker), candidate root axioms originating from candidate-endorsed deliverables (InDegree(v) == 0) are identified and sorted deterministically by out-degree centrality and text sequence: $$\text{Rank}(v) = \langle -\text{OutDegree}(v), \text{atom_index}{\text{asc}} \rangle$$ Up to $K{\text{axiom}}^{\max} = 8$ top-ranked axioms are injected into a persistent --- GLOBAL CONTEXT ANCHORS (ROOT AXIOMS) --- header prepended to downstream chunk packets. To guarantee adequate context capacity for current-window proposition discovery, the effective root axiom quota $K_{\text{eff}}$ adapts dynamically to the current window size $W_{\text{current}}$: $$K_{\text{eff}} = \min(K_{\text{axiom}}^{\max}, \max(0, M_{\text{win}} - W_{\text{current}})), \quad W_{\text{min}} = 12, \quad M_{\text{win}} \le 20$$ reserving a guaranteed minimum quota $W_{\text{min}} = 12$ atoms for current-window claims while bounding total window size to $M_{\text{win}} \le 20$ atoms. Crucially, root axioms participate in pairwise dependency extraction in a single deterministic topological pass without recursive graph traversal, preserving the Local Causal Markov Condition and enabling long-range inferential links ($v_{\text{root}} \xrightarrow{\mathbf{W}} u_{\text{leaf}}$) across arbitrary document horizons.

Within CausalDiscoveryEngine, Algorithm 1 dual fault attribution separates primary node defects (NODE_FAILURE) from broken warrant grounding dependencies (WARRANT_GROUNDING_FAILURE). When a causal edge warrant fails lexical verification ($\lambda(\mathbf{W}) = 0$) while parent claims pass, the engine attributes the failure specifically to the grounding warrant rather than improperly penalizing the underlying parent proposition.

docs.title: Proposition Graph Draft-to-Persisted Wave Materialization & Toulmin SQL Falsification
docs.text: Relational proposition graph persistence separates in-memory LLM extraction drafts from persisted database entities and executes wave ingestion in a single database round-trip: - Draft vs. Persisted Domain Segregation: During in-memory wave computation, extracted claims and dependencies are modeled as immutable draft contracts (NodeDraft keyed by step-local local_key and EdgeDraft linking source_local_key to target_local_key with self-loop rejection). Only upon database materialization are drafts elevated into persisted PropositionNode (nod_...) and DependencyEdge (edg_...) models carrying database-assigned RFC 9562 uuidv7() identifiers. - Single-Round Multi-CTE Wave Ingestion (materialize_wave): PostgresGraphAdapter.materialize_wave ingests an entire Kahn topological wave of node and edge drafts in a single parameterized multi-CTE SQL statement (WITH upserted_nodes AS (...), resolved_edges AS (...), inserted_edges AS (...)). Node upserts leverage PostgreSQL 19 ON CONFLICT (run_id, local_key) DO SELECT FOR UPDATE RETURNING to resolve both newly inserted and pre-existing node UUID keys in one pass without secondary lookup round-trips, immediately mapping local keys to UUID foreign keys for quorum_edges. - Post-Wave QuorumUnitOfWork Atomic Commit: All parallel LLM inference inside asyncio.TaskGroup executes 100% in memory with zero held database connections. Once the wave completes, PostgresUnitOfWork opens an atomic repeatable_read transaction, executes materialize_wave or upsert_wave_batch, verifies DAG acyclicity via WITH RECURSIVE ... CYCLE (assert_acyclic, raising CycleDetectedError on cyclic dependencies), and commits atomically. - Toulmin Structural Falsification Queries (CteReasoningStrategy): CausalReasoningPort.find_falsified_claims executes a 3-way relational join across quorum_edges (relation_type = 'FALSIFIES') and quorum_nodes, identifying active claims (CLAIM, HYPOTHESIS, ASSUMPTION) contradicted by high-confidence falsifier nodes (confidence >= min_falsifier_confidence) and projecting results directly into immutable FalsifiedClaimMatch models.

docs.title: 2.7. Asynchronous Background Workers & Non-Blocking Handshake
docs.text: Workflows and report generation execute completely outside the synchronous HTTP request-response cycle across decoupled background workers: 1. The API Ingress router receives an execution request, initializes and persists the execution record with status=RUNNING, persists the frozen context snapshot, and enqueues the heavy DAG job to the asynchronous Redis-backed task queue (execute_workflow_task). 2. The router returns an immediate HTTP 202 Accepted response with the execution record, preventing thread blocking. 3. The client connects to an independent Server-Sent Events (SSE) stream (/executions/{id}/stream) to receive real-time execution progress, status updates, and trace events while background worker processes compute the graph. The streaming endpoint queries execution state in a lightweight mode (hydrate=False, skip_resumability=True) decoupled from heavy blob loading, serializes payloads with null-exclusion (exclude_none=True), and governs polling cadence via central configuration (settings.sse_polling_interval_seconds = 2.0).

docs.title: Worker Completion & Decoupled Lifecycle Sovereignty
docs.text: Upon completion of the execution DAG topological sort and final telemetry aggregation in the execution worker: - The execution worker transitions ExecutionRecord.status directly and unconditionally to ExecutionStatus.PASSED (or FAILED if unhandled execution exceptions occurred). - Synthetic presentation step injections (specifically sys_render_*) are completely eliminated from ExecutionRecord.steps and step_states, preserving 100% semantic purity of the physical step execution timeline. - If an output profile was specified at execution ingress, an independent report generation job is enqueued to the background queue (generate_report_artifact_job). This report job runs in isolation without blocking, delaying, or altering the finalized PASSED status of the execution record.

docs.title: Decoupled Worker Architecture
docs.text: Worker responsibilities follow strict Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) and Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) boundaries: - Execution Worker: Dedicated exclusively to heavy DAG computation, atom evaluations, consensus voting, and telemetry persistence. - Report Worker: Dedicated exclusively to qualitative synthesis and presentation compilation (SDUI JSON, PDF documents, and multi-tab Excel/CSV exports), persisting materialized ReportArtifact records via generate_report_artifact_job. - Worker Daemon Entrypoint: Serves strictly as the pure Arq daemon runtime entrypoint (WorkerSettings, startup, shutdown, health_check). All worker coroutines are imported directly from their sovereign modules.

docs.title: Sovereign Execution Services Subpackage
docs.text: Execution services follow single responsibility partitions (lifecycle_service.py, ingress_service.py, resumption_service.py, override_service.py, stream_service.py, context_service.py) unified by a sovereign ExecutionService facade. External service bridges (storage, blueprint, pdf generator) are decoupled and purged from the package entrypoint, ensuring that execution services interact directly with canonical external services.

docs.title: 2.8. Sensor Caching Parity & Enriched Context Caching
docs.text: The matrix sensor prompt compiler maintains $O(1)$ context cache efficiency across matrix assertion evaluations. It compiles global logic, matrix theory context, and large source documents into a static cache prefix, while dynamic, batch-specific assertion data is encapsulated in the dynamic user message. Parallel evaluation batches against the same source text achieve maximum cache hit rates.

docs.title: 2.9. Synthesis Payload Compression & Zero-Loss Epistemic Distillation
docs.text: Before qualitative text synthesis, execution states are distilled into compact payloads via dedicated synthesis payload compression: - Metadata Stripping: All raw context keys, internal signatures, and intermediate trace metadata are stripped from the payload. - Unbounded Default Epistemic Fidelity & Zero-Loss Lineage Retention: Central synthesis clipper settings (max_synthesis_evaluations, max_synthesis_reasoning_length, max_synthesis_quote_length, max_synthesis_quotes_per_matrix, and max_synthesis_unmet_criteria_per_matrix) default to 0 (0 = unbounded), preserving all four steps of ReasoningStepDTO (premise_analysis, evidence_mapping, contra_indications, conclusion) and verbatim quotes without mid-sentence truncation. Character or item slicing executes exclusively when a positive integer bound (> 0) is configured. Evaluations with ExecutionStatus.PASSED, ExecutionStatus.FAILED, ExecutionStatus.N_A, or is_inverse_evidence = True are retained in DistilledEvaluation regardless of whether exact_quotes is empty, preserving depends_on_tda_ids, short_circuit_reason_tda_ids, is_inverse_evidence, and topological_out_degree. - Topological Priority Token Shield Stratification: When a positive evaluation cap (limit > 0) is configured and evaluation counts exceed the threshold, the Token Shield protocol allocates a configurable fraction (synthesis_deficit_stratification_ratio, default 0.7) of the evaluation budget to critical deficits (FAILED, UNMET, NON_COMPLIANT, and N_A). Deficits are sorted deterministically by topological priority (-int(is_inverse_evidence), -topological_out_degree, len(short_circuit_reason_tda_ids), atom_id), prioritizing poison hits, high-blast-radius root bottlenecks, and first-hop short-circuits, while strengths are sorted by quote count and atom identifier (-len(exact_quotes), atom_id) with dynamic spillover and a final canonical sort by atom_id for byte-for-byte deterministic JSON serialization. - Fail-Fast Safeguard: If an execution payload becomes empty after compression, the system halts with an explicit validation error rather than allowing the model to hallucinate an empty report.

docs.title: 2.10. Synthesis Source Filtering & Analytical Context Protection
docs.text: Step definitions declare explicit synthesis source flags (is_synthesis_source: bool). The synthesis distillation pipeline strictly filters available source step DTOs, omitting unparsed raw document ingestion steps (is_synthesis_source: false) from text synthesis prompt envelopes. This preserves prompt token budgets exclusively for analytical specialist findings, preventing token saturation and attention dilution in the synthesis model.

docs.title: 2.11. Matrix Explanation Service & Evidence Curation
docs.text: Matrix evaluations and qualitative explanation assembly are isolated within a dedicated matrix explanation service: - Tripartite Configuration Resolution: Resolves quote and unmet criteria limits following priority order: Output Profile configuration override -> Global settings default. - Evidence Curation: Curates supporting evidence using ranked round-robin selection across behavioral claims ranked by quote length, with candidate pre-deduplication to prevent single-claim and deduplication starvation. - Contrastive Deficit & Transitive Blame Curation: For matrices where raw_score < float(computed_max), curates structured MatrixFailureDeficitDTO items across all ExecutionStatus.FAILED and ExecutionStatus.N_A evaluations, sorted in ascending scale_score order with alphabetical tie-breaking on claim label. Each deficit preserves full cognitive evaluation_reasoning, is_inverse_evidence poison-hit status, transitive parent-to-child short-circuit lineage ([Blocked Claim] <-- SHORT-CIRCUITED BY PREREQUISITE FAILURE: [Parent Claim: <parent evaluation_reasoning>]) in short_circuited_by_claims, anti_patterns, and ContrastivePairDTO exemplars (contrastive_rejected, contrastive_acceptable). - Direct Rust Serialization: Enforces direct C/Rust serialization via a dedicated list TypeAdapter to eliminate double-serialization overhead in background workers.

docs.title: 2.12. Two-Tier Length Budgeting & Sentence Boundary Preservation
docs.text: Output volume and semantic coherence are governed through a two-tier length budgeting architecture: - Tier 1 (Prompt-Level Single Section Budget Sovereignty & Four-Task Causal Fan-Out): Five canonical section budgets configured on the output profile (synthesis_length_constraint, matrix_graph_length_constraint, row_explanation_length_constraint, xai_length_constraint, and variance_length_constraint) are compiled into task-specific <section_budget> XML boundaries when greater than 0 (and omitted when 0 or None for unbounded generation) without any conflicting global length constraint in base_dynamic_parts. Concurrently, the synthesis worker constructs a unified CausalSynthesisBriefDTO combining resolved CausalRootCauseDiagnosisDTO chains (root_cause_claim -> failing_node_claim (warrant_relation)), 3-way Toulmin falsifications (FalsifiedClaimMatch: rebuttal_claim -> invalidated_warrant -> falsified_claim), prescriptive remediations, and post-hoc fidelity and fair-scoring penalties, fanning out the formatted <causal_diagnosis> payload and a shared CognitiveTier.BALANCED LLMClient instance across all four parallel synthesis tasks (create_executive_summary_task, create_matrix_sections_tasks, create_xai_highlights_task, and create_row_explanations_task), governed by CAUSAL_TDA_DIAGNOSIS_MANDATE and CONTRASTIVE_FRONTIER_MANDATE. - Tier 2 (Post-Generation Sentence Boundary Guardrail): If generated text exceeds the maximum character budget, a dedicated length budget enforcer scans backwards within a [60%, 100%] window of the budget ceiling to locate the nearest terminal punctuation (., !, ?). This trims the output cleanly at a valid sentence boundary, preventing mid-sentence and mid-word slicing while strictly respecting the character ceiling. If a required section synthesis directive or budget configuration is absent for a given profile layout, the worker logs a structured warning and gracefully omits that specific synthesis generation task without halting the pipeline or falling back to hardcoded defaults.

docs.title: 2.13. Epistemic Separation in Prompt Compilation
docs.text: Prompt assembly strictly separates operational directives from bibliographic metadata: - Operational Directives: Standard prompt blocks extract purely operational instruction text (ai_description), excluding raw URLs and citations from runtime prompt bodies to prevent token bloat and attention distraction. - Academic Grounding: For matrix evaluations, academic references are injected as clean semantic context blocks (<theory_context>), derived exclusively from PromptBlock.theory_grounding (TheoryGrounding), activating the model's pre-trained conceptual representations without including un-actionable URL strings.

docs.title: 2.14. ExecutionEngine Protocol & Strategy Dispatch
docs.text: DAG node execution decouples macro-level routing from micro-level execution pipelines: - ExecutionEngine Protocol: The orchestrator delegates tasks to specialized engines conforming to the ExecutionEngine protocol: - TDAEngine: Evaluates matrix assertions and extractive sensor rules. - SynthesisEngine: Generates structured profile syntheses and qualitative narratives. - PromptEngine: Executes standard non-matrix structured steps. - CausalDiscoveryEngine: Extracts structured argument propositions and causal dependency graphs from unstructured text. - Pure Compute Engine Model: Execution engines and sub-executors are 100% pure computational pipelines with zero semaphore or event dependencies. Step dispatch transitions lifecycle status (ExecutionStatus.RUNNING) synchronously upon node dispatch, while concurrency limits are isolated exclusively to worker and provider layers. - Orthogonal Strategy Decoupling: NodeStrategyFactory resolves node strategies via NODE_STRATEGY_REGISTRY mapping StepType to StrategyBuilder protocols (StepType.LLM and StepType.CAUSAL_DISCOVERY to LLMNodeStrategy, and StepType.LOGIC to LogicNodeStrategy) while enforcing non-null ExecutionEngine instances for language model and causal discovery nodes, whereas model tier resolution (fast, reasoning, deep) is handled orthogonally by the model router. Any execution engine can run with any model strategy tier without altering underlying dispatch logic. All engines communicate via strict immutable request and result DTOs (EngineExecutionRequest and EngineExecutionResult) with zero permissive typing. - Four-Stage LLMNodeStrategy Execution Pipeline: For language model workflow nodes, LLMNodeStrategy coordinates execution as a stateless facade delegating sequentially across four isolated pipeline stages and focused private helpers (<= 50 lines per function) communicating through immutable frozen stage and intermediate containers: 1. Blueprint Resolution, Pre-Hooks & Context Metadata (BlueprintStageResult): Unpacks targeted source documents via SourceDocumentPacker, validates the step blueprint (Step), executes step pre-hooks via HookState and HookDependencies, resolves optional role, extraction protocol, and execution persona prompt blocks alongside mandatory criteria prompt blocks (criteria_block_ids), and resolves the target OutputProfile and target locale directly from hydrated repository domain models. 2. Context Building, Prompt Compilation & Dynamic Schema (PromptAndSchemaStageResult): Resolves the workflow schema_map and localized blueprint_labels, builds the execution context via ContextBuilder.build, enforces fail-fast validation that matrix steps carry non-empty shuffled_atoms, compiles the static system prompt and dynamic user payload via PromptFactory.build and AliasEngine, appends <execution_parameters> (tone_instruction and JSON-serialized matrix_synthesis_groups) to the user payload tail, chunks matrix atoms via ChunkingService.chunk_payload, validates SourceDocumentContext models on ExecutionRecord via direct isinstance(exec_obj, ExecutionRecord) verification, and compiles upfront dynamic Pydantic schemas when FrozenContext is present. 3. Client Binding, MCP Retrieval & Bounded Engine Retry (EngineRetryStageResult): Validates mandatory cognitive_tier and binds LLMClient.from_tier, executes optional pre-execution Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool retrieval (execute_mcp_retrieval) into an immutable _MCPRetrievalEnrichment container enriching both the user payload and source text with <mcp_evidence>, prepares the invocation via _PreparedEngineInvocation and constructs EngineExecutionRequest (building MatrixEvaluationContext for matrix steps and dynamically compiling response schemas and LLMMessageDTO sequences for synthesis and non-matrix steps), invokes engine.execute, runs step post-hooks into _PostHooksExecutionOutcome while preserving _evaluative_matrices and evaluative_matrices, and executes a bounded anomaly retry loop (llm_anomaly_retry_requested) up to settings.llm_max_retries while persisting ExecutionStatus.RUNNING and event_llm_anomaly_retry on ExecutionRecord via ExecutionUpdateDTO. 4. Telemetry Merging & TraceEvent Assembly (build_llm_step_trace_events): Validates non-empty step.id, reconstitutes and merges StepTraceMetadataDTO from pre-hook and post-hook state with aggregated token usage (retrieval_usage + engine_usage), model_strategy, cognitive_tier, and physical_model, and emits the ordered sequence of pre-hook, post-hook, and step output TraceEvent objects carrying TraceEventMetadataDTO and mcp_audit_traces.

docs.title: 2.15. Tripartite Prompt Architecture & Four-Layer Clean Stack
docs.text:
All system prompts are constructed through standardized prompt builders and static prompt modules organized into three decoupled functional tiers: 1. Common Directives: Shared foundational building blocks, linguistic context formatting, and structured system directives utilized across all prompt pipelines. 2. Graph Execution Directives: Step-level operational constraints, atom extraction prompts, causal graph linking protocols, and sensor matrix evaluation system prompts governing DAG execution. 3. Synthesis Directives: Qualitative reporting instructions, server-driven UI mandates, section synthesis guidelines, matrix graph narratives, row explanations, variance analysis, and explainable AI instructions governing report synthesis.

Every compiled prompt strictly adheres to the Four-Layer Clean Stack hierarchy: - Layer 1: Static System Directives & Mandates (Static prefix for context caching). - Layer 2: Theory Grounding & Epistemic Context (Academic references in <theory_context>). - Layer 3: Matrix Objective & Extraction Protocol (Step-level extraction behavior). - Layer 4: Dynamic User Payload & Execution Variables (Runtime text payloads, atom aliases, and dynamic inputs at the absolute tail).

All prompt-building pipelines route execution through LLMTaskExecutor to guarantee schema validation, token usage tracking, and model strategy multiplexing.

docs.title: 2.16. Structured Grounding & CDATA Prompt Tag Compilation
docs.text: Matrix sensor prompt compilation enforces structured semantic grounding with CDATA breakout protection across all evaluation assertions: - Structured Semantic Tags: Discrete assertion parameters are compiled into dedicated XML blocks: <contrastive_grounding> (enclosing <acceptable> and <rejected> exemplars), <acceptance_criteria> (ordered verification instructions), <anti_patterns> (disqualifying conditions; for existential error radars with inverse_evidence = true, legitimate contextual exceptions specifically faithful summarization of cited external research are formally encoded as deterministic anti_patterns on the atom model, replacing meta-cognitive contextual override oscillation), and <syntactic_anchors> (fast-filtering lexical tokens). - CDATA Breakout Shielding: All dynamic assertion text is wrapped in <![CDATA[...]]> containers via TemplateProcessor.encapsulate_payload(), strictly preventing user-authored quotation marks, XML characters (<, >, &), or punctuation from escaping tag boundaries and executing prompt injection. - Prompt Fidelity Expansion: Structured few-shot contrastive pairs and anti-patterns provide nuanced cognitive boundaries, expanding prompt tokens (+100–400 tokens per atom) while remaining strictly bounded within model context ceilings by MatrixSamplingStrategy.

docs.title: 2.17. Tripartite Context Capsule Segregation
docs.text: Dynamic execution inputs are encapsulated into three distinct semantic context capsules based on configured input modalities and conversational flags: - User Deliverable Capsule (<user_payload>): Encapsulates human-authored submissions, uploaded documents, audio transcriptions, or user turns in conversational dialogues. When inputs are configured with endorsed deliverable provenance (ExpectedInput.is_endorsed_deliverable = True), the submission represents the candidate's formally endorsed deliverable: adopting AI-assisted drafting, executive consultant framing, and curated jargon is permitted as authentic candidate-endorsed work product without triggering Echo Parroting penalties, while observation-layer performative pattern scanning remains active for transparent telemetry. - Model Output Capsule (<ai_draft_context>): Encapsulates AI assistant turns and generated responses within multi-turn dialogues (is_chat_history == True). - Assignment Context Capsule (<assignment_context>): Encapsulates external task assignments, problem briefs, evaluation criteria, and operational guidelines (assignment in input_modes or .assignment_context input paths). All context capsules are shielded against CDATA breakout. Layer 1 system instructions explicitly direct foundational models that <assignment_context> provides framing instructions rather than authorial evidence and must never be quoted as factual proof for either USER or AI claims, eliminating prompt injection and quote hijacking.

docs.title: 2.18. Inter-Step Context Packing & Execution Trace Matrix Reduction
docs.text: When workflows chain analytical findings across sequential steps, context transit preserves structured domain payloads without intermediate dictionary degradation: - Compound Step Target Resolution: Downstream steps can target prior step outputs using simple step identifiers ($steps.{step_id}) or compound targets ($steps.{step_id}.{block_id}). The source document packer resolves matching outputs deterministically, verifying all explicitly referenced steps exist and serializing structured payloads (BaseModel, list[BaseModel]) into formatted JSON capsules. - Execution Trace Matrix Reduction: The matrix reducer extracts evaluated atoms and behavioral extensions directly from authoritative runtime state in ExecutionRecord.execution_trace (event_type == 'output' containing results: list[AtomResultDTO]). All completed evaluations (ExecutionStatus.PASSED, ExecutionStatus.FAILED, ExecutionStatus.N_A, and ExecutionStatus.DLQ) are retained and compressed into LightweightMatrixDTO along with their topological lineage (depends_on_tda_ids, short_circuit_reason_tda_ids, and is_inverse_evidence in ReducedAtomDTO), populating evaluated_matrices alongside reduced_atoms and raw_extensions. During in-DAG synthesis execution, SynthesisEngine serializes both reduced_atoms (aliased deterministically via AliasEngine inside <reduced_matrix_atoms>) and raw_extensions alongside the global atom blackboard. - Deterministic Context Routing & Pruning: Context routing (ContextRouter.route_and_prune) requires strongly typed LightweightMatrixOutput models, strictly pruning behavioral extensions according to output profile configurations. When no output profile is specified, extensions resolve deterministically to an empty dictionary rather than leaking unconstrained context. Intermediate payloads pass directly as typed DTO instances across the pipeline without double-serialization.

docs.title: 2.19. Continuous Strictness & Unified Matrix Scoring Engine
docs.text: Evaluation rigor across matrix models flows through a unified scoring engine (UnifiedScoringEngine in backend_v2/utils/scoring/unified_engine.py) parameterized by a continuous strictness level bounded between 0 and 100 inclusive (default_strictness_level on Workflow): - Dual-Track Rubric Standard: - Track A (Developmental Progressive Competence: 7 matrices: blk_f921c7c0989b47e8 [Bloom], blk_53f32679aa514fcb [Goodhart], blk_7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e [HACM], blk_ff72c2d79edb4ebf [Supreme Adjudicator], blk_f6e286f050c94d60 [TaskXAI Clarity], blk_6b8c766185294f7e [XAI Reporter], blk_c0a1e50000000001 [Causal Cohesion]): Level 1 designates the positive Novice capability baseline (inverse_evidence: false). Fulfilling Level 1 awards positive points ($\text{hit_ratio}1 \times w_1$). Higher levels build cumulatively under the Cumulative Guttman Invariant ($L_1 \subset L_2 \subset L_3 \subset L_4 \subset L_5$). - Track B (Diagnostic Orthogonal Malus Error Radars: 8 matrices: blk_440a5fef9331451b [Toulmin], blk_109dab5b6b3f403a [Kahneman], blk_fb15f8dcf23f4865 [Archivist], blk_c5804a9143c34cb1 [Causal Analyst], blk_b476f89fb732448c [Falsifier], blk_80732a33fe1947ee [Taskguard], blk_c3bc5f3eb8e74110 [Causal & Abductive Integrity], blk_22e3598e06414409 [Epistemic Humility]): Levels 1–2 operate strictly as error radars (inverse_evidence: true, aggregation_mode: "EXISTS"). Clean baseline passes award zero positive capability points on Levels 1–2 ($\text{hit_ratio}_1 = 0.0, \text{hit_ratio}_2 = 0.0$), with positive capability points accrued exclusively from affirmative criteria on Levels 3–5 (inverse_evidence: false). Detected errors on Levels 1–2 trigger orthogonal malus deductions. - Weighted Level Hit Ratio Formulation: For each scale level $l \in {1, \dots, L}$ with weight $w_l = \text{score}_l$: $$\text{hit_ratio}_l = \frac{k_l}{N_l}$$ $$\text{Linear_Ratio} = \frac{\sum{l=1}^{L} (\text{hit_ratio}l \times w_l)}{\sum{l=1}^{L} w_l}$$ while excluding disqualified (DLQ) observations from the denominator. - Piecewise Continuous Exponent Dampening: Modulates the linear ratio using a continuous piecewise exponent curve $e(S)$: - Free ($0 \le S \le 50$): $e(S) = 1.00 + \frac{S}{50} \times 0.25$ (from $1.00$ at $0\%$ to $1.25$ at $50\%$) - Normal to Strict ($50 < S \le 85$): $e(S) = 1.25 + \frac{S - 50}{35} \times 0.45$ (with calibrated default $e(70) \approx 1.5071$ at $70\%$) - Strict to Absolute ($85 < S \le 100$): $e(S) = 1.70 + \frac{S - 85}{15} \times 0.50$ (from $1.70$ at $85\%$ to $2.20$ at $100\%$) $$\text{Dampened_Ratio} = (\text{Linear_Ratio})^{e(S)}$$ $$\text{Raw_Score} = \text{math_min} + \text{Dampened_Ratio} \times (\text{math_max} - \text{math_min})$$ - Per-Matrix Normalization Hook: In normalization_hook.py, every matrix score is mapped to a standardized $[0.0, 100.0]$ range using its dynamically computed scale extrema ($\text{computed_min}$ and $\text{computed_max}$): $$\text{Normalized_Score}m = \left(\frac{\text{Raw_Score}_m - \text{computed_min}_m}{\text{computed_max}_m - \text{computed_min}_m}\right) \times 100.0$$ - Gate 5 Epistemic Strictness Decoupling: Scoring dampening strictness ($\zeta{\text{score}} \in [0, 100]$, default_strictness_level) and lexical citation matching strictness ($\zeta_{\text{lex}} \in [0, 100]$, default_lexical_strictness_level) operate as completely independent sovereign execution parameters on Workflow. Scoring strictness dictates non-linear power-curve exponent dampening in UnifiedScoringEngine, while lexical strictness governs citation verification thresholds in AnchorValidationService, enabling morphological Snowball stemming for non-English inflections whenever $\zeta_{\text{lex}} < 85$ regardless of whether scoring strictness is calibrated to 100% Absolute Zero-Trust. - Typed Return Contract: Returns an immutable ScoringResultDTO containing the normalized score, structured XAI audit trace, and per-level breakdown mapped to dict[str, LevelStatsDTO], eliminating anonymous tuple passing and primitive obsession dictionaries.

docs.title: 2.20. Automated Score Deduction Penalties & Holistic Scoring Engine
docs.text: Holistic evaluation scores and automated score deduction percentages are execution-tier parameters defined on Workflow entities and evaluated deterministically inside the scoring logic hook (apply_scoring_logic_hook): - Automated Penalty Modalities: - Security Penalty (security_penalty): Deducted when prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, or unauthorized role escape patterns are detected in inputs or state.global_context_vars.sanitization.threat_detected. - Post-Hoc Penalty (post_hoc_penalty): Deducted when post-hoc rationalization, retrospective excuses, or confabulated causality patterns are identified in falsifier analysis. - Passivity Penalty (passivity_penalty): Deducted when evasive, non-responsive, or passive avoidance behaviors are detected in candidate deliverables via state.global_context_vars.passivity_detected. - Synchronous Post-Hook Wiring (Elimination of Phantom Penalties): Defining passivity_penalty > 0 on a Workflow requires synchronous wiring with "enforce_passivity_penalty" inside Step 4 Coach (sp_25664f44773a4354) post_hooks. Both configurations exist concurrently: the workflow-level penalty scalar sets the deduction magnitude, while the step-level post-hook executes the behavioral analysis and populates state.global_context_vars.passivity_detected. - Cumulative Clamping & Safety Bounds: Cumulative penalty percentages are capped at MAX_TOTAL_PENALTY_RATIO = 0.40 (40% maximum deduction). The effective penalty is computed as effective_penalty = min(total_penalty, 0.40). - Token Formatting & Audit Trail: Active penalties are formatted as tokens (PENALTY_<TYPE>:<PERCENTAGE>) and stored in scoring_result.penalties_applied within TraceScoringPayloadDTO, locking the evaluation score permanently upon execution completion.

docs.title: 2.21. Real-Time Step Progress Synchronization & Committer Invariants
docs.text: Step execution progression and anomaly indicators (progress: int | None, has_warning: bool) are first-class domain properties synchronized across DAG orchestration and background workers: - Real-Time Step Advancement: As steps process chunks and sub-tasks, progress callbacks mutate both the active step instance and the unified steps collection in ExecutionRecord. - Atomic Committer Persistence: The trace committer (ExecutionCommitter.commit_trace) accepts and persists the current steps collection alongside trace events, ensuring that intermediate commits and state updates never overwrite step progression with stale or null data. - Worker Completion Telemetry Preservation: When the DAG terminates, the background worker preserves verified step progression percentages and warning states during final telemetry aggregation and fallback step reconstruction, preventing timeline indicators from resetting upon task completion.

docs.title: 2.22. Commensurate Multi-Matrix Global Score Aggregation & Evaluative Gating
docs.text: In falsifier_hook.py and blueprint.py, commensurate normalized scores from state.global_context_vars.evaluative_matrices are aggregated into the holistic global_score via unweighted arithmetic averaging across all $N$ completed evaluative matrices, subject to automated workflow penalties: - Evaluative Gating (is_evaluative: bool) & Relational Identifier Invariant: Both Track A and Track B matrices calculate normalized scores $[0.0, 100.0]$ through UnifiedScoringEngine and normalization_hook.py. Gating into evaluative_matrices (and thus global_score) is governed strictly by MatrixPromptBlock.is_evaluative. In accordance with Quorum's relational integrity standards, slug values are strictly human-readable diagnostic labels and are NEVER permitted as relational foreign keys or state dictionary keys; all relational bindings, step criteria lists (criteria_block_ids), output profile target blocks (variance_target_block), and evaluative_matrices dictionary entries are keyed strictly and sovereignly by canonical opaque block IDs (blk_...): - Evaluative Matrices (10 matrices, is_evaluative: true): Directly participate in the global score average. Includes 4 Track A developmental matrices (blk_f921c7c0989b47e8 [Bloom], blk_f6e286f050c94d60 [TaskXAI Clarity], blk_7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e [HACM], blk_c0a1e50000000001 [Causal Cohesion]) and 6 Track B diagnostic matrices (blk_440a5fef9331451b [Toulmin], blk_109dab5b6b3f403a [Kahneman], blk_c5804a9143c34cb1 [Causal Analyst], blk_b476f89fb732448c [Falsifier], blk_22e3598e06414409 [Epistemic Humility], blk_c3bc5f3eb8e74110 [Causal & Abductive Integrity]). Track B matrices contribute full capability scores accrued from Levels 3–5 alongside Track A matrices. - Specialized Role Matrices (5 matrices, is_evaluative: false): Excluded from the global score average to preserve orthogonal functionality.
