Includes blk_53f32679aa514fcb [Goodhart] (Cartesian variance X-axis), blk_80732a33fe1947ee [Taskguard] (security containment guard triggering security_penalty), blk_fb15f8dcf23f4865 [Archivist] (statutory compliance checklist), blk_ff72c2d79edb4ebf [Supreme Adjudicator] (supervisory steering discipline), and blk_6b8c766185294f7e [XAI Reporter] (multi-specialist consensus reporting). - Mathematical Aggregation: $$\text{average_score} = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{m=1}^{N} \text{Normalized_Score}_m$$ $$\text{effective_penalty} = \min(\text{total_penalty}, 0.40)$$ $$\text{global_score} = \text{round}(\max(0.0, \text{average_score} \times (1.0 - \text{effective_penalty})), 1)$$ If matrix evaluations are absent without an explicit indeterminate justification, strict fail-fast validation halts execution to protect report integrity.

docs.title: 2.23. Dynamic Capability-Driven MCP Tool Dispatching & Multi-Tool Orchestration
docs.text: Quorum's Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool execution subsystem enables external computational and information-retrieval tool calling within multi-turn agentic reasoning loops. The orchestration architecture is governed by dynamic capability indexing, protocol-agnostic client transport, runtime schema compilation, and zero provider branching: - Capability Taxonomy (ToolCapability): All external tools declare an explicit ToolCapability enum attribute: ToolCapability.SEARCH, ToolCapability.DOCUMENT_READER, or ToolCapability.ACTION. - Dynamic Gateway Dispatching (ToolDispatcher): ToolDispatcher dynamically indexes tools across registered MCP gateways from system configuration. Orchestrators query tools by capability and resolve primary search tools via positive ID-set validation against step-level allowed tools (step.allowed_mcp_tools). Heuristic substring matching, provider-specific branches, and keyword lookups are eliminated. - Protocol-Agnostic Transport (GenericMCPClient): External tool calls execute through a protocol-agnostic client supporting Streamable HTTP and Server-Sent Events (SSE) transports. The client employs dual wire-framing, parsing JSON-RPC 2.0 payloads from direct responses and streaming event frames, accompanied by Tenacity retry coordination for transient transport interruptions. - Typed MCP Initialize Handshake Metadata (MCPServerInfoDTO, MCPIconDTO): During gateway discovery and initialization handshakes over JSON-RPC 2.0 (initialize), server implementation metadata returned by external providers is parsed into strongly typed, immutable models MCPInitializeResultDTO, MCPServerInfoDTO, and MCPIconDTO. In accordance with the Model Context Protocol Implementation specification, the schema captures name, version, title, description, website_url, and icons: list[MCPIconDTO] (src, mime_type, sizes), supporting cross-casing wire aliases while enforcing extra="forbid" to eliminate untyped dictionary leakage across external gateway integrations. - Runtime Pydantic Schema Compilation (SchemaFactory): Tool parameter schemas defined in recursive JSON Schema ASTs are compiled dynamically into typed Pydantic validation models using pydantic.create_model. Tools declare parameter specifications via MCPToolDeclarationDTO serialized with exclude_none=True for model function calling. - Just-in-Time (JIT) Micro-LLM Argument Synthesizer (synthesize_search_arguments): Tool argument synthesis resolves dynamic arguments for external tools with complex multi-parameter schemas. Synthesis dispatches lightweight model execution with MCP_JIT_ARGUMENT_SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION to extract precise tool parameters from step execution context and input texts against the tool's compiled Pydantic argument model (SchemaFactory.create_mcp_tool_argument_model). For standard search tools requiring a single text query, the dispatcher utilizes a 0ms deterministic fast-path (build_search_arguments), instantly projecting the primary query without LLM invocation. - Step-Level Parameter Overrides & Typed Argument Contracts (mcp_tool_params): Workflow steps declare static parameter overrides (step.mcp_tool_params) configured in Quorum Studio. Static overrides merge deterministically over synthesized arguments, binding fixed runtime properties (such as result limits, language codes, or filters). Tool argument structures adhere strictly to the MCPArgumentValue SSOT type union (MCPArgumentScalar, primitive list sequences, or dict[str, MCPArgumentScalar]), guaranteeing type safety across nested tool configurations without permissive dictionaries. - Deterministic Namespace Routing (AliasRegistry): Discovered tools are isolated under namespaced aliases combining gateway slug and tool identifier ({gateway_slug}__{tool_id}). Bijective alias resolution parses namespaced calls and routes execution deterministically to the corresponding gateway. - Non-Blocking SSRF & DNS-Rebinding Firewall (MCPUrlValidator): All gateway connections undergo pre-flight address validation in worker threads, strictly blocking loopback addresses, private subnets, cloud metadata services, and HTTP redirects. - Direct Node-Level Retrieval & Single Pipeline Invariance: When a workflow step declares allowed tools (step.allowed_mcp_tools), node execution triggers retrieval directly via execute_mcp_retrieval prior to primary model generation, returning an immutable MCPRetrievalResultDTO. Execution flows through a single sovereign pipeline without parallel runner forks. - Layer 4 Dynamic Evidence Injection & CDATA Encapsulation: Tool outputs undergo sentence-boundary character truncation and mandatory CDATA encapsulation. Extracted evidence payloads are injected into Layer 4 of the prompt hierarchy enclosed in <mcp_evidence> tags, preserving static Layer 1–3 directives for context caching. - Audit Logging, Provenance & Distributed Tracing: Every tool invocation produces an immutable MCPAuditTrace entry capturing tool identifier, gateway identifier, gateway slug, namespaced alias, execution parameters, sanitized outputs, and execution duration. Audit traces are returned in MCPRetrievalResultDTO, emitted via trace events, merged into frozen context, and traced under OpenTelemetry mcp.tool_call spans.

docs.title: 3.2. End-to-End Execution Lifecycle
docs.text:
The workflow execution pipeline is partitioned into three decoupled functional stages communicating through event-driven immutable data envelopes:

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Client Application (Flutter UI)
    participant API as API Ingress Router
    participant DB as Persistence Store (PostgreSQL 19)
    participant Arq as Background Task Queue (Arq/Redis)
    participant DAG as DAG Orchestration Engine
    participant LLM as LLM Provider Gateway
    participant Synth as Synthesis Engine
    participant SDUI as Presentation Blueprint Hub

    %% 1. Ingress & Non-Blocking Asynchronous Start
    User->>API: POST /executions (WorkflowInputs + ProfileID)
    API->>DB: Persist ExecutionRecord (status=RUNNING) & FrozenContext
    API->>Arq: Enqueue execute_workflow_job
    API-->>User: HTTP 202 Accepted (ExecutionRecord)

    %% 2. Real-Time State Streaming & Heavy Execution
    par Real-Time SSE Telemetry
        User->>API: GET /executions/{id}/stream (SSE)
        loop State Progression Broadcasts
            API->>DB: Query TraceEvents & ExecutionStatus
            API-->>User: data: ExecutionRecord / SSE Heartbeat Pulse
        end
    and Execution Stage: Heavy DAG Computation
        Arq->>DAG: Dispatch execution task -> Execute Workflow DAG
        DAG->>LLM: 1. Extract Global Ontology Map (TwoPassAtomizer Phase 0)
        LLM-->>DAG: Enriched ontology map and contextual entities
        DAG->>LLM: 2. Matrix Causal DAG Sensor evaluations (TDAEngine / Best-of-3 Flash)
        LLM-->>DAG: Evaluation observations and scale scores (1-5)
        DAG->>DAG: 3. Execute hooks, validation & MatrixReducer scoring math
        DAG->>DB: Update ExecutionRecord (TraceEvents, step_states)
        DAG->>Arq: Enqueue generate_report_artifact_job
    end

    %% 3. Qualitative Reporting & Text Synthesis Stage
    Arq->>Synth: Dispatch synthesis task -> Generate Profile Synthesis
    Synth->>LLM: Generate structured section syntheses & XAI highlights
    LLM-->>Synth: Structured text responses (section_syntheses DTO)
    Synth->>Synth: Enforce Two-Tier Length Budgeting (Sentence Boundaries)
    Synth->>DB: Persist RenderedSynthesisCache (profile_syntheses)

    %% 4. On-Demand Presentation Stage: SDUI Dumb Painter
    User->>API: POST /executions/{id}/reports & GET /reports/{id}/...
    API->>SDUI: Transform domain report data to visual blocks
    SDUI->>SDUI: Map to flat polymorphic inner_sdui_blocks (AnySduiBlock)

docs.title: Execution Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
1. Ingress & Asynchronous Non-Blocking Handshake:
  2. The client issues POST /executions with the raw input payload and target output profile identifier.
  3. The API Ingress router initializes and persists the ExecutionRecord with status=RUNNING, stores the frozen context snapshot, enqueues the workflow execution job to the background task queue, and returns an immediate HTTP 202 Accepted response to eliminate thread blocking.
  4. Real-Time SSE Telemetry & Graph Execution (Execution Stage):
  5. The client establishes an independent Server-Sent Events stream (GET /executions/{id}/stream) to receive real-time state broadcasts.
  6. The background worker executes the Directed Acyclic Graph, orchestrating Phase 0 global ontology extraction, topological wave evaluation of matrix assertions via Best-of-Three consensus, and mathematical normalization.
  7. The final execution state is committed to persistence, and the worker enqueues the subsequent synthesis stage.
  8. Structured Qualitative Synthesis (Synthesis Stage):
  9. The synthesis task distills and compresses the raw DAG evaluation state with zero-loss epistemic fidelity, filtering out unparsed ingestion steps via is_synthesis_source, retaining all PASSED, FAILED, N_A, and is_inverse_evidence evaluations with full topological lineage, and applying topological-priority deficit stratification when an explicit evaluation limit is configured.
  10. The synthesis engine generates structured qualitative text (Executive Summary, Matrix Sections, Row Explanations, XAI Highlights) mapped to specific layout identifiers.
  11. The Two-Tier length budget enforcer verifies character ceilings, concluding text on clean sentence boundaries before persisting the result into RenderedSynthesisCache.
  12. On-Demand SDUI Presentation (Presentation Stage - Dumb Painter):
  13. When the client or downstream consumer requests the visual report (GET /executions/{id}/sdui, GET /executions/{id}/report, or PDF export), the presentation blueprint transformer acts as a pure "Dumb Painter", translating domain DTOs into a flat array of inner_sdui_blocks: list[AnySduiBlock] with zero runtime LLM calls or domain math.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: The Server-Driven UI & Presentation capability governs the user-facing "Surface" of the Compound AI System. Its foundational architectural premise is the Dumb Painter Pattern: the client application (Flutter desktop frontend) and the report export engine (WeasyPrint HTML-to-PDF compiler) contain zero business logic, zero layout heuristics, zero scoring math, and zero prompt compilation routines. The backend acts as the sole authoritative state machine, compiling complex cognitive graphs and evaluation models into a deterministic, flat sequence of polymorphic visual blocks (inner_sdui_blocks). The presentation surfaces merely paint the declarative Markdown, typography, theme tokens, and structured data payloads they receive. This architecture guarantees strict 1:1 cross-platform semantic parity between interactive desktop dashboards and static vector PDF publications.

docs.title: 2.1. Dumb Painter Flat Polymorphic Pipeline (inner_sdui_blocks)
docs.text: The presentation layer strictly enforces a flat, sequentially ordered array: inner_sdui_blocks: list[AnySduiBlock]. Nested macro-routing trees, layout dictionaries (layouts), and client-side presentation inference are permanently banned. All report sections, graphs, summaries, and narratives are flattened by the backend into this linear array. The client iterates sequentially through the blocks, dispatching each block strictly according to its discriminator variant. Adapters assemble report sections in a strict, predictable sequential structure: 1. Header Block: MarkdownBlock(text="### " + title) 2. Synthesis Narrative: ParagraphBlock(text=synthesis_narrative) 3. Data Visualization Component: Dedicated chart or table (SduiRadarChartBlock, SduiScatterPlotBlock, SduiQuadrantMatrixBlock, SduiMetrics1DBlock, SduiMatrixTableBlock) with its internal title attribute explicitly set to None to prevent duplicate header rendering. Complex visualization components decompose into focused, private Dumb Painter cell widgets (header cells, matrix identity cells, distribution cells, and diagnostic narrative cells). In-build sorting and mutable list allocations within render cycles are completely eliminated; the renderer maps backend DTO sequences directly to decomposed cells. 4. Citations / Sources: Localized footer blocks (MarkdownBlock(text="#### " + localized_sources), PrintableSourcesBlock). For text-only views, the data visualization component is omitted entirely, producing strictly MarkdownBlock -> ParagraphBlock. All scaling math, score calculations, date formatting, and static headers are pre-computed and pre-localized on the backend, ensuring client rendering remains mathematically decoupled from presentation. Within the presentation pipeline, BlueprintTransformer operates as a 100% read-only Dumb Painter: it executes zero database mutation calls (update_execution is strictly prohibited in presentation transformers), directly projects the finalized evaluation score from scoring_result.total_score, and passes active penalty tokens directly to AdapterContext.penalties_applied for PenaltiesAdapter rendering, executing zero scoring recalculations or profile-based score mutations.

docs.title: 2.2. Strict Polymorphic Serialization & Discriminated Unions (18 Block Types)
docs.text: All dynamic UI layout blocks are strictly typed using polymorphic discriminated unions across both language boundaries: - Backend (Python Pydantic V2): AnySduiBlock = Annotated[..., Field(discriminator="block_type")]. Every concrete child model inherits from SduiBlockBase, configuring model_config = ConfigDict(title="<block_type>", strict=True, extra="forbid") and binding a literal discriminator field (block_type: Literal["<block_type>"]). Forward-reference hydration for complex nested SDUI blocks (MatrixScorecardRowDTO, ReportDataDTO) is deterministically resolved through co-located Pydantic model_rebuild() calls at the module level in view and report models, injecting the exact types namespace (AnySduiBlock, MCPAuditTrace) and eliminating runtime circular imports. - Frontend (Flutter Dart 3): Defined client sealed class @Freezed(unionKey: 'block_type') sealed class SduiBlockDTO. Every union variant enforces @JsonSerializable(disallowUnrecognizedKeys: true). - Exhaustive Renderer Matching: In the client block renderer, rendering uses Dart 3 native switch expressions over SduiBlockDTO exhaustively matching all 18 concrete block types without wildcard defaults (_ =>): 1. hero_insight: High-priority analytical takeaway with severity iconography. 2. paragraph: Markdown narrative prose with theme typography. 3. bullet_list: Structured bullet points with optional emphasis. 4. alert_box: Themed alerts with visual intent (VisualIntent.CRITICAL_OVERRIDE, WARNING, INFO). 5. accordion: Collapsible container for extensive analytical details. 6. markdown: Raw GitHub-flavored Markdown document chunk. 7. quote_card: Forensic quote citation anchored to source document fragments. 8. warning_card: System alert for operational exceptions and data starvation. 9. n_a_card: Explicit null-state card for un-evaluated or skipped criteria. 10. grid: Dynamic multi-column layout for comparative metrics. 11. metadata: Execution metadata, execution timestamp, user context, token telemetry, and financial costs. 12. 3d_matrix: Multi-axis radar chart for multi-dimensional competency models. 13. 2d_compare: Scatter plot for bivariate comparative evaluations. 14. quadrant_matrix: Four-quadrant matrix for variance and authenticity analysis. 15. matrix_summary: Comprehensive tabular matrix of evaluation scores, columns, and qualitative extension labels. 16. 1d_metrics: Linear scorecard list for individual matrix rows and indicators. 17. score_card: Prominent executive scorecard displaying the aggregated global score and penalty adjustments. 18. audit_trail: Immutable trace table of external tool interactions and MCP gateway invocations. Any unexpected discriminator or malformed schema triggers an immediate Fail-Fast crash (AppException on the backend, caught by AppErrorBoundary on the frontend) rather than silently dropping elements or hiding them with empty widgets (SizedBox.shrink()).

docs.title: 2.3. Self-Contained SDUI Presentation Adapters
docs.text:
Presentation logic is modularized into isolated presentation adapters. Every adapter strictly adheres to a standardized Two-Section Architecture: - Section 1 (Strongly Typed Aesthetic Rules): Module-level styling configurations bind to dedicated, immutable Pydantic V2 aesthetic DTOs (GlobalScoreAestheticsDTO, MatrixGraphsAestheticsDTO, MatrixSummaryAestheticsDTO, McpAuditAestheticsDTO, MetadataAestheticsDTO, SynthesisTextAestheticsDTO, WarningCardAestheticsDTO in sdui_rules). This centralizes all visual styling decisions, mapping domain keys to visual properties (severity, icon_name, label keys) via static dot-notation attributes and typed mappings, completely eradicating Primitive Obsession and untyped dictionary subscripting. Missing configurations trigger an immediate RFC 7807 error and an AppException, preventing unconfigured attributes from silently defaulting. - Section 2 (Adapter Class): An adapter class exposing a single @staticmethod def build(context: AdapterContext) -> list[AnySduiBlock]. It reads domain state from the context, queries visual properties from Section 1, and emits flat AnySduiBlock instances. - Immutable Context Envelope (AdapterContext): The input parameter AdapterContext is a frozen Pydantic V2 model (ConfigDict(frozen=True, strict=True, extra="forbid")) instantiated once by BlueprintTransformer before the dispatch loop and passed identically to all hydrators. It provides zero-cost $O(1)$ predicate helpers (specifically is_data_starved) while prohibiting side-channel keyword argument mutations.

The adapter cluster comprises 11 canonical hydrators mapped to TargetBlockType enums: 1. ExecutiveSummaryAdapter (EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY_BLOCK): Transforms profile executive narratives and cognitive persona assessments into ParagraphBlock and HeroInsightBlock. 2. GlobalScoreAdapter (GLOBAL_SCORE_BLOCK): Formats the normalized, penalty-adjusted composite score into an executive SduiScoreCardBlock. 3. MatrixGraphsAdapter (MATRIX_GRAPHS_BLOCK): Renders evaluated matrix synthesis groups into radar charts, scatter plots, 1D metric scorecards, or text-only views with localized headers and qualitative explanations. 4. MatrixSummaryTableAdapter (MATRIX_SUMMARY_TABLE_BLOCK): Assembles evaluated axes into comprehensive comparative tables with localized column headers and extension badges. 5. VarianceAdapter (VARIANCE_VALIDATION_BLOCK): Evaluates Cartesian variance across substantive cognitive depth and mechanical jargon load, assembling quadrant matrix visualizations (SduiQuadrantMatrixBlock) and analytical explanations. Substantive cognitive depth is extracted strictly and deterministically from the matrix block designated by OutputProfile.variance_target_block. Scale extrema (scale_min and scale_max) are dynamically resolved from context.parsed_matrices[target_block_id]. The adapter validates that scale_max > scale_min, computes the dynamic plot ratio (score - scale_min) / (scale_max - scale_min), and renders localized axis summaries reflecting the true scale maximum (e.g. f"{lbl}: {score:.1f} / {scale_max:.1f}"), seamlessly supporting arbitrary multi-scale cognitive frameworks (specifically 1–3, 1–5, and 1–6 models). 6. PenaltiesAdapter (PENALTIES_BLOCK): Maps applied policy or security penalties into AlertBlock notifications. 7. XaiHighlightsAdapter (GROUPED_EXTENSIONS_BLOCK): Curates behavioral claim highlights using fair round-robin interleaving to prevent single-category presentation bias. 8. McpAuditAdapter (AUDIT_TRAIL_BLOCK): Serializes immutable MCP tool invocations into an SduiAuditTrailBlock. 9. MetadataAdapter (METADATA_BLOCK): Emits execution metadata, execution timing, user context, token consumption, and financial costs into SduiMetadataBlock. 10. PrintableSourcesAdapter (PRINTABLE_SOURCES_BLOCK): Formats bibliographic citations, academic grounding, and extracted source anchors into verifiable citation lists, routing external findings through McpPresentationSanitizer to present clean, sentence-budgeted evidence lines with guaranteed terminal punctuation. 11. SynthesisTextAdapter (SYNTHESIS_TEXT_BLOCK): Translates custom markdown prefaces and qualitative narrative sections into MarkdownBlock. In addition, WarningCardAdapter dynamically injects pre-flight system alerts and data starvation warnings at the top of the stream.

docs.title: 2.4. Database-Driven Target Block Dispatching & Presentation Services
docs.text: The assembly sequence of SDUI blocks is 100% database-driven via OutputProfile.target_block_order (list[str]) configured in seed_data.json / OutputProfile: - Dynamic Reordering: The orchestrator (BlueprintTransformer) iterates strictly over the array defined by the active profile, looking up the corresponding hydrator in _target_block_hydrators. Users freely reorder sections in the Studio interface without code modifications. - Text Delivery Governance: The visibility of qualitative synthesis narratives and section titles is governed by OutputProfile.text_delivery_mode ("none", "titles_only", "full"). Modifying visibility is achieved by changing configuration in the database rather than inserting if/else logic in Python code. - Data Starvation Guardrail: If an execution lacks required evaluation data or triggers data starvation (adapter_context.is_data_starved), the dispatch loop restricts rendering strictly to METADATA_BLOCK alongside a prominent WarningCardAdapter banner, preventing broken or empty graphs from rendering. - Studio-Configured Variance Target Binding: Cartesian variance validation evaluates cognitive authenticity against performative language. The authenticity score is bound strictly and deterministically to the matrix block declared in OutputProfile.variance_target_block. When variance validation is active (visible_workflow_extensions contains "variance_validation" or VARIANCE_VALIDATION_BLOCK is present in target_block_order), OutputProfile enforces via Fail-Fast @model_validator that variance_target_block is non-null and points to an evaluated matrix. In Quorum Studio, VarianceBlockCard exposes a dedicated target matrix selector filtered strictly against allowedBlockIds declared by the active workflow's step criteria. The report worker extracts the authenticity score directly from out_content[target_block_id] without heuristic string matching or marker guessing.

docs.title: Materialized Report Artifacts (ReportService & REST API)
docs.text: ReportService coordinates the full lifecycle of ReportArtifact domain entities, providing independent presentation generation decoupled from execution runs: - Comprehensive Lifecycle Operations: Creates, retrieves, lists, regenerates, and deletes report artifacts. Artifacts compile and persist pre-rendered SDUI JSON, vector PDF documents, multi-tab Excel files, and flat-file CSVs. - Idempotent Ingress Guard: Simultaneous requests to generate identical reports for the same execution and profile return HTTP 409 Conflict, preventing duplicate background worker storms. - Cascade Deletion: Deleting an execution run triggers synchronous cascade deletion of all associated report records and physical disk storage blobs. - Public REST API: Report artifacts are served through a single authoritative APIRouter mounted under /api/v2: artifacts are created via POST /api/v2/executions/{execution_id}/reports and listed at GET /api/v2/executions/{execution_id}/reports, individual report status, lifecycle management, and format streaming endpoints (/sdui, /pdf, /excel, /csv, /rows, /regenerate) are served canonically at /api/v2/reports/{report_id}/..., and public external report retrieval is served at GET /api/v2/external/reports/{report_id} with zero shadow route aliases or legacy /api/v1 mounts.

docs.title: Dedicated Tabular & Multi-Format Export Service (ExportService)
docs.text: ExportService assembles structured tabular exports for corporate ingestion and audit compliance, operating strictly as a 100% pure Dumb Painter governed by the Anti-Synthetic Row Invariant: - Cross-Surface Dumb Painter Parity & Anti-Synthetic Row Invariant: Export generation produces deterministic, un-extrapolated records with zero phantom rows, zero synthetic summary entities, and zero ad-hoc metrics: - Excel Tab 1 (Matrix Summary Completeness): Unconditionally projects all standard matrix columns (specifically and exhaustively all 9 members of ReportMatrixColumn: label, context_target, distribution, row_explanation, criteria, quotes, source, normalized_score, score) using localized headers via ReportHeaderResolver with "Logiikkamatriisi" / "Logic Matrix" as the unified label. Visible columns default to the Single Source of Truth STANDARD_MATRIX_VISIBLE_COLUMNS = ["label", "distribution", "row_explanation", "criteria", "normalized_score"]. The row count is mathematically invariant: actual_summary_rows == len(matrices). - Excel Tab 2 (Forensic Evaluated Atoms) & Tabular CSV Streaming: Projects complete rectangular datasets containing every evaluated matrix atom and streamed causal graph proposition across all 14 members of ReportAtomColumn (matrix, context_target, level, level_name, criterion, claim_type, result_status, quotes, ai_reasoning, is_inverse, points_awarded, source_speaker, target_speaker, document_id). Dynamic unmapped causal graph propositions (CausalNodeDTO) stream deterministically into Tab 2 rows under matrix_label = "Kausaalipäättely" (matrix_label = "Causal Reasoning"). Rectangular CSV streams project all 22 denormalized flat columns ordered by ReportHeaderResolver.get_all_denormalized_csv_headers, combining execution metadata, matrix attributes, atom forensics, and ML-ready columns with UTF-8-SIG encoding for direct spreadsheet interoperability. - ML-Ready Indicators & Mathematical Scoring Identity: ExportForensicAtomDTO and ExportDenormalizedFlatRowDTO carry strictly bounded ML numeric indicators: is_inverse: int [0 or 1] and points_awarded: float [1.0 or 0.0]. The mathematical scoring identity holds across scorecards: hits == sum(points_awarded) + passed_clean_anti_patterns, where affirmative capability atoms earn 1.0 points upon passing (points_awarded == 1.0), and anti-patterns evaluate the absence of negative evidence without inflating affirmative capability points. - Strict DTO State Transit: All exported rows, rectangular streams, and download artifacts are encapsulated in immutable Pydantic V2 DTOs (ExportMatrixSummaryRowDTO, ExportForensicAtomDTO, ExportDenormalizedFlatRowDTO, ExportPayloadDTO) with model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, extra="forbid", frozen=True). Binary payloads, filenames, and MIME types are packaged in ExportPayloadDTO, eliminating anonymous tuples in export signatures. - Multilingual SSOT & Centralized Header Resolution: Column headers and worksheet titles resolve exclusively from centralized backend localization files (backend_v2/l10n/fi.json, en.json) via ReportHeaderResolver and typed enums (ReportMatrixColumn, ReportAtomColumn, ReportSheetKey) delegating to LocalizationService.translate(). ReportMatrixColumn.LABEL and ReportAtomColumn.MATRIX are unified under "Logiikkamatriisi" / "Logic Matrix", eradicating terminological divergence across export surfaces. - Bidirectional Studio Configuration Parity: Studio Output Profile configuration cards (MatrixSummaryTableCard, MetadataBlockCard, MatrixGraphItemEditor) and client ARB catalogs (client_app_v2/lib/l10n/app_fi.arb, app_en.arb) enforce 1:1 key and semantic parity across studioMatrixCol*, meta*, and xai* keys with backend SSOT files. Presentation layers enforce the Zero-Slug Fallback Invariant: domain entities expose human-readable names via I18nText, while machine slugs serve strictly as internal routing identifiers, never as presentation fallbacks. - B2B Tabular Row Delivery & Semantic Status Decoupling: Emits strongly typed ReportRowItemDTO items via /rows for programmatic ingestion into enterprise BI platforms. The boolean indicator is_inverse_evidence: bool explicitly decouples capability point awards from inverse negative evidence findings: affirmative capability rows (is_inverse_evidence == false) display quantitative score badges (+1 p / 0 p), whereas inverse negative evidence rows (is_inverse_evidence == true, specifically error radar / anti-patterns) display qualitative diagnosis badges (Puhdas [Clean] / ⚠️ Negatiivinen löydös [Negative Finding]), ensuring that client presentation remains a pure Dumb Painter without conflating negative evidence detection with capability scoring. - Dual-Axis Localization Anchoring: Export column headers and section titles resolve strictly from backend I18nText database records and static SSOT dictionaries, guaranteeing that backend export services never access client .arb resource files.

docs.title: Desktop-Class Pro Tool UI for Report Artifacts
docs.text: Client-side report browsing and authoring adhere strictly to the 16-pillar Desktop Pro Tool UX standard: - ExecutionReportsView: Built with the Adaptive Master Selector standard (LayoutBuilder wide >= 900px lateral 280px sidebar list with ListView.builder virtualization vs compact < 900px horizontal ChoiceChip top-bar), Single Cognitive Unit isolation (rendering exactly ONE report at a time), 4-tab Progressive Disclosure (SDUI visual tree, PDF document preview, tabular rows table, execution telemetry and FinOps metadata), and full AppErrorBoundary containment. - CreateReportDialog: Implements the Dual-Shield FormField Architecture with focus-loss auto-flush, modal exit interception via PopScope(canPop: false) with post-frame blur flush, serialization-based model dirty checking (jsonEncode(_model.toJson()) != _initialModelJson), Modal-Internal Error Surface (absolute SnackBar ban), auto-scroll to invalid fields, and atomic save debouncing.

docs.title: 2.5. Asynchronous SDUI Matrix Synthesis & Arq Worker Orchestration
docs.text: Qualitative report synthesis is decoupled from synchronous API endpoints and executes asynchronously within Arq background workers (generate_report_artifact_job): - Centralized Prompt Directives SSOT: Foundational prompt templates, Layer 1 system identities, and structural constants are imported from the static synthesis prompt assets SSOT (SYNTHESIS_SYSTEM_PROMPT, ROW_EXPLANATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT, VARIANCE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY_SECTION_ID, SYNTHESIS_SECTION_RULES_PREFIX, SYNTHESIS_XAI_CURATION). - Native Structured Output API: Worker tasks invoke LLMClient.run_structured_task(response_model=SynthesisOutputDTO), eliminating text-based regex JSON extraction. - Deterministic Cache Persistence: Synthesized sections (SynthesisSectionDTO) are stored in RenderedSynthesisCache.section_syntheses, keyed strictly by TargetBlockType constants ("executive_summary_block") or layout identifiers (layout_0_2d_compare). Adapters look up synthesis text strictly via these enum constants, permanently banning fallback key loops. - Modular Synthesis Gating: The system enforces two-tier synthesis gating: 1. Global Executive Summary Scope: Driven by OutputProfile.executive_summary_directive and emitted as EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY_SECTION_ID. 2. Matrix Group Synthesis Scope: Driven by OutputProfile.matrix_synthesis_groups (list[MatrixSynthesisGroup]), bounded in length by matrix_graph_length_constraint. Profiles gracefully support zero-group states for non-matrix workflows, while concrete matrix groups require at least one target block (min_length=1), validated by @model_validator cross-field coherence checks. Missing profile directives log warnings and gracefully skip synthesis tasks without halting the pipeline.

docs.title: 2.6. Strict ICU Markdown Parity & Tripartite Rendering Boundary
docs.text: The presentation engine enforces a strict boundary between structured data and layout rendering: - Zero Backend HTML/CSS: Backend Python services are strictly forbidden from emitting HTML tags (<span>, <font>, <br>, <div>, <a>), inline CSS, or manual spacing hacks ( ). All textual data must be semantic GitHub-flavored Markdown. Entities requiring interactive navigation use standard Markdown link syntax ([Link Text](tda_123)). - Pure Data Payloads: Python services return pure Pydantic DTOs or discrete SDUI component blocks, never concatenating business data into synthetic ASCII or Markdown tables. - Client-Side ICU Message Formatting: Parameterized system messages and static UI labels are defined as ICU message templates in Flutter message catalogs (app_en.arb, app_fi.arb) and evaluated via AppLocalizations.of(context). The backend supplies raw numerical parameters, dates, and enum keys; the frontend handles pluralization and grammatical agreement deterministically. Dynamic domain strings use structured I18nText models. - Tripartite Rendering Parity: The backend emits the identical inner_sdui_blocks array to both Flutter desktop and WeasyPrint Jinja (report_template.jinja2), verified continuously by automated parity tests (test_sdui_semantic_parity.py and test_sdui_template_parity.py) to guarantee 100% semantic and visual alignment.

docs.title: 2.7. 3rd-Party Semantic Sandboxing & Desktop Accessibility
docs.text: Complex 3rd-party visual components (specifically fl_chart radar charts, scatter plots, and multi-axis graphs) are strictly isolated from the accessibility tree: - ExcludeSemantics Boundary: Visual charts are wrapped inside Flutter's ExcludeSemantics(), acting purely as decorative visual canvases. This prevents 3rd-party chart engines from polluting the screen reader tree with unlocalized coordinate spam (specifically "X: 0.5, Y: 1.2"). - Adjacent Textual Representation: Accessible descriptions, metric lists, and tabular summaries are rendered as standard accessible Flutter widgets (Semantics, Text) placed adjacently, driven directly by backend SDUI data. - Desktop Windows UI Automation (UIA) Protection: Custom interactive widgets and expandable cards utilize excludeSemantics: Platform.isWindows or universal semantic sandboxing on Windows Desktop to prevent cyclical or non-standard render object trees from crashing Windows UI Automation.

docs.title: 2.8. SDUI Dynamic Schema Builder Registry Pattern
docs.text: Structured output schemas for dynamic LLM steps are governed through a decentralized Strategy and Registry architecture in the core schema registry: - Strategy Decoupling: Each distinct presentation type (markdown, hero_insight, grid) implements a dedicated SchemaBuilderStrategy registered via @register_sdui_schema('type'). - Central Registry SSOT: _SDUI_SCHEMA_REGISTRY is the Single Source of Truth for schema resolution. Unknown schema types trigger an immediate Fail-Fast AppException with ErrorCodes.INVALID_OUTPUT_SCHEMA. - Single Registration Collision Defense: The decorator validates that type keys are unique, preventing registration collisions and module import race conditions. - Deterministic Schema Compilation Caching: SchemaFactory caches dynamically compiled Pydantic models in _schema_cache using composite keys (criteria IDs, document IDs, dynamic keys, schema name, locale, strictness), preventing repetitive runtime create_model() compilation overhead in large DAG loops.

docs.title: 2.9. Studio 3-Zone Workflow Governance & Visual Design System
docs.text: The Studio interface provides visual management of workflows, steps, and output profiles: - 3-Zone Pipeline Governance: 1. Zone A (Input Anchors): Ingestion steps, source document bindings, and immutable input sources. 2. Zone B (Dynamic Specialists): Configurable analytical steps, prompt blocks, and upstream dependency wiring. 3. Zone C (Funnel Anchors): Downstream scoring, synthesis generation, and forensic explanation reporting with multi-source aggregation. - System Core Protection: Foundational steps marked with is_system_core: true display locked visual indicators, hide deletion buttons, and prevent accidental mutation of core system hooks. - Server-Driven Step Zone Classification & Dumb Painter UI: Workflow step cards (WorkflowStepCard) and step tabs (WorkflowStepsTab) operate strictly as Dumb Painters. Step zone classification, deletion locks (canDelete = step.zone == StepZone.zoneB && !step.isSystemCore), and visual layout are driven directly by backend step.zone (StepZone SSOT: zone_a, zone_b, zone_c), completely eliminating client-side index heuristics and positional math. Workflow step authoring in WorkflowBuilderView isolates blueprint selection via allBlueprintsProvider (StepFilterScope.all), ensuring workflow authoring remains decoupled from dashboard filter scope state. - Unified Visual Design System: All Studio management views enforce consistent Card containers (elevation: 2, BorderRadius.circular(12)), interactive FilterChip/ChoiceChip selectors, pill-shaped status badges, standardized action triggers, and 100% Theme.of(context) color token adherence. - Bilingual Editing Parity (I18nText): Dynamic ontology strings are edited simultaneously in baseline English and localized Finnish, maintaining referential integrity across locales.

docs.title: 2.10. System Audit Trail & Explainable AI (XAI) Transparency
docs.text: In accordance with international AI transparency regulations (specifically EU AI Act Articles 12-15): - Immutable MCPAuditTrace: External tool calls, web searches, and MCP gateway interactions capture full parameter inputs, responses, latency, and status in immutable MCPAuditTrace records. - Data Leak Prevention (DLP): Raw user prompts, API keys, and sensitive tokens are scrubbed and sanitized before SDUI serialization. - Auditable Presentation: Audit records are serialized via McpAuditAdapter into SduiAuditTrailBlock and displayed to users as structured, verifiable execution traces. - XAI Qualitative Extensions: Analytical reasoning traces and evidence quotes are structured into HighlightBoxDisplay cards and AlertBlock components, providing clear provenance for every score and recommendation.

docs.title: 2.11. Desktop Pro-Tool Studio Input Architecture & Modular Component Foundation
docs.text: Studio matrix and rubric authoring surfaces enforce desktop-class ergonomics, de-stringified inputs, and state loss prevention: - Adaptive Master Selector Navigation: In complex editors (specifically matrix scale modals), claims are isolated into single cognitive units with a lateral sticky sidebar (viewports >= 900px) or horizontal choice chip selector (< 900px), with real-time status badges and cross-claim error navigation. - 5-Card Semantic Hierarchy: Editor canvases group inputs into 5 visual cards (elevation: 2, BorderRadius.circular(12), fontSize: 20, fontWeight: FontWeight.bold): 1. Core Hypothesis & Scope, 2. Reasoning Chain & Anti-Patterns, 3. Contrastive Calibration, 4. Lexical Anchors & Fast Falsification, 5. Aggregation & Reverse Polarity. - Modular SSOT Sub-Widgets: - TagChipInput: Tokenized chip collection implementing the Dual-Shield FormField architecture. Automatically commits pending text buffers upon focus loss, FormField.save(), FormField.validate(), Enter, comma, or Tab, preventing keystroke evaporation when clicking save or triggering shortcuts (Ctrl+S). Enforces bounded chip layout (maxWidth: 240px, ellipsis, hover tooltip). - DynamicItemListEditor: Discrete numbered step cards for reasoning criteria and disqualifying anti-patterns, eliminating brittle newline delimiter splitting. - ContrastivePairEditor: Dedicated two-field editor for ContrastivePairDTO (acceptable vs rejected), with real-time character counters, semantic color accents, and responsive vertical stacking when pane width < 520px. - LinguisticShieldBanner: Non-blocking warning banner powered by a two-phase LinguisticShieldDetector (Unicode check outside Basic Latin with typographical whitelist + target-language grammatical stopword gate), alerting authors when non-English text is entered into prompt instructions without blocking submission. - McpToolParamsPanel: Schema-driven parameter configuration panel (mcp_tool_params_panel.dart) embedded in StepBuilderView. Dynamically inspects parameter declarations in AllowedMcpTool.inputSchema.properties for allowed tools on the step, filtering out dynamic query variables (query, q, search_query, search_term), and renders strongly typed interactive controls: dropdown selectors for enums, switches for booleans, bounded numeric text fields for integers and floats, and constrained text fields for strings. Parameter mutations synchronize reactively through onParamsChanged, emitting typed override maps into step.mcpToolParams with full Flutter Theme Sovereignty. - Shared XML Prompt Preview SSOT (PromptPreviewDialog): The shared PromptPreviewDialog widget (prompt_preview_dialog.dart) and pure PromptPreviewFormatter utilities provide a unified, desktop-class 3-tab syntax modal (BoxConstraints(minWidth: 600, maxWidth: 1000, minHeight: 500, maxHeight: 800)) with monospace typography and system font fallbacks (Courier, Consolas), serving both matrix scale rubrics and workflow step simulations: 1. Static Directive Prefix (previewPromptStaticTab): Displays system instructions, academic theory grounding, and context documents compiled as the cacheable prefix. 2. Dynamic Claims & Rules (previewPromptDynamicTab): Displays CDATA-shielded criteria, anti-patterns, and contrastive examples for the active rubric or step. 3. Compiled Prompt & Schema (previewPromptSchemaTab): Displays expected response JSON schemas, tools configuration, and full compiled output prompts. - Workflow Step Simulation Architecture (StepSimulationDialog): Authoring workflow steps in StepBuilderView features interactive step-level dry-run simulation via StepSimulationDialog (step_simulation_dialog.dart): - Dynamic Input Form Generation: Dynamically generates dedicated TextFormField controls for every input key declared in step.expectedInputs, alongside sample context document text editing and target locale selection (en / fi). - Responsive Desktop Layout: Enforces bounded constraints (minWidth: 640, maxWidth: 1100, minHeight: 550, maxHeight: 850) with an adaptive two-pane layout on wide viewports (>= 900px, 380px left input config vs right tabbed preview) and single-column tabbed layout on compact viewports (< 900px). - Execution Telemetry & Validation: Displays real-time execution duration in milliseconds, estimated BPE token metrics (~N), and structured validation error banners when referenced prompt blocks are missing or input configurations are invalid. - Two-Tier Information Architecture for XAI Extensions (XaiExtensionsBlockCard): Output Profile authoring partitions XAI extension chips into two distinct semantic visual zones: 1. Macro Synthesis & Reporting: Run-level extensions synthesized across the entire execution trace (riskFlag, emotionalSentiment, theoryLink, confidence, justification), accompanied by subtitle description. 2. Micro Atom Enrichments: Observation-level enrichments extracted directly from individual matrix observations (citation, coaching, falsification, remediationSteps, sourceId, missingContext, contextualOverride), accompanied by subtitle description. Both sections mutate the single authoritative backend array payload.visibleBlockExtensions with zero schema fragmentation, enclosed in bounded Wrap widgets guaranteeing hazard-stripe-free rendering down to 360px viewports. - Scalable Master List Browsing & Virtualization Standard: All master list browsing views utilize virtualized rendering (ListView.builder with prototypeItem for $O(1)$ layout calculation and 60 FPS scrolling), sticky pinned top headers (StudioMasterHeader) integrating real-time search inputs and active item count indicators, and centered 1200px max-width containment (Bounded Canvas Containment), preventing unconstrained canvas stretching on high-resolution displays while maintaining responsive usability across compact and split viewports. - Modal Feedback & Submission Guard: Dialogs eradicate SnackBar popups in favor of modal-internal error surfaces, implement in-flight atomic save debouncing (_isSaving), auto-scroll to invalid fields, and enforce a robust PopScope protocol with serialization-based model dirty checking (jsonEncode(model.toJson()) != initialJson) that prevents false-positive discard dialogs on models utilizing reference identity while intercepting all exit triggers with discard confirmation when uncommitted changes exist. - Studio Pro-Tool Form State Retention & Hook Safety (McpGatewayView): - Unconditional Hook Registration: State hooks (such as useState for in-form alert banners) are registered unconditionally at the top of the widget's build() method, preserving static hook indexing and preventing premature disposal crashes during asynchronous loading and error transitions. - Form State Retention Pattern: The view inspects the controller's asynchronous state using Dart 3 pattern matching, prioritizing AsyncValue(value: final payload?) when formState.hasValue to keep the active form mounted, interactive, and populated with current form data while displaying in-card error banners whenever background operations fail (specifically dynamic tool discovery or gateway submission). Fullscreen ErrorView is reserved strictly for initial cold-load failures (hasValue == false). - Riverpod Asynchronous Transition Standard: In form controllers (specifically McpGatewayForm), background actions update state by re-assigning current data (state = AsyncData(currentPayload)) immediately before transitioning to loading (state = const AsyncLoading()). This activates Riverpod's native asynchronous transition mechanics, ensuring that hasValue remains true and prior state is preserved without calling internal framework methods.

docs.title: 2.12. Matrix Summary Table Architecture & Evaluative Column Mechanics
docs.text:
The matrix summary table (MatrixSummaryTableAdapter / SduiMatrixTableBlock) presents a comparative, multi-matrix evaluation breakdown. The table format is composed of three primary columns:

  1. Logiikkamatriisi (Matrix Identity & Grounding):
  2. Identifies the evaluated dimension with its localized title (specifically Harkintakyky (Kahnemanin Kaksoisprosessiteoria)) and underlying academic theory citation.
  3. Displays the composite star score rating for the matrix.

  4. Exposes an explicit context target input scope badge (specifically Kaikki syötteet for target_input_key: "all", Lopputuote for product_text, or Keskusteluhistoria for chat_log), guaranteeing evidentiary transparency for the user.

  5. Jakauma ($k/N$ Scale Hit Distribution):

  6. Deconstructs the overall evaluation into discrete, empirical BARS scale hit fractions $k/N$.
  7. In each scale row (specifically 1 - Systeemi 1 (Nopea): 5/5, 2 - Siirtymä: 3/5, 3 - Systeemi 2 (Hidas): 2/5), the denominator $N$ represents the total number of TDA assertions defined for that scale tier in the seed vault, while the numerator $k$ represents the count of assertions that achieved PASSED status during blind evaluation.

  8. The overall pass rate is computed as the sum of passed atoms over total atoms (specifically $10/15 = 66.7\%$). The composite normalized score (specifically 1.9 / 3 or 46.3%) is calculated deterministically by the UnifiedScoringEngine using weighted ratio hit distribution and continuous strictness power-curve dampening without subjective LLM scoring.

  9. Selitys (Diagnostic Narrative Synthesis, Contrastive Deficits & Inline Topological Lineage):

  10. Rather than summarizing the entire document, the diagnostic narrative provides a focused, single-sentence explanation of cognitive deficits, prerequisite short-circuits, and performative breakdowns.
  11. During DAG execution, MatrixReducer extracts all completed atom evaluations (PASSED, FAILED, N_A, and DLQ) along with their topological dependency lineage (depends_on_tda_ids, short_circuit_reason_tda_ids, is_inverse_evidence) into ReducedAtomDTO. Concurrently, MatrixExplanationService curates structured MatrixFailureDeficitDTO records for all FAILED and N_A criteria, preserving cognitive evaluation_reasoning, transitive parent-to-child short-circuit blame ([Blocked Claim] <-- SHORT-CIRCUITED BY PREREQUISITE FAILURE: [Parent Claim: <parent evaluation_reasoning>]), anti_patterns, and ContrastivePairDTO exemplars (contrastive_rejected, contrastive_acceptable), while the synthesis worker injects CausalSynthesisBriefDTO across all synthesis tasks.
  12. The synthesis LLM ingests this contrastive and topological deficit context to formulate a diagnostic sentence explaining the exact root-cause failure modes and rubric boundary gaps.
  13. At the presentation layer, MatrixSummaryTableAdapter, CausalGraphAdapter, and BlueprintTransformer attach short_circuited_by_claims: list[str] and falsified_warrant_claims: list[str] inline on SduiMatrixTableBlock, SduiCausalGraphBlock, CausalNodeDTO, and ReportDataDTO (normalized in WeasyPrint Jinja2 PDF templates via normalize_lineage_claims and rendered natively in Flutter Freezed widgets) rather than appending disembodied SduiNACard blocks at the bottom of the report.

docs.title: 2.13. Cross-Surface Presentation Parity & Machine-Readability Standard
docs.text: Presentation rendering across all four surfaces (UI, PDF, Excel, and CSV) operates strictly under Dumb Painter principles, ensuring 100% semantic and numeric alignment: 1. UI and PDF Tab 1 (Matrix Summary Table): - Track A (Developmental Competence): Displays progressive level mastery with positive novice percentages (specifically 17.9% for HACM novice baseline). Jakauma displays standard progression (specifically: 1 - Matkustaja: 2/2, 2 - Reaktiivinen viilaaja: 1/2). - Track B (Diagnostic Error Radars): Normalisoitu pisteytys resolves strictly to 0.0% if no positive mastery is demonstrated on levels 3–5, eliminating the legacy 12.2% phantom score glitch. Jakauma displays explicit diagnostic labels (specifically: 1 - Mahdoton (Kriittinen virhe): 1/1 (Havaittu virhe) when an error occurs, or 0/1 (Puhdas) when clean). 2. UI, PDF Tab 2 and Excel Tab 2 (Forensic Atom Breakdown): - Decoupled semantic badge rules via ReportAtomColumn and is_inverse_evidence: - Positive Claims (is_inverse: false): Passed atom displays +1 p (points_awarded: 1.0); unfulfilled atom displays 0 p (points_awarded: 0.0). - Inverse Claims (is_inverse: true): Passed/clean atom (no error) displays Puhdas (points_awarded: 0.0, zero false positive points); failed/detected error atom displays Negatiivinen löydös with red visual alert, exact lexical quote citation, and triggers orthogonal malus deduction (points_awarded: 0.0). - Multi-Segment Evidence Formatting: When citations contain multiple constituent segments (source_quotes: tuple[str, ...] | None / quotes: list[str]), the segments are formatted and rendered using join(' [...] '). This preserves visual demarcation across non-contiguous excerpts without fabricating contiguous sentences or inserting chimera ellipses. 3. Excel Tab 1 (Yhteenveto): - Standard 13 Columns: Suoritustunniste, Logiikkamatriisi, Arvioinnin kohde, Jakauma, Osumat, Kriteerejä yhteensä, Osumasuhde, Pisteet, Maksimipisteet, Normalisoitu pisteytys, Selitys, Kriteerit, Lähde. - Track B Levels 1–2 hits do NOT count as positive capability points; total hits strictly reflect positive levels 3–5 (specifically: 0 / 8 instead of legacy 3 / 11), aligning normalized score at 0.0%. 4. CSV 22-Column Rectangular Machine-Readability Standard (export_flat_csv): - Rectangular, denormalized, strictly typed 22 columns ordered by ReportHeaderResolver.get_all_denormalized_csv_headers: 1. Suoritustunniste (execution_id), 2. Logiikkamatriisi (matrix_label), 3. Arvioinnin kohde (context_target), 4. Jakauma (distribution), 5. Osumat (hits), 6. Kriteerejä yhteensä (total_atoms), 7. Osumasuhde (hit_ratio), 8. Pisteet (raw_score), 9. Maksimipisteet (scale_max), 10. Normalisoitu pisteytys (normalized_score), 11. Taso (level: 1..5), 12. Tason nimi (level_name), 13. Arviointikriteeri (criterion), 14. Väitetyyppi (claim_type: 'Positiivinen kyvykkyys' vs 'Virhedetektori / Anti-pattern'), 15. Käänteinen ehto (is_inverse: 1 or 0), 16. Saadut pisteet (points_awarded: 1.0 or 0.0), 17. Tulos (result_status: 1 or 0), 18. Tekstin havainto (quotes), 19. Selitys (ai_reasoning), 20. Kausaalistatus (causal_status: ROOT_CAUSE, ISOLATED, BLAMED, NORMAL), 21. Juurisyyn tunnus (blame_parent_id), 22. Riippuvuuksien lkm (dependent_count). - Mathematical scoring identity: points_awarded_val = 1.0 if (atom.status == PASSED and not is_inverse_claim) else 0.0. - Total mathematical insulation for automated ML/data pipelines: SUM(Saadut pisteet) never accumulates error detections as points.

docs.title: 2.14. Studio Workflow Step Topology & Specialist Causal Governance
docs.text: Quorum Studio workflow authoring surfaces (WorkflowStepsTab, WorkflowStepCard) enforce 100% engine symmetry, responsive topological sequencing, and strict relational integrity: - 100% Engine Card Symmetry: All workflow execution nodes (including EngineType.causalDiscovery) are fully visible and editable as first-class Step Cards with explicit status badges, input mapping lists, and dependency chips. - Append-to-Zone-B Authoring Flow: Adding specialist steps appends them directly before the first Zone C funnel anchor (_findFirstZoneCIndex), guaranteeing upstream execution ordering without manual drag-and-drop complexity. - Specialist Causal Source Selector & Full-Duplex Reactive Synchronization: Specialist steps with upstream causal discovery nodes expose a dedicated causal source selector (DropdownButtonFormField<String>). Selecting or modifying the causal source automatically updates stepDef.dependsOn, adding the causal source ID to dependencies and pruning obsolete ones. - Defensive Dropdown Value Guard: Dropdown values enforce defensive scoping: (stepDef.causalSourceStepId != null && allowedCausalIds.contains(stepDef.causalSourceStepId)) ? stepDef.causalSourceStepId : null, preventing Flutter dropdown assertion crashes when referencing unmapped or deleted steps. - Cascading Step Deletion Referential Integrity: Deleting a workflow step automatically scans all remaining steps; if any step referenced the deleted step as its causalSourceStepId, the pointer is reset to null while preserving the step definition. - Flutter Theme Sovereignty: All Studio workflow authoring widgets derive typography and color metrics strictly from Theme.of(context).textTheme and Theme.of(context).colorScheme, eradicating raw TextStyle instantiations, while static UI labels resolve through Axis 1 compile-time .arb localization keys (studioWorkflowCausalSourceLabel, studioWorkflowCausalSourceNone).

docs.title: 2.15. Studio Workflow Strictness Controls & Epistemic Decoupling (WorkflowStrictnessTab)
docs.text: Workflow strictness authoring in Quorum Studio exposes Gate 5 Epistemic Strictness Decoupling within WorkflowBuilderView Tab 4 (WorkflowStrictnessTab), featuring independent continuous sliders (0–100%) for both Matrix Scoring Strictness (defaultStrictnessLevel) and Lexical Verification Strictness (defaultLexicalStrictnessLevel). The interface renders four calibrated consequence zones: - Free Zone ($0 \le S \le 30$): Free scoring dampening ($e(S) \in [1.00, 1.15]$) and relaxed lexical verification ($\tau_{\text{tier}} = 60.0\%$, Snowball stemming enabled). - Normal Zone ($30 < S \le 50$): Balanced scoring dampening ($e(S) \in [1.15, 1.25]$) and standard lexical threshold ($\tau_{\text{tier}} = 67.5\%$). - Strict Zone ($50 < S \le 85$): Rigorous scoring dampening ($e(S) \in [1.25, 1.70]$) and calibrated lexical threshold ($\tau_{\text{tier}} = 75.0\%$). - Absolute Zero-Trust Zone ($85 < S \le 100$): Uncompromising score dampening ($e(S) \in [1.70, 2.20]$) and strict lexical verification ($\tau_{\text{tier}} = 76.5\%$ for $S < 100$, jumping to $100.0\%$ exact-match only at $S = 100$, where all stemming and approximate fallbacks are completely deactivated). Both sliders operate with full Flutter Theme Sovereignty, live numerical indicators, and compile-time .arb localization keys, maintaining complete decoupling between scoring rigor and evidentiary citation thresholds.

docs.title: 2.16. Interactive Causal Discovery Canvas (CausalInspectorModal)
docs.text: Presentation of extracted argument graphs integrates an interactive desktop modal (CausalInspectorModal) accessible directly from SduiCausalGraphWidget. Built with Flutter Desktop ergonomics: - Interactive Pro Tool Canvas: Utilizes InteractiveViewer with constrained scaling ($0.5\times$ to $2.5\times$) and smooth panning, rendering directed dependency edges and Toulmin backing warrants ($X \xrightarrow{\mathbf{W}_{XY}} Y$). - Topological Node State Indicators: Nodes display distinctive visual tokens for root causes (ROOT_CAUSE), blamed downstream nodes (BLAMED), and warrant grounding failures (WARRANT_GROUNDING_FAILURE). - Inspection Detail Drawer: Selecting an argument node reveals its verbatim text citations, Toulmin backing warrants, parent dependencies, and child reachability cascade. - Theme Sovereignty & Containment: Renders with 100% Theme.of(context) color and typography tokens, wrapped in AppErrorBoundary to prevent any visualization anomaly from compromising the primary dashboard.

docs.title: 2.17. Deterministic Presentation Sanitization & Dumb Painter Evidence Grounding (McpPresentationSanitizer)
docs.text: To preserve Dumb Painter parity and prevent raw protocol artifacts, CDATA envelopes, or technical payloads from reaching client views or PDF reports, presentation layers enforce server-side text sanitization: - Presentation Pre-Sanitization Pipeline: All external tool findings and audit traces rendered in executive reports flow through McpPresentationSanitizer.sanitize_finding (backend_v2/services/sdui/sanitizers/mcp_presentation_sanitizer.py) before entering SDUI blocks or template payloads (ReportDataDTO.mcp_audit_data). - Structured Payload Extraction: The sanitizer automatically detects and extracts substantive finding text from JSON response payloads using Pydantic V2 Rust deserialization (MCPStructuredContentDTO.model_validate_json(strict=False)), inspecting standard content attributes (content, snippet, text, summary, answer, description, finding, message) without naked dictionary parsing. - Envelope & Markup Stripping: Envelopes such as XML CDATA wrappers (<![CDATA[...]]>) and Markdown code fences (json`,) are cleanly removed, HTML tags are stripped, whitespace is normalized, and surrounding quotes are unwrapped. - Sentence-Boundary Character Budgeting: Text length is capped strictly at sentence boundaries within configured character budgets (settings.mcp_presentation_max_chars, default 300) via enforce_sentence_boundary_budget, ensuring excerpts never terminate mid-word or mid-sentence. - Terminal Punctuation Guarantee: All sanitized findings deterministically conclude on terminal punctuation (., !, ?). Non-extractable, empty, or whitespace-only inputs evaluate to None, allowing presentation templates (report_template.jinja2) and adapters (PrintableSourcesAdapter) to omit empty evidence lines cleanly. - Evidentiary Integrity Preservation: Sanitization applies exclusively to presentation summaries (response_summary). Verbatim claims (claim_text), search queries (query), source URLs (source_urls), and raw forensic audit events remain permanently immutable.
