SSOT Implementation Plan — Work Package 2 (WP2) Tavoite: Nostaa koko koodikanta natiivien Python 3.12–3.14+ tyyppitysominaisuuksien tasolle staattisen analyysin (MyPy strict / IDE) ja kääntöaikaisen turvallisuuden maksimoimiseksi. Korvataan perinteinen periytyminen (ABC) rakenteellisella tyypityksellä (Protocol), suojataan rajapintatoteutukset @override-dekoraattoreilla (PEP 698) ja modernisoidaan tyyppisyntaksit (PEP 695).

@[.agents/rules/00-antigravity-core.md] @[.agents/rules/01-python-backend.md] @[.agents/rules/04_directory_reference.md] @[.agents/rules/05_llm_architecture.md] @[ki_zero_permissive_typing.md] @[ki_ast_guardrail_engine.md] @[ki_python_314_concurrency_strictness.md] @[ki_god_code_prevention.md]

- Do NOT use legacy abc.ABC or @abstractmethod where structural typing.Protocol can achieve loose coupling (schema_convergence_mandate). - Do NOT implement protocol or base class methods without explicit @override (PEP 698) annotations (modern_type_aliases_pep695). - Do NOT use legacy TypeVar, Generic[T], Optional[X], Union[A, B], or TypeAlias in new or refactored code (python_314_modern_syntax). - Do NOT introduce duck-typing (getattr/hasattr/isinstance(dict)) during protocol modernizations (the_zero_compromise_pledge). - Do NOT break runtime introspection in FastAPI, Pydantic, or dependency injection containers (acyclic_top_level_import_invariant). - Do NOT leave # noqa: QGR... suppressions or bypass AST guardrails without explicit architectural justification (the_duct_tape_ban).

docs.title: 1. Problem Statement & Nykytilan Haasteet
docs.text:
1. Jäykkä Periytyminen (abc.ABC & @abstractmethod):
  2. backend_v2/llm/adapters/base_adapter.py käyttää perinteistä class BaseLLMAdapter(ABC) -abstraktioluokkaa. Tämä luo kiinteän periytymishierarkian ja vaikeuttaa kevyiden, tilattomien testifakien ja erillisten adaptereiden kytkemistä.
  3. Kääntöaikaisen Ylikirjoitusturvan Puute (PEP 698 – @override):
  4. Suurin osa Protocol-toteutuksista (9 tietokantarepositoriota, 4 LLM-adapteria, SDUI-adapterit) toteuttaa metodit ilman @override-dekoraattoria. Jos interfaces.py:n tai LLMAdapter-protokollan metodisignatuuri muuttuu (esim. parametri poistetaan tai nimetään uudelleen), tyyppitarkastin ei aina varoita toteutuksesta, mikä johtaa ajonaikaisiin virheisiin (TypeError: unexpected keyword argument).
  5. Vanhentunut Tyyppisyntaksi (PEP 484 vs. PEP 695):
  6. Koodikannassa esiintyy edelleen hajallaan TypeVar("T"), Generic[T], Optional[T] ja Union[A, B] (esim. chunking.py, auth.py, handler.py, ingress_pipeline.py).
  7. Python 3.12–3.14+ tarjoaa natiivin PEP 695 type-aliassyntaksin ja class Foo[T: BaseModel]: -syntaksin, joka on suorituskykyisempi, siistimpi ja paremmin MyPy/IDE-tuettu.

docs.title: 2.1 Abstraktiot $\rightarrow$ typing.Protocol
docs.text: • Muutetaan BaseLLMAdapter LLMAdapter(Protocol) -muotoon. Konkreettiset adapterit eivät enää periydy suoraan perusluokasta, vaan toteuttavat protokollan vaatimat metodit (prepare_payload, calculate_cost, extract_token_usage).

docs.title: 2.2 Ylikirjoitusturva $\rightarrow$ @override
docs.text: • Merkitään kaikki protokollia tai rajapintoja toteuttavat metodit @override-dekoraattorilla. Tämä takaa 100 % suojan refaktorointien aiheuttamia signatuurieroja vastaan.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Harden the cognitive evaluation architecture across the Single Source of Truth (SSOT) data vault @[backend_v2/seed/seed_data.json], the Python backend (backend_v2), the Flutter client (client_app_v2), and the E2E variance test harness (scripts/run_e2e_variance_test.py and scripts/diff_executions.py).

This unified plan eliminates inter-model epistemic divergence between Google Gemini 3.8 Flash and OpenAI GPT-5.1 on Sitra foresight strategy (data/test_inputs_sitra) and hybrid work dialogue (docs/jwdatat) corpuses by: 1. Disambiguating Upper Bloom & Kahneman Matrices: Ontologically hardening Level 5 Criteria Anchoring (tda_5198e13cde3447fe9d0737a80abe458c), Level 6 Creation (tda_07ef835fd139e70fd9d9f2151dc9a5aa), Scale 1 Qualitative Association (tda_ab3ebf5a42f0d72eca9acceeb2e12ce1), and Scale 2 Deliberative Pause (tda_5fc55ef72665907c426e2598cddde565) with strict anti-patterns and contrastive pairs. 2. Eliminating Infrastructure Coupling via Provider-Agnostic Cognitive Tiers: Replacing legacy freeform string strategies ("fast", "deep", "reasoning", "synthesis", "openai_strict") with a typed CognitiveTier ontology (FAST, BALANCED, DEEP, REASONING) mapped across multiple model providers (GOOGLE, OPENAI, ANTHROPIC). 3. Establishing Computational Reasoning Symmetry: Symmetrizing thinking token budgets across providers (e.g. OpenAI DEEP tier allocated 4,096 thinking tokens mapping to reasoning_effort: "medium" to symmetrically match Gemini DEEP). 4. Calibrating Execution Strictness & Eliminating Phantom Penalties: Upgrading Workflow 3 to default_strictness_level: 70 ($e = 1.5071$) and synchronously wiring "enforce_passivity_penalty" into Step 4 Coach post_hooks alongside passivity_penalty: 0.05. 5. Modernizing Quorum Studio UI: Refactoring step_builder_view.dart to present vendor-neutral Cognitive Tiers with dynamic resolution badges, isolating workflow authors from infrastructure churn and replacing hardcoded sizing doubles with design tokens. 6. Enforcing Pure Telemetry & Report Transparency: Upgrading run_e2e_variance_test.py and diff_executions.py to always report real provider names (Google Vertex AI, OpenAI), allowed token ceilings (max_tokens, thinking_budget_tokens, reasoning_effort), rate limits (tpm_limit, rpm_limit), and human-readable names, strictly banning raw database IDs (wf_..., sp_..., sys_...) and abstract top-level strategy aliases (evaluation_strategy, test_strategy) in report headlines. 7. Enabling Scientific Cross-Provider E2E Variance Testing: Upgrading run_e2e_variance_test.py with --providers support, allowing sequential multi-provider runs that preserve step-level cognitive tier differentiation without brutal environment variable flattening.

docs.title: User Review Required
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] Measure 1 Token & Latency Budget Decision: Step 2 (Archivist) evaluates 30 atoms in Bloom's Taxonomy. Under Best-of-3 ensemble evaluation (3 parallel calls per atom = 90 total calls), assigning strategy REASONING (8,192 thinking tokens) would generate up to $90 \times 8,192 \approx 737,280$ thinking tokens in Step 2 alone. This would multiply total workflow thinking tokens by nearly $6\times$, triggering 60 RPM Gemini rate limits and causing Arq worker job timeouts ($>15$ minutes). Approved Solution: Step 2 is upgraded to CognitiveTier.DEEP (thinking_budget_tokens: 4096), which provides structured analytical reasoning depth within safe latency ($<180$ seconds) and token limits.

[!CAUTION] Measure 2 Empirical Falsification & Architecture Ban: The proposal to disable Best-of-3 on baseline levels (Bloom 1–2, Kahneman 1) was empirically falsified by diff_report_2026-09-16_1314.md. Level 1 atoms (tda_216cc3fd... and tda_ab3ebf5a...) had 0.0% consistency and maximum entropy (1.000). Baseline levels test dogmatic statements and intuitive heuristics, not mechanical regex. Furthermore, backend_v2/tests/unit/seed/test_matrix_anchoring_rules.py:230 enforces 100% high_entropy: true across all 305 matrix atoms. Best-of-3 remains 100% active on all atoms.

[!WARNING] Measure 4 Phantom Penalty Trap: Setting passivity_penalty = 0.05 on wf_03a1d71000000003 without adding "enforce_passivity_penalty" to Step 4 (sp_25664f44773a4354) post_hooks is a silent NO-OP because no step in Workflow 3 emits the passivity_detected flag (Step 7 Judge is not present in Workflow 3). Both must be updated synchronously.

[!NOTE] Telemetry & Reporting Mandate: All reporting and CLI outputs across run_e2e_variance_test.py and diff_executions.py MUST report concrete physical reality: actual provider, allowed token capacity ceilings (max_tokens, thinking_budget_tokens, reasoning_effort, tpm_limit, rpm_limit), and human-readable localized names. Printing raw opaque IDs (wf_..., sp_..., sys_...) or abstract strategy wrapper aliases (evaluation_strategy, test_strategy) in report headlines is strictly banned.

docs.title: 5-Column Architectural Directives Table
Anti-Happy-Path Test Scenarios
docs.text:
1. Negative Scenario 1 (Thematic Grouping Rejection): A submission clusters diverse source items into umbrella pillars without an explicit operational or causal mechanism. The evaluator MUST evaluate tda_07ef835fd139e70fd9d9f2151dc9a5aa as FAILED.
  2. Negative Scenario 2 (Passive Mandate Citation Rejection): A submission lists regulatory directives as compliance obligations without benchmarking observed telemetry against their explicit limits. The evaluator MUST evaluate tda_5198e13cde3447fe9d0737a80abe458c as FAILED.
  3. Negative Scenario 3 (The Lazy Observer Reflection Pass Rejection): A user allows multi-persona dialogue to run unmonitored, then writes in reflection: "Pysähdyin pohtimaan, että olisiko pitänyt rajata tarkemmin." The evaluator MUST evaluate tda_5fc55ef72665907c426e2598cddde565 as FAILED.
  4. Negative Scenario 4 (Quoted Metaphor Attribution Fallacy Rejection): A user pastes an external report into the chat containing narrative metaphors ("Sitran näkemyksen mukaan tulevaisuus ei vain vyöry päälle..."). The evaluator MUST evaluate tda_ab3ebf5a42f0d72eca9acceeb2e12ce1 as FAILED.
  5. Negative Scenario 5 (Provider Capability Asymmetry Guard): An unconfigured provider or model without thinking capabilities is assigned to CognitiveTier.DEEP. Pre-flight validation fails fast with ValidationError, requiring explicit thinking_budget_tokens > 0 for deep/reasoning tiers.
  6. Negative Scenario 6 (Partial Provider Registration Guard): A provider is registered in seed_data.json with only FAST and BALANCED configured. Pre-flight dry-run fails fast with ValidationError, asserting that every provider must implement all four canonical CognitiveTiers.
  7. Negative Scenario 7 (Reasoning Latency & Token Explosion Guard): Step 2 (Archivist) is assigned CognitiveTier.DEEP (4,096 tokens), rejecting REASONING (8,192 tokens), capping thinking tokens to $\approx 368,000$ and preventing Arq worker timeouts and 60 RPM Gemini rate limits.
  8. Negative Scenario 8 (Phantom Penalty Silent Bypass Guard): Setting passivity_penalty = 0.05 on wf_03a1d71000000003 without adding "enforce_passivity_penalty" to Step 4 Coach post_hooks is prevented by synchronous verification.
  9. Negative Scenario 9 (Opaque ID & Top-Level Name Leaks in Telemetry Guard): Automated assertion in test suite verifying that report headers in diff_executions.py and startup telemetry in run_e2e_variance_test.py strictly print human-readable localized names, real providers, and explicit token limits (max_tokens, thinking_budget, tpm_limit, rpm_limit), and contain zero raw database IDs or abstract strategy aliases in headlines.

docs.text: Provide a unified, highly intuitive Model Registry interface and robust backend discovery engine in Quorum: 1. Google AI Studio (Direct Gemini API): Support fetching and running Google models directly via GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY without requiring GCP service accounts, project IDs, or regional constraints. 2. Google Vertex AI Multi-Region: Allow selecting target GCP regions (specifically: europe-north1 [Hamina, FI], europe-west1 [Belgium], europe-west4 [Netherlands], europe-west3 [Frankfurt], us-central1 [Iowa], us-east4 [Virginia]) dynamically from the UI, executing existing parallel validation in the chosen region. 3. When Google Vertex AI is chosen, present the Location dropdown. Dynamically fetch and populate available models based on the selected platform and location. 4. docs.title: 2. Tri-Axis Dialectical Audit & Root Cause Analysis
Root Cause Analysis
docs.text:
• Root Cause: Historically, model discovery in LLMHandler was coupled strictly to GCP service account authentication and the single settings.vertex_location. Users wanting to evaluate Gemini models via direct API keys (Google AI Studio) or test deployment availability across alternative European/US GCP regions were blocked by hardcoded region lookups and missing dual-path platform filtering.
  • Architectural Justification: Decoupling platform selection (LLMPlatformType) and regional targeting (GCPVertexLocation) in LLMHandler while maintaining strict Pydantic DTOs and Riverpod provider families guarantees 100% Fail-Fast deterministic routing across Enterprise (Vertex) and Developer (AI Studio) pipelines.

docs.title: Tri-Axis Dialectical Audit
docs.text:
1. PROSECUTION (Over-Engineering & YAGNI Advocate):
  2. Attack: Why introduce a dedicated /locations endpoint and family-based Riverpod providers instead of just hardcoding region strings in the Flutter UI?
  3. Mandatory Deletion Test: If /locations endpoint were cut, Flutter would rely on client-side hardcoded strings. If GCP adds a region, client and backend drift immediately. Centralizing GCPVertexLocation in backend enums.py and exposing GET studio/model-registry/locations guarantees backend SSOT authority.
  4. DEFENSE (Architectural Sovereignty & Fail-Fast Advocate):
  5. Defense: Strict separation of LLMPlatformType (vertex_ai, ai_studio, openai, anthropic) and GCPVertexLocation prevents string mismatches, ensures Pydantic validation on query parameters, and avoids the catastrophic "e.g." ban in configuration models.
  6. REALIST (Duct-Tape & Blast Radius Interrogator):

Blast Radius: We must verify LLMFactory.create_provider and VertexCacheAdapter so that setting vertex_location dynamically in strategy additional_params doesn't collide with settings.vertex_location. docs.title: Architectural Implementation Plan: Zero-XML UI & Automated Prompt Assembly Pipeline
1.1 Context & Motivation
docs.text:
In Quorum, cognitive evaluation relies on foundational LLMs (Gemini, Claude) instructed via Server-Driven Prompts. Currently, the Studio UI exposes raw text fields (ai_description) across dozens of granular prompt blocks (specifically: system_rule, matrix, role, protocol, execution_persona), requiring humans to understand and manually construct XML tags (<banned_concepts>, <role_enforcement>, <theory_context>) and ALL-CAPS directive anchors.

Furthermore, Studio Steps currently associate up to 27 redundant, fine-grained system_rule blocks (specifically: block_headermandates, block_mandate2..5, block_headerrules, block_rule1..6, block_oprule1..3, block_headerinstructions, block_instructionlanguage_dynamic), creating UI clutter, cognitive overload, and fragile prompt configurations.

docs.title: 1.2 The Architectural Goal: Zero-XML UI & Automated Prompt Assembly
docs.text:
1. Zero-XML UI: The human user in Studio UI or Matrix Editor writes pure, natural text and structured lists (specifically: objective, list of banned_concepts, evaluation_rules, role_enforcement, and theory_grounding citations). The user NEVER writes raw XML tags.
  2. Deterministic Prompt Compilation (Clean Stack Model): The backend compiler (PromptFactory, LocalizationCompiler, MatrixSensorPromptBuilder) deterministically assembles these structured models into a 100% Context Caching-compliant, 4-tier XML hierarchy.
  3. Global Mandates SSOT: Universal system rules (Null Hypothesis, Anti-Score, Anti-ID, Epistemic Glossary, Semantic Bleed, Verbatim Extraction, Extension Anchoring, Tone, Schema Purity, Context Segregation, Language Mandates) are injected automatically from global_mandates.py without requiring manual block selection in the Studio UI.
  4. Preserve Dynamic Matrix Creation: Creating new matrices remains 100% dynamic, plug-and-play, and decoupled from underlying system rules.

SESSION EXECUTION PLAN: This plan MUST be executed across 3 separate /tier2-execute sessions: - Session A: Phase 1 + Phase 2 (Backend Models + Compiler Layer) - Session B: Phase 3 (Seed Data Simplification) - Session C: Phase 4 + Phase 5 (Flutter UI + Tests)

docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ LAYER 1: GLOBAL SYSTEM INVARIANTS (Automated by Backend)                    │
│   Source: backend_v2/models/prompts/global_mandates.py                      │
│   Injected into: static prefix (100% Gemini Context Cacheable)              │
│   Tags: <global_system_mandates> containing:                                │
│         <language_mandate>, <anti_score_mandate>, <anti_id_mandate>,        │
│         <epistemic_glossary>, <semantic_bleed_mandate>,                     │
│         <null_hypothesis_mandate>, <verbatim_extraction_mandate>,           │
│         <extension_anchoring_mandate>, <tone_mandate>,                      │
│         <schema_purity_mandate>, <context_segregation_mandate>              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 2: STEP GOVERNANCE & PROTOCOLS (Configured in Step Blueprint)         │
│   - <EXECUTION_PERSONA>: How LLM parses (Deterministic Parser or XAI)      │
│   - <ROLE_DIRECTIVE>: Operational mode (Prosecutor, Analyst, or Coach)      │
│   - <EXTRACTION_PROTOCOL>: Evidence extraction rules (Zero-Trust Quotes)    │
│   - <TASK_DIRECTIVES>: Step-specific heuristics (Passivity, PII, Tone)      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 3: DOMAIN CRITERIA MATRIX (Configured in Matrix PromptBlock)          │
│   - <CRITERIA_GUIDELINES> containing:                                       │
│     - <objective>: Pure rubric objective string                             │
│     - <evaluation_rules>: Specific evaluation boundaries                    │
│     - <banned_concepts>: Explicit negative heuristics                       │
│     - <role_enforcement>: Role enforcement directive                        │
│     - <theory_context>: Verbatim academic citation (from TheoryGrounding)   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ LAYER 4: DYNAMIC CLAIMS & EVIDENCE PAYLOAD (Per-Execution Dynamic Tail)     │
│   - <execution_context>: Target locale, document date, mechanical anchors   │
│   - <context>: User source document (HTML-escaped, cached)                  │
│   - <user_payload>: LinkedAtomGraph nodes with obfuscated aliases (a0..an)  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: Universal Eradication of Legacy UUIDv4 Generators & Full 32-Hex RFC 9562 UUIDv7 Enforcement
1. Objective & Architectural Background
docs.text:
Following the universal 32-character hexadecimal RFC 9562 UUIDv7 cutover (OPAQUE_STRIPE_ID_REGEX = r"^([a-z]{2,5})_[a-fA-F0-9]{32}$" and parse_prefixed_uuid7(..., enforce_v7=True) in @[backend_v2/models/core_base.py#L230-L279]), residual side-paths in both the Flutter desktop client (client_app_v2/lib/) and the Python backend (backend_v2/) still invoke legacy Uuid().v4() and uuid.uuid4() generators:

  1. Flutter Studio Client Side-Path Failures (Uuid().v4() and 16-Hex Truncations):
  2. @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/workflow/workflow_steps_tab.dart] (_addStep at line 43 and _copyStep at line 74) generates Uuid().v4() and truncates sr_ identifiers to 16 hex characters (uuidHex.characters.take(16)), which fails backend 32-hex StepRule.id validation upon saving a workflow.
  3. @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/profile/blocks/matrix_graphs_block_card.dart] (_addGroup at line 165) and @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/profile/layout_editor_card.dart] (_addGroup at line 30) generate grp_ identifiers via const Uuid().v4().replaceAll('-', '').substring(0, 16) (violating both DGR008 .substring() and backend 32-hex MatrixSynthesisGroup.id validation).
  4. @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/utils/workflow_cloner.dart] (line 54) generates 16-hex sr_ IDs via _uuid.v4().replaceAll('-', '').substring(0, 16) (violating DGR008).
  5. @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/models/prompt_block.dart] (TDAAssertion.create at line 172) generates a 32-hex tda_ ID using const Uuid().v4(), embedding version nibble 4 instead of RFC 9562 version 7.
  6. @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/scale_editor_modal.dart] (_previewScalePrompt at line 173) uses a 16-zero placeholder 'blk_0000000000000000', which fails backend 32-hex PromptBlockBase.id validation during scale prompt preview.

  7. @[client_app_v2/lib/utils/json_converters.dart] (StrictOpaqueIdConverter at line 58) still permits {16,32} hex characters instead of enforcing {32}.

  8. Backend Side-Path Failures (uuid.uuid4() Version 4 & Truncated Hex):

  9. Domain model default_factory lambdas in @[backend_v2/models/auth.py] (Organization.id at line 90, User.id at line 235), @[backend_v2/models/domain/base.py] (UsageRecord.id at line 286), @[backend_v2/models/domain/matrix.py] (TDAAssertion.tda_id at line 130), @[backend_v2/models/chunking.py] (Chunk.id at line 42), and @[backend_v2/models/state.py] (TraceEvent.event_id at line 163, WorkflowState.execution_id at line 316) call uuid.uuid4().
  10. Service, repository, hook, and LLM modules (@[backend_v2/services/auth/organization_service.py#L79-L140], @[backend_v2/services/auth/user_service.py#L96-L221], @[backend_v2/services/usage_service.py#L121-L213], @[backend_v2/services/orchestrator/two_pass_atomizer.py#L254-L357], @[backend_v2/services/orchestrator/dag_executor/workflow_bootstrap_stage.py#L321-L380], @[backend_v2/services/mcp/dispatcher.py#L529-L627], @[backend_v2/services/drivers/local_file_driver.py#L105-L169], @[backend_v2/database/repositories/audit.py], @[backend_v2/database/repositories/execution.py#L31-L95], @[backend_v2/database/repositories/knowledge.py], @[backend_v2/hooks/linguistics.py#L77-L222], @[backend_v2/hooks/llm.py#L25-L159], @[backend_v2/hooks/references.py#L33-L82], @[backend_v2/llm/client.py#L127-L309], @[backend_v2/llm/mock_data.py#L411-L491], @[backend_v2/llm/provider/litellm_response_stage.py#L62-L284]) invoke uuid.uuid4(), which either produces version-4 UUIDs rejected by PostgresEntityAdapter (parse_prefixed_uuid7(..., enforce_v7=True)) or 8/16-hex truncated strings.

This plan extracts a canonical generate_uuid7() helper in @[backend_v2/models/core_base.py] and generateOpaqueUuid7(String prefix) in @[client_app_v2/lib/utils/json_converters.dart], migrates every production and test-factory uuid4() / .v4() call to RFC 9562 UUIDv7, and adds static AST (QGR030) and Dart (DGR008) guardrails banning uuid4 and .v4(.

docs.title: 3. Pre-Implementation Technical Debt Cleanups (Phase 1)
docs.text: Running scripts/audit_technical_debt.py on the target scope identified 4 FATAL violations in touched Flutter Studio files and 1 unscoped stdlib mock in test_references.py: 1. DGR008 (Banned .substring() clipping) in @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/utils/workflow_cloner.dart] (line 54), @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/profile/blocks/matrix_graphs_block_card.dart] (line 165), and @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/profile/layout_editor_card.dart] (line 30): Resolved in Step 1 by replacing .v4().replaceAll('-', '').substring(0, 16) with generateOpaqueUuid7(...). 2. DGR003 (Banned hardcoded string literal in Text()) in @[client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/widgets/profile/layout_editor_card.dart] (line 134): Resolved in Step 1 by replacing Text('${index + 1}', ...) with Text((index + 1).toString(), ...). 3. Unscoped patch("uuid.uuid4") in @[backend_v2/tests/unit/test_references.py#L190-L199]: Resolved in Step 3 by scoping the patch to backend_v2.hooks.references.generate_uuid7. 4. Pre-existing advisory TD_DICT_GET warnings (⚠️ WARN) in 1-hop repository callers (self.driver.get(...) in audit.py, execution.py, knowledge.py, identity.py, workflow.py): These invoke the StorageDriver.get(collection, doc_id) async method (which the AST name matcher flags as .get()) and are preserved untouched per ban_drive_by_schema_mutations.

docs.title: Problem Statement & Architectural Context
docs.text:
Following the integration of the initial Tavily search tool (mcp_tavily_search) in backend_v2/services/mcp/, Quorum's Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool execution loop supports live external retrieval. However, the MCP tool registry is currently coupled to a single provider (mcp_tavily_search), and backend_v2/services/mcp/mcp_tool_loop.py contains hardcoded assumptions targeting Tavily specifically.

To provide specialized encyclopedic research and factual anchoring without commercial API costs or search noise, Quorum requires native Wikipedia MCP Tools: 1. mcp_wikipedia_search: Rapid search querying the Wikipedia Action API returning article titles, snippets, page identifiers, and canonical Wikipedia URLs. 2. mcp_wikipedia_read: Detailed content retrieval querying the Wikimedia REST API page summary endpoint, protected by a strict character truncation shield (mcp_wikipedia_max_chars in backend_v2/settings.py) to prevent context window explosion and preserve prompt caching.

Furthermore, as established in the Tier 8 Feature Audit (feature_audit_mcp_capability_abstraction.md), adding a second tool must not create a hardcoded two-provider branching cascade. Instead, this implementation standardizes Quorum's MCP subsystem into a Dynamic Capability-Driven Architecture: 1. ToolCapability SSOT Enum: Discrete operational capabilities (SEARCH, DOCUMENT_READER, ACTION) declared on domain contracts in backend_v2/models/enums.py. 2. BaseSearchTool Contract: Specialized abstract base class enforcing StandardSearchInputDTO(query: str) input validation and uniform MCPAuditTrace output generation. 3. Eager Capability Indexing in ToolDispatcher: O(1) capability lookup and deterministic primary search tool resolution preserving explicit step author priority (Step.allowed_mcp_tools). 4. Zero-Provider Orchestrator Pipeline: mcp_tool_loop.py consumes ToolCapability.SEARCH with zero provider name checks, enabling arbitrary future retrieval tools (PubMed, ArXiv, DuckDuckGo, SEC EDGAR, Vector DB) to plug in cleanly without modifying orchestrator code.

Because Quorum's presentation layers (TraceEvent -> dag_executor.py -> frozen_context.mcp_tool_audit -> PrintableSourcesAdapter) operate strictly on standard MCPAuditTrace models, registering Wikipedia tools and capability abstraction requires zero modifications to SDUI presentation adapters or Flutter rendering widgets.

Furthermore, Studio V2's MCP-yhdyskäytävät view (client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/mcp_gateways_master_view.dart) and StepBuilderView dynamically read SystemConfigMCPGateways from /api/v2/studio/mcp_gateways. Registering Wikipedia and tool capabilities in backend_v2/seed/seed_data.json instantly surfaces them for configuration on any specialist workflow step in Quorum Studio.

docs.title: Four Dynamic Operational Invariants:
docs.text:
1. Discrete Capability SSOT: Operational capabilities are strictly enumerated in @[backend_v2/models/enums.py] (ToolCapability enum members SEARCH, DOCUMENT_READER, ACTION). Every tool declares an immutable capability property conforming to BaseTool.
  2. Unified Search Input Contract: All search-capable tools inherit from BaseSearchTool in @[backend_v2/models/domain/tools.py] and consume StandardSearchInputDTO(query=str, step_name=str, target_language=str, reasoning=str, claim_text=str|None, llm_client=Any). Concrete search providers never receive unstructured keyword arguments.
  3. O(1) Capability Indexing & Step-Author Precedence Resolution: ToolDispatcher in @[backend_v2/services/mcp/dispatcher.py] indexes tools eagerly upon initialization into _capability_index. When resolving search tools, resolve_primary_search_tool(allowed_tools) traverses allowed_tools in author-defined sequence and returns the first tool matching ToolCapability.SEARCH, deterministically preserving step configuration priority.
  4. Zero-Provider Orchestrator Pipeline: execute_tool_loop() in @[backend_v2/services/mcp/mcp_tool_loop.py] resolves active_search_tool purely via DISPATCHER.resolve_primary_search_tool(allowed_tools). Zero tool identifier literals (TAVILY_TOOL_ID, WIKIPEDIA_SEARCH_TOOL_ID) exist in orchestrator branching logic, eliminating bifurcated execution paths.

docs.title: Cloud-Agnostic Secret & Credential Ingress Topology:
docs.text:
To guarantee enterprise portability across multi-cloud environments (specifically Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and on-premise Kubernetes) without coupling tools to cloud-specific SDKs:

  1. Dual Ingress Separation (Runtime Execution Parameters vs. Infrastructure Secrets):
  2. Runtime Execution Parameters (Dynamic per LLM call / Step configuration): Query strings, reasoning rationale, target language codes, step names, and claim texts vary dynamically on every LLM invocation. These are validated fail-fast through strongly typed, immutable Pydantic V2 DTOs (StandardSearchInputDTO and WikipediaReadInputDTO). Allowed tools are configured dynamically per specialist workflow step in Quorum Studio (Step.allowed_mcp_tools).

  3. Infrastructure Credentials & Secrets (Dynamic per environment / Cloud Secret Provider): API keys (specifically: TAVILY_API_KEY), service URLs, passwords, rate limiters, user-agent identifiers, and timeouts represent infrastructure secrets. These are NEVER passed through LLM prompts, NEVER stored in database seeds, and NEVER hardcoded in Python tool logic.

  4. Settings Model as In-Application Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL):

  5. Settings in @[backend_v2/settings.py] (inheriting from Pydantic V2 BaseSettings) acts as the sovereign abstraction wrapper.
  6. MCP tools never directly read .env files, never call os.environ.get(), and never execute cloud vendor SDK calls.

  7. Tools consume settings strictly via typed property access (get_settings().property).

  8. Container-Native Environment Injection (Zero-Touch Cloud Migration):

  9. Cloud secret engines inject secrets directly into container environment variables at deployment time:
    • Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run / GKE): Secret Manager secrets map to container environment variables via deployment configuration (specifically: gcloud run deploy --set-secrets="TAVILY_API_KEY=tavily-key:latest").
    • Amazon Web Services (ECS / EKS): AWS Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store inject secrets into container task definitions (secrets: [{name: "TAVILY_API_KEY", valueFrom: "..."}]).
    • Microsoft Azure (Container Apps / AKS): Azure Key Vault secrets map into container environment variables.
    • Kubernetes / On-Premise: HashiCorp Vault Agent or Kubernetes Secret Store CSI Driver injects secrets into container pods as standard environment variables.

  10. BaseSettings hydrates these transparently upon application startup. Switching cloud providers modifies infrastructure configuration exclusively, leaving MCP tools, dispatcher logic, and Python services 100% untouched.

  11. Future-Proof Dynamic Secret Rotation Architecture:

  12. If enterprise requirements evolve to demand runtime dynamic secret polling or ephemeral token renewal (specifically: rotating short-lived Vault tokens without container restarts), Pydantic's native PydanticBaseSettingsSource in @[backend_v2/settings.py] provides the single pluggable extension point. Tool implementations (TavilyTool, WikipediaClient) remain completely unaware of the underlying secret retrieval engine.

docs.text:
1. Python Backend Specialist:

To prevent third-party envelope noise (continue, batchcomplete, searchinfo, timestamp, thumbnail) from crashing model_validate, WikipediaClient implements an Ingress Sanitization Gate that strips unmodeled HTTP keys at the client boundary before validating into strict intake DTOs (WikimediaActionApiResponseDTO, WikimediaRestSummaryResponseDTO). Internal Domain Models (WikipediaReadInputDTO, WikipediaSearchResultItem, WikipediaSearchResponseDTO, WikipediaPageSummaryResult) enforce strict domain transit.

  6. LLM Orchestration Architect:
  7. Tool declarations conform strictly to OpenAI Function Calling JSON Schema. Under strict: True, all declared properties are exhaustively included in required (["query", "reasoning"] for search, ["title", "reasoning"] for read).
  8. Dynamic prompt injection preserves Layer 1-3 cache prefix purity by injecting external evidence strictly at the Layer 4 dynamic user message tail.

  13. Anti-Pattern & Zero Backward Compatibility Sweep:

docs.title: Phase D: Falsification & Red-Teaming (Concrete Failure Points)
docs.text:
1. Failure Point 1 (Downstream Flutter Deserialization Crash):
  2. Attack: Adding capability to backend AllowedMCPTool and seed_data.json without updating Flutter AllowedMcpTool causes CheckedFromJsonException (disallowUnrecognizedKeys: true) when Studio client fetches /api/v2/studio/mcp_gateways.
  3. Remediation: Explicitly add @Default('search') String capability to AllowedMcpTool in client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/models/mcp_gateway.dart in Phase 1 cleanups and run flutter_audit_loop.py --build.
  4. Failure Point 2 (Extra Keyword Argument Pydantic ValidationError in execute_tool):
  5. Attack: mcp_tool_loop.py passes llm_client=llm_client to DISPATCHER.execute_tool(). If input DTO enforces extra="forbid" without declaring llm_client, tool execution crashes with ValidationError.
  6. Remediation: Declare llm_client: Any = None on StandardSearchInputDTO with arbitrary_types_allowed=True, allowing search tools to accept standard loop arguments safely without permissive typing.
  7. Failure Point 3 (Abstract Property Instantiation Crash on Test Fakes):
  8. Attack: Introducing abstract capability property on BaseTool causes DummyTestTool in backend_v2/tests/unit/services/mcp/test_dispatcher.py to raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class DummyTestTool with abstract method capability.
  9. Remediation: Explicitly update DummyTestTool in Phase 1 cleanups to declare capability: ToolCapability = ToolCapability.SEARCH.
  10. Failure Point 4 (Wikimedia Disambiguation and Empty Page Handling):
  11. Attack: Querying a disambiguation page or non-existent title returns HTTP 200 with an empty extract or missing page identifier. If unhandled, tool returns empty evidence, polluting downstream LLM context.
  12. Remediation: Validate in WikipediaClient that extract is non-empty and pageid is present; raise AppException(ErrorCodes.RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND) if summary extract is empty or missing.
  13. Failure Point 5 (Wikimedia 3rd-Party Payload Schema Drift & Extra Envelope Keys):
  14. Attack: Wikimedia Action API and REST endpoints return rich response envelopes with evolving metadata keys (batchcomplete, continue, searchinfo, timestamp, thumbnail, dir, revision, tid, displaytitle). In strict mode (extra="forbid" under QGR007), unpruned envelope noise causes fatal Pydantic ValidationError.
  15. Remediation: Implement HTTP Ingress Sanitization Gate in WikipediaClient: filter raw JSON to authoritative field sets before calling model_validate, guaranteeing 100% QGR007 compliance while shielding against external envelope variations.
  16. Failure Point 6 (OpenAI Function Calling Strict Schema Property Mismatch):
  17. Attack: Declaring optional properties (specifically: target_language) in tool declaration schemas with strict: True without including them in required causes LiteLLM and OpenAI to reject the tool declaration with 400 Bad Request.
  18. Remediation: Declare strictly required fields in OpenAI schemas (["query", "reasoning"] for search, ["title", "reasoning"] for read), with orchestrator-level parameters (target_language, step_name) passed deterministically at execution time.
  19. Failure Point 7 (HTTP 301/302 Redirect Dropping & Spaces in REST API Titles):
  20. Attack: Wikimedia REST API endpoint /page/summary/{title} frequently redirects article synonyms (specifically synonym redirection: article alias "AI" resolving to canonical title "Artificial_intelligence"). If httpx.AsyncClient is instantiated with default follow_redirects=False, the client returns HTTP 301/302, erroneously triggering AppException(ErrorCodes.FETCH_FAILED). Additionally, un-normalized titles with raw spaces or unescaped non-ASCII characters crash REST route resolution.
  21. Remediation: Instantiate httpx.AsyncClient with follow_redirects=True, and normalize article titles using urllib.parse.quote(title.strip().replace(" ", "_"), safe=":/@") before dispatching REST requests.
  22. Failure Point 8 (Cloud Secret Manager Coupling & Direct Vendor SDK Lock-In):
  23. Attack: Directly coupling MCP tools or clients to cloud-specific secret SDKs (specifically google.cloud.secretmanager, boto3, or azure-keyvault-secrets) creates severe vendor lock-in, breaks local development without cloud mocks, and crashes offline unit/integration test suites. Alternatively, bypassing Pydantic by reading unvalidated environment variables directly via os.environ introduces runtime type errors and silent failures.
  24. Remediation: Enforce the sovereign Pydantic V2 Settings Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) in @[backend_v2/settings.py]. All tool credentials, endpoints, and secrets hydrate strictly through Settings with mathematical type enforcement and fail-fast validation. Cloud secret managers inject secrets into standard container environment variables at orchestration/deployment time, ensuring zero Python code modifications when migrating between cloud providers.

docs.text:
• Mental and programmatic dry-runs confirm Wikimedia REST API page summary endpoint (https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/{title}) returns JSON with extract, title, and pageid.
  • Action API (https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&list=search&srsearch={query}&format=json) returns query.search array with title, snippet, and pageid.

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Annotated, Any

class StandardSearchInputDTO(BaseModel):
    """Standardized validated input payload for all search capability tools."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(strict=True, extra="forbid", frozen=True, arbitrary_types_allowed=True)

    query: Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, description="Search query string")]
    step_name: Annotated[str, Field(description="Name of the calling step")] = "unknown_step"

class BaseTool(ABC):
    """Abstract interface for all MCP tools."""

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def tool_id(self) -> str:
        """The strictly defined unique identifier for the tool."""
        pass

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def capability(self) -> ToolCapability:
        """The operational capability implemented by this tool."""
        pass

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def declaration(self) -> MCPToolDeclarationDTO:
        """The tool declaration in OpenAI JSON schema format."""
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    async def execute(self, **kwargs: Any) -> MCPAuditTrace:
        """Execute the tool logic and return a standard audit trace."""
        pass


class BaseSearchTool(BaseTool):
    """Abstract base class for all search capability MCP tools."""

    @property
    def capability(self) -> ToolCapability:
        """Return SEARCH capability."""
        return ToolCapability.SEARCH

class TavilyTool(BaseSearchTool):
    """MCP tool for executing Tavily web searches."""

    @property
    def tool_id(self) -> str:
        """Return the canonical tool identifier."""
        return TAVILY_TOOL_ID

    @property
    def declaration(self) -> MCPToolDeclarationDTO:
        """Return the OpenAI JSON Schema declaration for Tavily."""
        return MCPToolDeclarationDTO(
            type="function",
            function=MCPFunctionDefinitionDTO(
                name=TAVILY_TOOL_ID,
                description=(
                    "Perform an explicit search on the live internet using Tavily. "
                    "Use this ONLY when the necessary facts are completely missing from the provided "
                    "context and you require up-to-date or external world knowledge."
                ),
                parameters={
                    "type": "object",
                    "properties": {
                        "query": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": "The exact search query to execute on the internet.",
                        },
                        "reasoning": {
                            "type": "string",
                            "description": (
                                "Why you believe this search is mathematically necessary. Must be 1-2 sentences."
                            ),
                        },
                    },
                    "required": ["query", "reasoning"],
                    "additionalProperties": False,
                },
                strict=True,
            ),
        )

    async def execute(self, **kwargs: Any) -> MCPAuditTrace:
        """Execute the Tavily search using validated StandardSearchInputDTO."""
        input_dto = StandardSearchInputDTO.model_validate(kwargs)
        start_ms = int(time.monotonic() * 1000)
        try:
            result = await tavily_search(input_dto.query)
            response_summary = result.answer

            if (
                input_dto.target_language
                and input_dto.target_language.lower() != "en"
                and response_summary
                and input_dto.llm_client
            ):
                response_summary = await translation_service.translate_text(
                    text=response_summary,
                    target_lang=input_dto.target_language,
                    llm_client=input_dto.llm_client,
                    source_language="English/Original",
                )

            elapsed_ms = int(time.monotonic() * 1000) - start_ms
            trace_id = f"tavily_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"

            return MCPAuditTrace(
                id=trace_id,
                tool_id=self.tool_id,
                step_name=input_dto.step_name,
                claim_text=input_dto.claim_text,
                query=input_dto.query,
                reasoning=input_dto.reasoning,
                response_summary=response_summary,
                source_urls=result.source_urls,
                timestamp=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
                duration_ms=elapsed_ms,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            msg = f"Tavily search failed for query: '{input_dto.query}'"
            logger.error(
                "[TavilyTool] %s: %s",
                ErrorCodes.FETCH_FAILED.name,
                msg,
                extra={"error_code": ErrorCodes.FETCH_FAILED.value, "detail": str(e)},
                exc_info=True,
            )
            if isinstance(e, AppException):
                raise
            raise AppException(
                message=msg,
                status_code=502,
                details={"error_code": ErrorCodes.FETCH_FAILED.value, "detail": str(e)},
            ) from e

docs.text:
Update ToolDispatcher with eager capability index and priority resolution:

class ToolDispatcher:
    """Registry and dispatcher for MCP tools."""

    def __init__(self, tools: list[BaseTool]) -> None:
        self._registry: dict[str, BaseTool] = {tool.tool_id: tool for tool in tools}
        self._capability_index: dict[ToolCapability, list[BaseTool]] = {
            cap: [] for cap in ToolCapability
        }
        for tool in tools:
            self._capability_index[tool.capability].append(tool)

    def get_declarations(self, allowed_tools: list[str]) -> list[MCPToolDeclarationDTO]:
        declarations: list[MCPToolDeclarationDTO] = []
        for tool_id in allowed_tools:
            if tool_id in self._registry:
                declarations.append(self._registry[tool_id].declaration)
        return declarations

    def get_tools_by_capability(
        self, allowed_tools: list[str], capability: ToolCapability
    ) -> list[BaseTool]:
        """Return allowed tools implementing the specified capability preserving allowed_tools order."""
        allowed_set = set(allowed_tools)
        if capability not in self._capability_index:
            return []
        return [
            self._registry[t_id]
            for t_id in allowed_tools
            if t_id in self._registry and self._registry[t_id].capability == capability
        ]

    def resolve_primary_search_tool(self, allowed_tools: list[str]) -> BaseSearchTool | None:
        """Resolve primary search tool preserving explicit step configuration priority.

        The order of tools in allowed_tools defines the precedence hierarchy.
        Returns the first tool matching ToolCapability.SEARCH, or None if no search tool is allowed.
        """
        for tool_id in allowed_tools:
            if tool_id not in self._registry:
                continue
            tool = self._registry[tool_id]
            if tool.capability == ToolCapability.SEARCH and isinstance(tool, BaseSearchTool):
                return tool
        return None

    def has_capability(self, allowed_tools: list[str], capability: ToolCapability) -> bool:
        """Check if any allowed tool implements the given capability."""
        return len(self.get_tools_by_capability(allowed_tools, capability)) > 0

  3. General Secrets & Credential Management Principles:
    • SSOT & Anti-Corruption Layer: Establishes Settings (backend_v2/settings.py) as the sovereign in-application wrapper for all infrastructure secrets (API keys, service endpoints, passwords, tokens). Tools and background services access secrets strictly via get_settings().property.
    • Categorical Hardcoding Ban: Absolute ban on hardcoding API keys or secrets in source code, configuration dictionaries, prompts, seed data, or git commits per rule credential_hardcoding_ban.

In cloud staging and production (Google Cloud Platform, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Kubernetes), secrets are managed in cloud secret engines (Secret Manager, Secrets Manager, Key Vault, HashiCorp Vault) and injected into container environment variables at orchestration/boot time.

- Do NOT use naked dictionaries (dict[str, Any]) for state transit inside Service or Adapter layers. - Do NOT break polymorphic_parsing_mandate / service_layer_hydration_firewall before the Clean Pydantic DAL transition is globally scheduled (Repositories return dict[str, Any] with id filtering; Service/Transformer layers hydrate). - Do NOT use defensive isinstance(..., dict) or .get(...) fallback branching in new service or adapter code. - Do NOT use legacy workflow_id == "*" wildcards in OutputProfile resolution. - Do NOT allow deleting active default output profiles (Workflow.default_profile_id). - Do NOT execute generic limit=1 unindexed queries when fetching MCP Gateways by ID. - Do NOT hardcode localized tool names in Python constants. - Do NOT couple MCP Gateway documents to specific workflows (Gateways are standalone; Workflows reference Gateways N : 1).

docs.title: Problem Statement & Architectural Context
docs.text:
In Quorum 2026, the relationship between Workflows, Output Profiles, and MCP Gateways must adhere strictly to the Tripartite Pipeline Architecture (ki_tripartite_pipeline_architecture.md) and the Zero Permissive Typing Architecture (@[ki_zero_permissive_typing.md]):

  1. Phase 1 (Heavy LLM Execution Phase — Pre-bound MCP Gateways & Reusability):
  2. Täysi riippumattomuus työnkulusta (Standalone System Entity): SystemConfigMCPGateways -määrittelyt (system_config-kokoelmassa) ovat täysin riippumattomia ja itsenäisiä järjestelmätason entiteettejä. Ne eivät sisällä mitään viittauksia työnkulkuihin. Useat eri työnkulut voivat käyttää samaa MCP-yhdyskäytäväkonfiguraatiota (N : 1 uudelleenkäytettävyys).
  3. Yksikäsitteinen sidonta työnkulun puolelta: Kukin Workflow sidotaan yhteen ja vain yhteen MCP-yhdyskäytävään suoralla viittauksella: Workflow.mcp_gateway_id: str | None = Field(default="sys_8172bda70c8641c5") (tai None, jos työnkulku ei käytä ulkoista tiedonhakua).

  4. MCP-työkalut (Tavily, Wikipedia, PubMed jne.) suorittavat reaaliaikaisen ulkoisen tiedonhaun DAG-ajon aikana (vaiheet 7 & 14). Kaikki noudettu todistusaineisto ja MCPAuditTrace-jäljet jäädytetään immutaabelisti suoritustietueeseen ExecutionRecord.frozen_context.

  5. Phase 2 & 3 (Synthesis & SDUI Presentation — Post-Hoc Output Profiles):

  6. Output Profiles ovat puhtaita "Dumb Painter" -esitysmalleja (target_block_order, matrix_visible_columns, tone_instruction).
  7. Jokainen OutputProfile kuuluu täsmälleen yhteen työnkulkuun (1 : N relaatio OutputProfile.workflow_id -kentän kautta).
  8. Työnkulku ilmoittaa oletusprofiilinsa Workflow.default_profile_id -kentässä.

  9. Tripartite Decoupling: Koska Vaiheen 1 suoritusdata on täysin eriytetty Vaiheiden 2 & 3 esityslogiikasta, käyttäjä voi jälkikäteen (post-hoc) renderöidä minkä tahansa aiemman ajon minkä tahansa samaan työnkulkuun kuuluvan OutputProfile-profiilin läpi ilman, että raskasta LLM-graafia tarvitsee suorittaa uudestaan!

  10. Pydantic Transition State (Repository Hydration Firewall):

  11. Noudattaen polymorphic_parsing_mandate ja service_layer_hydration_firewall -sääntöjä, ISystemRepository palauttaa dict[str, Any] täsmällisellä id-suodatuksella ([Filter("id", "==", id)]).
  12. Service-kerros (SystemConfigService) ja esitysmuuntaja (BlueprintTransformer) toimivat Hydration Firewallina, validoiden raakadatan Pydantic V2 -malliksi (SystemConfigMCPGateways.model_validate(raw, strict=False)).
  13. Kaikki sisäiset domain-operaatiot ja adapterikontekstit toimivat 100 % tiukoilla Pydantic V2 -malleilla (ConfigDict(strict=True, extra="forbid")) puhtaalla pistenotaatiolla.

docs.text: 1. Kohdealue & Skoopit (Target Scope) 2. 🚫 KIELLETTY PURKKA (Eradicated Duct-Tape) 3. 🎯 TEE NÄIN (Approved Best Practice) 4. ✂️ KARSITTU YLISUUNNITTELU (Pruned Over-Engineering) 5. 🔒 VERIFIOINTI & FAIL-FAST (Proof Anchor) Workflow.mcp_gateway_id (models/v2_core.py#L1096-L1224) Epämääräinen limit=1 -haku kannasta ilman relaatiota; singleton-oletus. Eksplisiittinen mcp_gateway_id: str \| None = Field(default="sys_8172bda70c8641c5", pattern=r"^sys_[a-fA-F0-9]{16,32}$", description="The system_config ID of the MCP gateways configuration attached to this workflow.") sitoen työnkulun täsmälleen yhteen itsenäiseen MCP-yhdyskäytävään (useat työnkulut voivat jakaa saman yhdyskäytävän). Suora N:1 skalaarirelaatio; ei monimutkaisia väli-mapping-tauluja. Pydantic regex-validointi ja yksikkötestit (test_workflow_model.py). docs.title: Objective
docs.text:
Evolve Quorum's model configuration architecture into Option A: Sovereign Model Stack Architecture (One Document = One Coherent 4-Tier Model Stack) with deterministic workflow-level binding (Workflow.model_registry_id), eradicate vendor name leakage from workflow step authoring, upgrade the Model Registry UI to strictly comply with Desktop Pro Tool UX standards (@[ki_desktop_pro_tool_studio_ux.md]), and modernize run_e2e_variance_test.py to source all model telemetry dynamically from the database without hardcoding and support automated --compare-registries differential benchmark runs.

This plan delivers five core pillars: 1. Option A Sovereign Model Stack Architecture: Flattens SystemConfigModelRegistry.tier_definitions from a nested multi-provider map (dict[provider, dict[tier, profile]]) to a direct 4-tier mapping: tier_definitions: dict[CognitiveTier, ModelProfile]. Each registry document represents a single named, self-contained model stack (specifically: "Google Gemini Sovereign Stack", "OpenAI O-Series Stack", or a custom hybrid stack). Each tier profile encapsulates its own provider, model_name, and execution parameters. 2. Strict Vendor-Neutral Step Authoring: Eradicates physical model strings (specifically [gemini/gemini-3.8-flash]) and hardcoded vendor chips from StepBuilderView. Workflow steps author pure abstract cognitive tiers (FAST, BALANCED, DEEP, REASONING), decoupling workflow blueprints from underlying physical model infrastructure. 3. Deterministic Workflow-to-Registry Binding: Establishes Workflow.model_registry_id across backend domain models, studio DTOs, Flutter Freezed models, and WorkflowGeneralTab, enabling workflows to deterministically target dedicated model stacks. 4. Desktop Pro Tool UX for Model Registry CRUD & Clone: Upgrades ModelRegistryView and StudioDashboardView to satisfy ki_desktop_pro_tool_studio_ux.md: - Enforces Bounded Canvas Containment (maxWidth: 1200px) centered on screen. - Dual-Shield PopScope navigation guards with serialization-based dirty checking and localized discard confirmation modals. - In-view deep clone trigger (Icons.copy) in the top AppBar. - Clean 4-card tier layout (FAST, BALANCED, DEEP, REASONING) without nested expansion tiles. - Scalable list browsing in Studio Dashboard Tab 6 with real-time search, count indicator, and density-optimized tiles. 5. Dynamic Database Sourcing & Automated Multi-Model Comparison in E2E Variance Harness: - In scripts/run_e2e_variance_test.py, all model telemetry and execution parameters are dynamically resolved from the active database (data/db_v2.json or seed_data.json) eliminating hardcoded assumptions. - All printed telemetry displays human-readable stack names (specifically: "Google Gemini Sovereign Stack"), default providers, and actual physical model names (specifically: gemini/gemini-3.8-flash, openai/gpt-5.1) rather than opaque ID strings. - Adds --model-registry CLI option enabling ad-hoc override of the model stack for a single execution run. - Adds automated --compare-registries CLI option (supporting zero-argument automatic pairing of workflow registry against alternative DB stack, or explicit two-argument pairing) that executes sequential runs across two distinct model stacks with identical inputs and automatically synthesizes a differential report via scripts/diff_executions.py.

docs.title: User Review Required
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] Option A Schema Flattening: SystemConfigModelRegistry simplifies from dict[LLMProvider, dict[CognitiveTier, ModelProfile]] to dict[CognitiveTier, ModelProfile]. Each registry document represents one complete 4-tier stack. A workflow binds to exactly one registry via Workflow.model_registry_id. When a step requests CognitiveTier.FAST, the orchestrator queries registry.tier_definitions[CognitiveTier.FAST], resolving the exact physical model and provider configured for that stack.

[!IMPORTANT] Workflow General Tab Selection: In WorkflowGeneralTab (Quorum Studio), the workflow author selects which Model Registry stack is used by that specific workflow from a dedicated dropdown (Workflow.model_registry_id). Individual workflow steps only choose abstract cognitive tiers (FAST, BALANCED, DEEP, REASONING) with zero vendor leakage.

[!IMPORTANT] Automated Multi-Model Comparison (--compare-registries): In scripts/run_e2e_variance_test.py, --compare-registries supports both automatic and explicit modes: - Automatic Mode (--compare-registries without arguments): Automatically discovers the active workflow's bound registry (specifically: "Google Gemini Sovereign Stack") and pairs it against the alternative registry available in the database (specifically: "OpenAI O-Series Stack"). - Explicit Mode (--compare-registries <REG1> <REG2>): Allows specifying any two registries by ID, slug, or title (specifically: --compare-registries sys_e26807f3bfa3454d sys_6f8b1c4a2e0d49f1). - Execution & Differential Synthesis: Executes Run 1 with Registry A, Run 2 with Registry B using identical inputs, and automatically spawns scripts/diff_executions.py to compare scoring variance, Cohen's Kappa, quote provenance, latency, and FinOps costs between the two models, saving the diff report to data/files/executions/.

docs.title: Falsification & Red-Teaming Analysis (Attack Surface & Mitigations)
docs.text:
1. Failure Vector 1: Seed Vault & In-Memory Pre-Flight Deserialization Shock:
  2. Attack: Modifying SystemConfigModelRegistry.tier_definitions in backend_v2/models/v2_core.py before updating seed_data.json or running database re-seed will immediately break all backend tests and application boots with Pydantic ValidationError.
  3. Mitigation: Enforce strict Two-Phase Atomic Ingress per 03_seed_vault.md: migrate backend_v2/seed/seed_data.json in the exact same atomic transaction as v2_core.py, run scripts/audit_database_atoms.py --strict, and execute uv run python backend_v2/seed/run_seed.py local --dry-run to verify 100% in-memory validation before persisting.
  4. Failure Vector 2: Tab 6 Dashboard Runtime Method Absence (NoSuchMethodError):
  5. Attack: In client_app_v2/lib/features/studio/views/studio_dashboard_view.dart#L571, the code runs config.tierDefinitions.values.fold(...) assuming tierDefinitions is a nested map where .values returns maps with .length. With Option A flat Map<String, LlmModelConfig>, .values returns LlmModelConfig objects. Calling .length on LlmModelConfig throws runtime NoSuchMethodError crashing Tab 6.
  6. Mitigation: Update studio_dashboard_view.dart in Phase 1 before running flutter_audit_loop.py, replacing the fold loop with direct config.tierDefinitions.length.
  7. Failure Vector 3: Multi-Registry Fallback Cascade vs Single Sovereign Pipeline Invariant:
  8. Attack: If Workflow.model_registry_id targets a non-existent or deleted registry ID, the orchestrator might fall back to parameterless get_model_registry(), violating <rule_block id="zero_backward_compatibility_planning_ban"> and silently executing workflows on unintended models.
  9. Mitigation: ISystemRepository.get_model_registry(registry_id: str | None = None) MUST raise ResourceNotFoundError(resource_type="system_config", resource_id=registry_id) Fail-Fast when an explicit ID is not found, preceded by structured logger.error per rfc7807_dual_reporting_mandate. Zero silent fallback to other registries.
  10. Failure Vector 4: Freezed Model Dirty Checking False Positives:
  11. Attack: In ModelRegistryView, using reference inequality (_editableConfig != widget.initialConfig) triggers false-positive dirty confirmation dialogs on unmodified views because @Freezed entities do not implement deep value equality.
  12. Mitigation: Implement Serialization-Based Dirty Checking per desktop_pro_tool_studio_ux_mandate: jsonEncode(_editableConfig.toJson()) != _initialConfigJson, guaranteeing deterministic dirty state with zero false positives.
  13. Failure Vector 5: E2E Runner Argument Count Ambiguity:
  14. Attack: In scripts/run_e2e_variance_test.py, --compare-registries configured with nargs="*" could receive 1 or 3+ arguments, causing indexing errors or ambiguous pairings.
  15. Mitigation: Explicitly validate in main: if len(args.compare_registries) not in (0, 2): parser.error("--compare-registries requires either 0 arguments (auto-paired against DB alternative) or exactly 2 arguments (<REG1> <REG2>).").

docs.title: Implementation Plan: Autonomous Headless CLI Phase Orchestrator (scripts/auto_phase_runner.py)
1. Executive Summary & Objective
docs.text:
Create an autonomous headless phase orchestrator [NEW] @[scripts/auto_phase_runner.py] that automates the unattended, sequential execution of multi-phase implementation trackers (docs/epic/EPIC_XXX_tracker.md, docs/epic/*_decomposition_tracker.md, and docs/implementationplans/TRACKER_*.md).

The orchestrator: 1. Discovers and parses phase definitions from the tracker document (supporting both multi-phase Epic topology and single-phase Standalone Plan topology). 2. Iterates through pending ([ ]) phases, launching an isolated agy CLI subagent process for each phase with Gemini 4 Argon (High) and continuous full-auto permission authorization. 3. Streams live execution logs and thought telemetry directly to the console. 4. Executes the mandatory Universal Quality Gate (backend_audit_loop.py) upon phase completion, failing fast on any regression. 5. Performs atomic git checkpoint commits per completed phase, updating tracker checkmarks in-place. 6. Seamlessly hands off to scripts/auto_hardening_runner.py upon completion of all phases for Epoch 2 post-implementation hardening (supporting optional --hardening-agent to dispatch full AI-driven /tier2-hardening-backend subagents per target file).

      2. Detect topology:
         - **Multi-Phase Epic Topology**: Scan for `### Phase\s+(\d+)[:\-]?\s*([^\n]*)\n([\s\S]*?)(?=(?:### Phase\s+\d+|### Integration Checkpoint|### Post-Implementation|\Z))`.
           Extract plan path via `(?m)^(?:\s*-\s*)?\*\*Plan:\*\*\s*@?\[?([^\],\n`]+)\]?`.
           Extract execution line via `-\s*\[([ xX])\]\s*(?:\([a-f0-9]+\)\s*)?\*\*\[(?:OK|NOK)\]\s*Execution(?:\s*\([^\)]+\))?:\*\*\s*(?:`?(/tier2-execute[^\n`]+)`?|[^\n]*)`.
           Clean slash command by stripping enclosing backticks and any trailing parenthesized commit hashes `(?:\s*\(`?[a-f0-9]+`?\))?`.
           If no execution command is explicitly found, default deterministically to `f'/tier2-execute --full-auto @<{plan_path}> @<{tracker_path}>'`.
           Determine completion strictly from `[x]` checkbox on execution line or all sub-steps checked.
         - **Single-Phase Standalone Plan Topology**: Scan for `## Step Execution Status\n([\s\S]*?)(?=(?:### Post-Implementation|\Z))`.
           Extract single plan path via `(?m)^(?:\s*-\s*)?\*\*Plan:\*\*\s*@?\[?([^\],\n`]+)\]?` and execution command, cleaning backticks and trailing parenthesized hashes.
           If no execution command is found, default deterministically to `f'/tier2-execute --full-auto @<{plan_path}> @<{tracker_path}>'`.
      3. Verify each referenced `plan_path` physically exists on disk (checking `plan_path.exists()` or `(root / plan_path).exists()`). If missing, fail-fast with `FileNotFoundError`.
      4. Implement `filter_phases(phases: list[PhaseItemDTO], from_phase: int | None = None, only_phase: int | None = None) -> list[PhaseItemDTO]`:
         - If `only_phase is not None`: return `[p for p in phases if p.phase_num == only_phase]` regardless of prior `is_completed` state.
         - Otherwise, filter out phases where `p.is_completed is True`, and if `from_phase is not None`, filter out phases where `p.phase_num < from_phase`.
      5. Return an ordered list of `PhaseItemDTO` objects.
    </action>
  </step>

  <step id="3" name="Implement agy Subagent Spawner with Streaming &amp; Tree Killing">
    <constraint invariant="async_background_execution_mandate">Subprocess execution must support cross-platform Windows 11 tree termination (taskkill /F /T /PID) on timeouts or cancellations to prevent orphaned zombie LLM CLI processes.</constraint>
    <action>In `[NEW] @[scripts/auto_phase_runner.py]`, implement `resolve_agy_binary() -> Path` and `execute_phase_subagent(phase: PhaseItemDTO, args: AutoPhaseRunnerArgsDTO, repo_root: Path) -> SubagentExecutionResultDTO`:
      1. Binary resolution:
         - Check `shutil.which("agy")`.
         - If None, check Windows paths `Path.home() / "AppData/Local/agy/bin/agy.exe"`, `Path.home() / "AppData/Roaming/npm/agy.cmd"`, `C:/Program Files/agy/bin/agy.exe`.
         - If unfound, raise `FileNotFoundError("Antigravity CLI (agy) not found in PATH or standard installation directories.")`.
      2. Command formulation:
         - Inspect `phase.command`. If `"PERMISSION GRANTED"` is not already present, construct:
           `f'{phase.command}. PERMISSION GRANTED for continuous full-auto execution across all steps. Proceed autonomously through all steps without intermediate confirmations.'`
         - If already present, use `phase.command` directly.
         - Build arguments list:
           If `sys.platform == "win32"` and str(agy_bin).lower().endswith((".cmd", ".bat")):
             `cmd = ["cmd.exe", "/c", str(agy_bin), "--model", args.model, "--dangerously-skip-permissions", "-i", prompt]`
           Else:
             `cmd = [str(agy_bin), "--model", args.model, "--dangerously-skip-permissions", "-i", prompt]`
      3. Subprocess execution with watchdog tree killing:
         - Launch with `subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", cwd=repo_root)`.
         - Set `is_timeout_triggered = False`. Record `start_time = time.monotonic()`.
         - Define watchdog callback:
           `def _on_timeout(): nonlocal is_timeout_triggered; is_timeout_triggered = True; _tree_kill(proc.pid)`
         - Start `threading.Timer(args.timeout, _on_timeout)` to enforce deterministic timeout without blocking pipe reads.
         - Stream stdout directly to terminal (`sys.stdout.write(line); sys.stdout.flush()`), catching `UnicodeEncodeError` on Windows consoles and falling back to `sys.stdout.buffer.write(line.encode("utf-8", errors="replace"))`, while accumulating lines into in-memory buffer. Wrap read in `try...except (OSError, ValueError): break`.
         - In `finally:` block, cancel the watchdog timer.
         - If `is_timeout_triggered` is True:
           Wait for child tree termination, compute `elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time`, and return `SubagentExecutionResultDTO(exit_code=-1, output="".join(collected_output), duration_seconds=elapsed, is_timeout=True)`.
         - Wait for process termination via `proc.wait()`. Compute `elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time`.
         - Return `SubagentExecutionResultDTO(exit_code=proc.returncode, output="".join(collected_output), duration_seconds=elapsed, is_timeout=False)`.
    </action>
  </step>

  <step id="4" name="Implement Quality Gate Verification &amp; Atomic Git Checkpointing">
    <constraint invariant="atomic_checkpoint_mandate">Never commit if quality gates fail. Always stage explicit target files and tracker using Conventional Commits syntax.</constraint>
    <action>In `[NEW] @[scripts/auto_phase_runner.py]`, implement `run_phase_quality_gate(phase: PhaseItemDTO, repo_root: Path) -> QualityGateResultDTO` and `commit_phase_checkpoint(phase: PhaseItemDTO, tracker_path: Path, repo_root: Path) -> str | None`:
      1. Quality Gate:
         - Inspect working tree via `git status --porcelain` to identify dirty files in `scripts/`.
         - Dynamically resolve quality gate targets: `targets = ["backend_v2/"] + [f for f in dirty_files if f.startswith("scripts/") and f.endswith(".py")]`.
         - Run `uv run python scripts/backend_audit_loop.py <resolved_targets> --test`.
         - Return `QualityGateResultDTO(success=(proc.returncode == 0), output=stdout, exit_code=proc.returncode)`.
         - If exit code non-zero, log error banner and halt pipeline immediately (circuit breaker).
      2. Git Checkpoint:
         - Inspect dirty files using `git status --porcelain`.
         - If working tree is clean: log "Working tree clean, no commit required" and return None.
         - Parse modified and untracked files from porcelain output, strictly filtering out scratch/ephemeral directories (`.gemini/`, `.system_generated/`, `scratch/`, `tmp/`).
         - If only tracker is modified: stage tracker via `git add <tracker_path>` and commit `git commit -m "docs(tracker): mark phase {phase.phase_num} complete in {tracker_path.name}"`.
         - If domain files are dirty: sanitize title via `title_cleaned = re.sub(r"^Phase\s+\d+[:\-]?\s*", "", phase.title, flags=re.IGNORECASE).strip()`, stage verified domain files and tracker via `git add <filtered_files> <tracker_path>`, and commit `git commit -m "feat(phase{phase.phase_num}): complete {title_cleaned}"`.
         - Return short commit hash extracted via `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
    </action>
  </step>

  <step id="5" name="Implement In-Place Tracker Marking &amp; Post-Implementation Hardening Handoff">
    <constraint invariant="deterministic_hardening_state">Synchronize tracker checkboxes in-place. Execute auto_hardening_runner.py upon pipeline completion.</constraint>
    <action>In `[NEW] @[scripts/auto_phase_runner.py]`, implement `mark_phase_completed_in_tracker(tracker_path: Path, phase_num: int, commit_hash: str | None = None) -> None` and `run_post_hardening_gate(tracker_path: Path, args: AutoPhaseRunnerArgsDTO, repo_root: Path) -> int`:
      1. Tracker update:
         - Read tracker file content.
         - Slice target section: For target Phase N (in Multi-Phase Epic topology bounded by `### Phase {phase_num}` up to the next `### Phase` or section marker) or the execution section (in Single-Phase Standalone Plan topology `## Step Execution Status` up to `### Post-Implementation`), perform in-place replacement strictly within that slice.
         - Within the target slice, replace `- [ ] **[NOK] Execution:** <command>` with TRK002-compliant formatted line preserving standard bold colon:
           `- [x] **[OK] Execution:** <command> (`{commit_hash}`)` if `commit_hash` is present, or `- [x] **[OK] Execution:** <command>` otherwise.
         - Replace indented `- [ ] Step` with `- [x] Step` within the target section slice.
         - Reassemble and save updated tracker with UTF-8 encoding.
      2. Post-Implementation Hardening handoff:
         - If `not args.skip_hardening`:
           - Construct command: `cmd = ["uv", "run", "python", "scripts/auto_hardening_runner.py", "--tracker", str(tracker_path), "--gate", "backend"]`.
           - If `args.hardening_agent`:
             - Determine hardening model: `h_model = args.hardening_model or args.model`.
             - Format agent command template: `agent_template = f'agy --model {h_model} --dangerously-skip-permissions -i "/tier2-hardening-backend {{target}}"'`.
             - Append `["--agent-cmd", agent_template]` to `cmd`.
           - Execute subprocess with output streaming. Pass through exit code and log summary banner.
    </action>
  </step>

  <step id="6" name="CLI Argument Parser, Main Entrypoint &amp; test_scripts_cli_help.py Registration">
    <constraint invariant="windows_powershell_mandate">CLI must support standard flags (--tracker, --model, --from-phase, --only-phase, --skip-commit, --skip-hardening, --hardening-agent, --hardening-model, --dry-run) and output clean help text.</constraint>
    <action>In `[NEW] @[scripts/auto_phase_runner.py]`, implement `run_phase_pipeline(args: AutoPhaseRunnerArgsDTO, repo_root: Path | None = None) -> AutoPhaseRunSummaryDTO`, CLI argument parsing, and `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int`; and update `@[backend_v2/tests/unit/scripts/test_scripts_cli_help.py#L61-L67]`:
      1. In `scripts/auto_phase_runner.py`:
         - Implement `run_phase_pipeline(args: AutoPhaseRunnerArgsDTO, repo_root: Path | None = None) -> AutoPhaseRunSummaryDTO`:
           - Parse phases via `parse_tracker_phases(args.tracker, repo_root=root)` and filter via `filter_phases(all_phases, from_phase=args.from_phase, only_phase=args.only_phase)`.
           - If `args.dry_run` is True: print planned phases and commands without spawning subprocesses or mutating git/tracker, and return `AutoPhaseRunSummaryDTO`.
           - For each pending phase: execute `execute_phase_subagent`, verify `exit_code == 0` and `not is_timeout` (halting immediately on failure), run `run_phase_quality_gate` (halting immediately on failure), mark phase complete via `mark_phase_completed_in_tracker(args.tracker, phase.phase_num)`, and if `not args.skip_commit`, commit via `commit_phase_checkpoint(phase, args.tracker, root)`.
           - If all phases succeed and `not args.skip_hardening`, invoke `run_post_hardening_gate(args.tracker, args, root)`.
         - Configure `argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Autonomous Headless CLI Phase Orchestrator (Multi-Phase Pipeline Runner).")`.
         - Add all flags defined in `AutoPhaseRunnerArgsDTO` (including `--hardening-agent` and `--hardening-model`).
         - Wire `main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int` with proper exit codes (0 for full success, 1 for failure, 2 for CLI arg error).
      2. In `@[backend_v2/tests/unit/scripts/test_scripts_cli_help.py#L61-L67]`:
         - Insert `"auto_phase_runner.py"` into sorted `ALL_SCRIPTS` list.
         - Update assertion count from 35 to 36 in `test_script_count_is_exhaustive`.
    </action>
  </step>

  <step id="7" name="Comprehensive Unit &amp; Mock Verification Suite in test_auto_phase_runner.py">
    <constraint invariant="anti_happy_path_compliance">Test both success and negative failure paths: invalid tracker, missing plan, agy crash, timeout tree kill, quality gate rejection.</constraint>
    <action>In `[NEW] @[backend_v2/tests/unit/scripts/test_auto_phase_runner.py]`, implement the comprehensive unit test suite:
      1. `test_parse_tracker_phases_epic_topology`: Verify phase extraction against `docs/epic/matrix_domain_parser_decomposition_tracker.md`.
      2. `test_parse_tracker_phases_standalone_topology`: Verify phase extraction against `docs/implementationplans/TRACKER_auto_phase_runner.md`.
      3. `test_parse_tracker_with_commit_hash`: Verify regex parses `- [x] (hash) **[OK] Execution:` correctly.
      4. `test_parse_tracker_missing_file_raises`: Verify `FileNotFoundError` on non-existent tracker.
      5. `test_parse_tracker_missing_plan_file_raises`: Verify `FileNotFoundError` when referenced plan does not exist.
      6. `test_resolve_agy_binary_found_and_missing`: Mock `shutil.which` and path lookups to verify both success and clean error reporting.
      7. `test_dry_run_mode_prints_phases_without_subprocess`: Verify `--dry-run` discovers phases and exits 0 without calling `agy`.
      8. `test_phase_failure_triggers_circuit_breaker`: Mock failed `agy` return code (1) and assert pipeline stops immediately without committing.
      9. `test_quality_gate_failure_stops_pipeline`: Mock successful `agy` but failed quality gate, verifying git commit is aborted.
      10. `test_mark_phase_completed_in_tracker_in_place`: Verify regex in-place replacement of checkboxes and commit hash insertion.
      11. `test_execute_subagent_timeout_tree_kill`: Mock watchdog timer firing and verifying `taskkill /F /T /PID` is dispatched.
      12. `test_commit_phase_checkpoint_clean_working_tree`: Verify clean working tree skips commit without error.
      13. `test_full_pipeline_success_mocked`: Mock successful 2-phase execution with git commit and hardening handoff.
      14. `test_filter_phases_only_phase`: Verify `--only-phase` filters down execution to the designated single phase.
      15. `test_filter_phases_from_phase`: Verify `--from-phase` skips all phases with index lower than the threshold.
      16. `test_run_post_hardening_gate_with_hardening_agent`: Verify `--hardening-agent` appends `--agent-cmd` with `/tier2-hardening-backend {target}` template to `auto_hardening_runner.py`.
      17. `test_execute_subagent_cmd_wrapper_on_windows`: Verify `.cmd` / `.bat` binary wrapping via `cmd.exe /c` on Windows platforms.

docs.title: IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: Modernize Tier 3 God Code Decomposition Workflow
Executive Summary
docs.text:
This implementation plan hardens and modernizes the Tier 3 God Code Decomposition Planner workflow (@[.agents/workflows/tier3-god-code-decomposition.md]) based on the exhaustive findings of the Tier 8 Red Team Security & Architecture Audit (red_team_audit_tier3_god_code_decomposition.md) and Tier 0 System 2 Research Deconstruction.

The refactoring eliminates seven critical vulnerabilities: 1. Elimination of Text-Based Method Boundary Guessing: Replaces naive grep_search with mandatory AST boundary extraction via @[scripts/_ast_boundary_utils.py], preventing silent code cuts and syntax truncation. 2. Resolution of Inter-Slice Circular Dependency Deadlocks: Replaces generic type-splitting with strict Bottom-Up Topological Leaf-First Order, guaranteeing extracted modules never import unextracted logic from the God File. 3. Protection of Shared In-Memory State and Concurrency Primitives: Introduces mandatory shared concurrency state containers (@dataclass(frozen=True)) for asyncio.Lock (_update_lock), asyncio.Semaphore, and circuit breakers, eliminating Split-Brain state corruption during execution. 4. Context Amnesia Prevention and Double-Migration Elimination: Mandates in-flight module hardening prior to consumer migration and enforces strict batching of 1-hop consumer updates (maximum 5 files per batch) coupled with atomic commits and /tier5-session-handover intervals. 5. Modern Python 3.14 & Quorum Modernity Sweep: Expands the legacy 7-item checklist into an authoritative 10-item Tech Debt Inventory covering PEP 695 type aliases, PEP 750 template strings, PEP 742 TypeIs, Tuple Hell eradication, and strict Pydantic V2 configurations. 6. Enforcement of Foundational Quality Gates & Facade Lockdown: Integrates mandatory AST mutation testing (@[scripts/audit_mutation_coverage.py] with a 100% mutant kill rate on mathematical cores), SDUI/PDF semantic parity testing (@[backend_v2/tests/integration/test_sdui_semantic_parity.py]), post-deletion AST Guardrail QGR017 lockdown, and canonical directory synchronization. 7. Test Suite Preservation & Modular Test Decomposition Invariant: Guarantees that existing monolithic tests continue passing without modification during extraction via the Strangler Fig proxy, and mandates that consumer migration explicitly rewires and decomposes monolithic test suites into modular test files mirroring the newly extracted domain modules.
